review_full: Having selected and booked (do book) this restaurant based on TA recommendations, my expectations were pretty high. But from the minute we walked into this small vinoteca we were looked after in a completely open and down the earth way. The waiter, who was probably also part time owner and/or chef, took the time to apologize for his bad english before describing the entire menu in fast and fluent english... he claims he can only speak English about his menus :) He also helped us to order just the right amount of food, halving some of the portions where necessary so that we could explore more dishes.  It's not really Tapas, but you can approach it like that, which is what we did. The menu is short though, so perhaps not a great place for fussy eaters. As all the other reviews say, the potatoes (not ordered, almost an amuse bouche), the artichokes, and the leeks are all amazing. Simply cooked through a sous vide style (from what we could understand), but well prepared and served with amazing seasoning, from complex and rich sauces, smokey paprika, to a little crunch of sea salt. The beef tartare was fantastic, and served with a very spicy Peruvian hot sauce which we could add to taste. The veal cheek cannelloni was also rich yet delicate with a kind of fluffy béchamel on top. They also helped us match a couple of nice local whites wines. All the staff were pros, with fresh dishes and cutlery between dishes, fresh glasses for each wine, and all able to answer questions about the food. But my biggest surprise was the bill at the end of the night. Only 55 euros total for two people including five *fantastic* dishes (between us) and a couple of glasses of palatable wine each. Wow! If I lived near by I'd be making a standing reservation for Friday nights!

review_full: I was lucky to go the Vinoteca Moratin the day that I arrived because there would be a table for one available the next day for lunch. As the other reviews indicate, one must make reservations, the sooner the better. Fortunately for me, my hostal was also on Moratin Street. I was able to secure a lunch reservation for the earliest seating: 2:30 p.m.  To dine at Vinoteca is a culinary experience. I used “culinary” rather than “gustatory” because the meal is as much an exploration of the process as of the enjoyment. The owner/chef is Marcos. He wore Nikes and a beard and mustache peppered with gray. Marco is proud of his restaurant and eager to share with his customers each intimate detail of preparation and presentation. A diner should be ready to accept his enthusiasm and join in the culinary discussion. Otherwise, one should seek a restaurant where the chef is mostly behind the scenes.  Marcos explained each dish starting with a complimentary amuse-guele of potatoes and paprika, quite simple quite tasty, along with a flute of Cygnus champagne. Then an artichoke dish cooked long and lowly slowly, served with sea salt and olive oil. Excellent. Next came a soft octopus entrée with a glass of La Fou tinto (I did not note the year.) Very good combination. There was another course which I failed to note, but I recall enjoying everything immensely, including the fragrance of the main course, hot fresh mushrooms over pureed potatoes. I wafted the fragrance into my nose. The mushroom dish tasted great. Unfortunately, half way through this mushroom dish I began to feel a little queasy. I doubt that the dish was anything but perfect because it tasted delicious. I probably was still experiencing jet lag.  With dessert and a glass (perhaps two, I don’t recall) of the tinto, my bill was only 34 euro including tip. Thirty-four euro for a meal in one of the top ten (TripAdvisor) restaurants in Madrid. What a bargain ! (Of course, I had to leave something extra, hoping that this offer would not offend the waiter who did his job extremely well.) The outside and inside of the Vinoteca Moratin are unprepossessing. There is no napery, except napkins. The tables and seats are bare wood, minimalist. The emphasis here is on the food and service. Make your reservations soon.

review_full: I had read the other reviews on Tripadvisor and was looking for something different for an evening meal in Madrid with my wife, brother and sister-in-law. I was not disappointed! I was staying nearby at the Hotel Opera (see my seperate review) but having been to Madrid several times previously and experienced both good and bad, cheap and overpriced, meals in the Spanish capital wanted to look for something special for my wife's and my brother's first visit and in particular something memorable. The restaurant is located just of the Plaza Isobel II in a side street (Calle Union) opposite the south side of the Teatro Real. It looks nothing special from the outside (especially during the day when it mostly has its shutters down but does have a large hanging plant growing outside which makes it easy to spot, I went one night to have a look (as it doesn't open until 9 p.m.) and found it closed so had to wander around another day, saw the shutters half opened and rang on the doorbell. The restuarant is run by two sisters Isabel and Pilar. The very charming Isabel answered, explained that a booking was required as the restaurant only had seats for 20 people. Booked there and then and nervously we turned up as a group of 4 slightly early (8.50 p.m.). Isabel asked us to wait outside as the tables weren't quite ready but let us in a few minutes later. Wow! I can only describe the restaurant as being a bit like visiting someone's house (say your favourite aunty) who has laid out a few tables for a private dinner party with a few select guests. Isabel then swung into action providing an English language menu and between her pretty good English and my broken Spanish we started to have a conversation just as if we were at our favourite Aunty's house making small talk and discussing our travels etc etc. Brilliant fun and so welcoming. The menu is not huge but lots of interesting things (with specialities from the Rioja region of Spain from whence the sisters come) which are prepared in the kitchen by Isabel's sister Pilar. Little nibbles were provided to keep us going and we chose the house red which Isobel proudly showed bore the name of her (and her sister's) restuarant on the label. As is only right for two sisters from Rioja it was an exellent Rioja wine! Isabel was happy to let us order starters (and later puddings) to share which was just as well as the mains were very filling indeed and absolutely delicious! Pilar the chef came out afterwards and spoke to all the customers about their meals and like her sister was very chatty and welcoming. In summary, not the cheapest but very good value for money, food was superbly cooked and delicious but without doubt, for me, the absolute best thing about this restaurant is the feeling of exclusivity, being part of such a small group, the undivided individual attention shown by both Isabel and Pilar to their customers and the amazing homely surroundings. As I said previously, it was like being invited to a family dinner with the best food and the best wine and, (this is for you Isabel and Pilar), the best company.

title_review: Great ambience and service, good but unspectacular food and wine
review_preview: I suppose the headline sums it up for me. I was travelling along on business, and went there based on the TripAdvisor reviews. The decor, seating/table arrangements and atmosphere were perfect for what I wanted: a nice place to have dinner and a glass of...
review_full: I suppose the headline sums it up for me. I was travelling along on business, and went there based on the TripAdvisor reviews. The decor, seating/table arrangements and atmosphere were perfect for what I wanted: a nice place to have dinner and a glass of wine while reading my book. The service was great: prompt, knowledgeable and very warm and friendly from all three people I dealt with. The food was good, but I did feel a tad disappointed having expected perhaps too much after reading the reviews. While tasty it was fairly basic (I had a half-portion of polpo on mashed potatoes followed by the veal cannelloni and a Creme brûlée-style desert). All the food was tasty but lacked a spark of elegance or inspiration. I'd say a good 3 or low 4 out of five - not average in a bad way, just solidly decent but not more. I was offered two tasters of wine by the glass, which was a nice touch. One was a fairly boring mainstream number from a mainstream producer, the other a more interesting Tempranillo from Rivera del Duero. Very good for the price (€4) but nothing special. I suspect the ones not offered by the glass but only whole bottles will be the better ones, which is fine and to be expected. All of in all, perfectly good and I'd go back, but with expectations adjusted. It certainly was not my best meal in Madrid but it fit the bill for what I wanted. While my earlier lunch at Luzi Bombon (goat's leg and truffled potato puree) was very good indeed and better for the food alone, I would not have wanted to go there for dinner on my own with a book. For that Moratin Vinoteca was a very good choice.

review_preview: During our 4 day city break to Madrid we used Tripadvisor to find some good places to go and eat and we were so pleased we went to Restaurante Morgana. A small but perfectly sweet little restaurant in the Chueca district (right near our accommodation),...
review_full: During our 4 day city break to Madrid we used Tripadvisor to find some good places to go and eat and we were so pleased we went to Restaurante Morgana.  A small but perfectly sweet little restaurant in the Chueca district (right near our accommodation), we were met by two extremely welcoming and polite waiters/owners. Our Spanish is limited but we were introduced to the menu in superb English and given the best introduction to the Galician-fusion menu/wine list.  The croquetas were excellent (so crisp, excellent flavour and filling) and the tomatoes/avocado were a delight. So unique and very much haute cuisine - but reasonably priced.  Main courses - moules in a sort of spicy Thai or laksa-inspured broth for myself (I don't eat red meat) so it was lovely to see options of fish/vegetarian on a Spanish menu. My partner had the special of the rump steak, with padron peppers and potato chips.  To finish we had a breaded pudding with sweet sauce and apple flavours..  All in all it was excellent: service, food, price and setting. We would definitely recommend for foodies or walk-ins alike.

title_review: Galician Fusion: It's In, Not Con
review_preview: When it comes to food, I'm wary of the word "fusion" because for me it also spells "not authentic." So to hedge my bet, I ordered two fusion dishes (Galician-style taco and pulpo with kimchi mashed potato) and one traditional dish (tuna empanada). Ironically, of...
review_full: When it comes to food, I'm wary of the word "fusion" because for me it also spells "not authentic." So to hedge my bet, I ordered two fusion dishes (Galician-style taco and pulpo with kimchi mashed potato) and one traditional dish (tuna empanada). Ironically, of the three dishes, the two fusion dishes turned out to be more successful - although good, I think the empanada would have been better if it was slightly warmed up. I liked the tender meat and mild cheese in the taco. I'm not sure if it was roughly grounded corn chips, but they added another layer of flavor and extra crunchiness to the taco. I was worried that the kimchi might overpower the octopus dish, but it did not - rather, it added a slight kick to the potato, which in turn complemented the mild octopus flavor. Definitely worth trying for those looking for something new but do not want to wander too far off. Overall, I can say that this restaurant's attempt to meld different traditions resulted in INfusion, not CONfusion of flavors. P. S. This restaurant welcomes half orders so take advantage of it. Also, be patient because there might be some pauses between the dishes.

review_preview: We came across Kueco after a really long stroll across Madrid. It was late (10.30 PM). We were cold and hungry and we wanted to have good food. I’m normally not too generous with rating food. I’m a pretty good chef myself and if I...
review_full: We came across Kueco after a really long stroll across Madrid. It was late (10.30 PM). We were cold and hungry and we wanted to have good food. I’m normally not too generous with rating food. I’m a pretty good chef myself and if I cannot replicate a dish, to me that means I came across a special restaurant. Literally, I didn't had such good food in a long time. The taste was so delicately, fresh and pure. We had really good wine with it. They recommend to take one dish of each course, which we didn't because it was late, but I would definitely do so when I have the change to come back. I would take my friends and family to this restaurant, but even if I'm in Madrid for business, I would take my colleagues here to have. I'm traveling to many places very often for work and this is defenitely a restaurant to impress your business relationships.

review_full: We had booked a table through The Fork and it did not say that you would only have the table for 2 hours, and 2 hours is way too little time to be seated, look at the menu, have a snack, a starter, a main, a dessert, coffee. The experience was really stressfull and the waiters seemed really stressed as well. The Fork did not say anything about that the tasting menu is only served for dinner (and their webpage does not either). Furthermore there was a cold breeze through the restaurant coming form the ventilation above the door, we were moved to another table which was better. We had some snacks which tasted really good, and then some starters that were tasty but tasted somewhat the same, the mains were mixed: the duck was really good, the iberain pork ok and the beef cheeks too spicy. The water had a slight taste of chemical, so we are not sure it was bottled water (but filtered). The waiters were friendly but really stressed and we constantly felt rushed to finish and the food came really fast and we did not have time for coffee and dessert. If the purpose is to give guests a gourmet experience 2 hours is simply not enough, so they should write on the webpage that its more for people who want a quick dinner (and only 2 courses is possible in 2 hours if you should not feel rushed). All in all the stress ruined the experience which is a shame cause they have some good interesting dishes on the menu.

As a Singaporean, the chilli crab croquette didn't really taste like what we have back home (their version is creamier and less spicy), so I wouldn't recommend it. Had the black noodles - with seared squid and crispy onions - this could do with less salt, but is a fusion dish done well - gravy was good and not too spicy. Finished off with a yoghurt dessert with matcha meringue(?) and figs - great end to a meal and I actually don't really eat figs but I polished the bowl. Not exactly cheap but had an enjoyable meal. There was a male staff who could speak English very well and had good recommendations.

review_full: Angelita was one of the restaurants recommended by my hotel, and they were right in their positive assessment. I ate in the street level wine bar, not the basement American bar. I was most lucky to get a seat as the restaurant is generally booked full with reservations. I was asked if I would sit at the bar and said yes. I ended up at a small raised table above the main seating area and a few feet from the actual bar. It allowed good views of food, activity, and satisfied people. The menu is a simple one page list with the expectation that orders are for two to split. My delightful server said that there were entrees that could be ordered as half and I took his advice on selections. I had four small plates, dessert, and two glasses of wine. All was good. My first course was a single fresh oyster. Then a very tasty organic ratatouille with added texture, egg and rosemary mayonnaise. Different and delicious. Oxtail cannelloni with wild mushrooms brought another pleasing flavor. Then came the amazing charcoal Iberian pork with sweet potato and "burned" eggplant. The pork was tender and had a edge of crispness. The server said it is first grilled and then oven cooked. Dessert was porcini mushroom mousse with fruits and thyme crumble. It was a different taste and I expect that I will reserve judgment until I try it again. There was no rush, I was asked about my enjoyment level, and was treated with true concern. All in all, a real treat.

We had tuna tartare which was also excellent and a good sirloin steak. The only negative was that I asked for the steak to be cooked "Chicago-style", charred outside and rare inside. The staff assured me that they were fully familiar with this cooking method. However, when it arrived, the steak was neither charred nor rare...(it was nicely grilled and medium rare). Not anywhere near enough to send back, but this is not a cheap dining option in Madrid and so I offer this as a constructive suggestion to the kitchen.

title_review: Surely one of the finest Steakhouses in Madrid.
review_preview: It was my great good fortune to have dinner here about 3 days ago.I was looking for a Restaurant fairly close to my hotel that I could walk to and not need to worry about how much wine I consumed. Grin.It's easily located...
review_full: It was my great good fortune to have dinner here about 3 days ago. I was looking for a Restaurant fairly close to my hotel that I could walk to and not need to worry about how much wine I consumed. Grin. It's easily located with Google Maps, well reviewed and bookings are simply made using the Google function. You can also just dial its number manually the old fashioned way. Unless you propose turning up at 11:15pm and hope to get a walk in table, I suggest you do make a booking as it is very busy. If you show up at a more normal 9pm without booking I suspect you will be disappointed. The person who answered the phone when I booked spoke perfect English. As the name of the Restaurant suggests, they are justifiably proud of their Argentine steak and accordingly this is what I ordered and what I recommend.  They do however have local steaks, excellent fish, pork and chicken dishes, so I think that any discerning diner will find something to his or her taste here. I hesitate to say that this is the best steak I have ever tasted. I can't recall however, a particular occasion when I have had a markedly better one. I can say that it was here that I found the finest tasting tomato I have ever had, as part of a delicious side salad.  As it was just quartered and in a simple salad, you might argue that little praise can be given to the Chef. Rather I would point out his/her product sourcing and attention to detail. I live in the UK and travel widely in Europe. I have experienced no tomatoes available in the UK which remotely compare in flavour.  Nor have I found any in France or any other place.  A little thing I know, but the Devil is in the detail, No ? The wine selection is as you'd expect and has choices for all wallets. I chose a dessert of Flambeed Crepes, similar to my all time favourite of Crepe Suzette, (but not with Oranges), this was also delicious and memorable. I tasted the dishes my companion chose and paid close attention to the dishes chosen by my neighbouring diners.  Everything I tasted was of a very high standard and all of the other dishes that I viewed I would be happy to order on another occasion. The decor and ambiance of the place is lovely and also memorable. The staff, I found, were friendly and efficient. To summarise, the whole evenings dining experience was a delight.

review_full: We discovered this gem through a review in The Guardian and, based on the advice given, booked well in advance of our trip to Madrid. From the first email, the communication was great - prompt, friendly and welcoming. On arrival, the same qualities were evident and we were quickly seated and drinks ordered. There was something both informal and highly organised about the staff, and we were soon relaxed and thinking what to order. Marcos makes the menu redundant ! He took us through each dish with such detailed and passionate descriptions that it was hard not to ask for one of everything. When we suggested three starters (a family of three, one being a teenager), Marcos said he thought that might be too much food and suggested half portions of two dishes, and he was right to do so. We had leeks that were so sweet, sicculent and tender, and artichokes that dissolved in the mouth. The 'full' dish was octopus in a smoky paprika sauce. All three were delicious. The choice of mains was as difficult to make, but we plumped for chicken, cannelone and steak tartare. All perfectly cooked (or devised in the case of the steak) and flavoured. The wine list was very good, but this was an easier choice for us since we are currently impressed with Ribera del Duero wines, and the one we chose was a step up from our usual bottle. Time passed ever so quickly. The service was very attentive (our glasses remained empty for seconds only!) and the ambience was warm and lively but not intrusive, especially for such a small venue. The bill ? A very reasonable sum for this level of quality in a capital city on a Friday evening.

review_full: The concept behind Pizzateca is that Pizza meets library (biblioteca in Spanish). review_full: This is a story I would rather not tell...it really bothers me when a place with such good credentials fails in a not-so-understanding way... I was one day ago with a very good friend in Madrid, hanging around in a totally not occupied time slot around the Museums (Prado/Thyssen-Bornemisza) quarter.l We searched for a nice Iberic wine place. And there's one, some friends mentioned to us. I'm going to be totally blunt: I suppose it's a nice place, it was wholeheartedly recommended to us. From the start I will admit that we had no prior reservation, and boy, did we learned a hard way lesson! We have very gently approached the staff around 8 PM and we have very decently accepted that all tables were booked and that the restaurant was not available for the evenings to come. We did understand, and we headed for a less in-the-bundle restaurant in the area. Heading back at around 11 PM in the evening, we passed along this place again. We really praised it, wanting a good evening to remember in this great city, a true European capital, Madrid!  We took a look inside and there were at least two tables where I and one remaining friend could be sitted in. With full fledged smiles we entered the place. It had more than an hour of opening hours, judging from its TripAdvisor advertising open hours. And this is where the spell was broken. Our evening in this ever-party city was ruined with a smile :). No, I'm not smiling! At a very early 11 PM, we were, frankly said, kicked out! Why? There's the funny part! Although there were admittedly free tables, at 11 PM, we were kicked out because, I quote: you haven't booked a table, and it would be unfair for the others to be accepted. We said: we did understand this earlier, at around 8 PM, when we walked away with no comments, as we had no reservations in place. But at 11 PM, with available places, why treat tourist so arrogantly? Why send us in such a discarding manner away? We even mentioned that there were no other opportunities in the near future and that we saw no reason in not being allowed to enjoy a relaxing night in the great Madrid, a city we so longed to visit. Our begging was so majestically ignored! Basically we were "invited" to walk away, regardless of our availability to order a full menu dinner (which was an excuse to be sent away, although the kitchen was long time closed!). I won't mention names, the employees have no doing in this humiliation. We were, according to "restaurant policy", invited to leave! We did mention complaining on TripAdvisor, and we received the most condescending smile you can image. Many things can be said about how we felt! But I will not have this review be driven by anger, as we have not chosen Madrid for this! We came here for the spirit of this great city! And we were grateful in seeing this all over the places we were so warmly invited in. Except this one. I've been in many places. Most of them not reviewed here.  But I have recently decided to share my experiences, so I will leave this here, for you to consider.

review_preview: My wife and I had a wonderfully memorable dinner at the Morotín Vinoteca Bistrot.  I had made a reservation by email from home and I was glad that we did.  It is a small restaurant and was filled by the time we finished dinner (the...
review_full: My wife and I had a wonderfully memorable dinner at the Morotín Vinoteca Bistrot. I had made a reservation by email from home and I was glad that we did. It is a small restaurant and was filled by the time we finished dinner (the restaurant was empty when we arrived for dinner at 8 PM — late for us, apparently early for Madrileños). One of the reviews I had read said that the chef discusses the menu with each patron, which he did with us, and he also agreed to help me select a bottle of wine - based, of course, on the entrees we selected. He chose a wine from a bodega in Madrid, Bodega Marañones, which was fabulous. One great thing about the restaurant is that almost every wine in the wine list was priced from 20 to 30 Euros. The chef said that he created the wine list with price in mind, to showcase the extremely high quality of moderately priced wines. Judging by the wine that he suggested for us, he has succeeded! He took the time to speak with us for several minutes. He is clearly proud of his work and his restaurant and, as we found out, has every reason to be. It was a great choice and, without a doubt, our best dining experience during our ten-day trip to Madrid and Seville.  The menu had a good selection of appetizers, entrees, and desserts, and we had a tough time choosing among them. We started with a tomato salad, which consisted of a huge platter of simply delicious cut and peeled tomatoes, dressed only with olive oil and a little salt. This was a recommendation from the chef, who told us that the tomatoes were in season and probably would not be anywhere near as good in a week. They were fresh, juicy, and flavorful. We had a poached cod — incredibly good, not the salt cod that can be on offer in many Madrid restaurants. And two desserts, an apple tart and violet ice cream. The dishes were on the simpler side — our preference — but be assured that the chef was inventive and original without being flamboyant. The atmosphere was dark and subdued, a perfect place for a non-fussy romantic dinner.

For the main course I had the chicken which a previous reviewer described as a ‘hoysin sauce’ and I am inclined to agree! My wife had the Sea bass and rice which she loved! Hopefully the restaurant will look at their ‘timings’ as this made us feel rushed. Prices were reasonable and overall, the staff were very good. My wife would certainly rate this as a 5 stars but I would only give 3 so we’ve compromised and given a 4.

We had several conversations with the owner throughout the evening about his philosophy of food procurement and preparation. It was a delightful evening and I would highly recommend it for the food, comfortable ambiance, and welcoming service. You'll need a reservation, many people were turned away who didn't have one.

title_review: We were talking about the steaks the day after!
review_preview: Found La Cabana in Madrid actually April 2010 (but dates for this review only go back as far as June 2010).  Anyway, we ordered some fries and salad to go with it - don't bother.. the steak was SOoooooooo delicious you ruined the flavor by...
review_full: Found La Cabana in Madrid actually April 2010 (but dates for this review only go back as far as June 2010). Anyway, we ordered some fries and salad to go with it - don't bother.. the steak was SOoooooooo delicious you ruined the flavor by contaminating it with fries and salads. What can I say about this steak. I'm not a steak person, come from the UK, prefer chicken as steaks in the UK r like cardboard. However, this steak, madre mia! It melted in your mouth, was so tasty. It was however expensive: two steaks, fries and some salad to share, couple of beers cost 60 euros. Next day on the train to Toledo for the easter processions both of us had the same thought: that steak last night was so tasty wasn't it? A random thought by two people on a train about the steaks!!! Needless to say we went there the next night and paid another 60 Euros, this time we didn't touch the fries. Viva Argentina!

title_review: Great find on the back streets of Madrid
review_preview: We stayed at the Urban Hotel in Madrid for 4 nights & we were desperate to find a really good restaurant that wasn't the usual run of the mill tapas which you seem to find in Santa Ana just round the corner.  Our receptionist recommended...
review_full: We stayed at the Urban Hotel in Madrid for 4 nights & we were desperate to find a really good restaurant that wasn't the usual run of the mill tapas which you seem to find in Santa Ana just round the corner. Our receptionist recommended this Argentinian restaurant & we were not disappointed. On arrival we were asked if we had a reservation by which we replied no (it was a rainy Sunday night & the place only had one other couple currently dining), the waitress then just disappeared before reappearing & guiding us to a table without uttering another word (or smile). The food here was just great - the steak excellent, nice fries & fresh salad/bread. The waitresses did have a snotty nosed approach to dealing with you as if you were an inconvenience to them having to serve you. That was a shame as otherwise the place couldn't really be faulted. Good food, good wine, nice ambience just horrible sour-faced waitressing. Would recommend if you want a change from the Spanish cuisine but don't expect any smiles (even when you pay!).

review_full: A very pleasant experience. First, there are only 8-10 tables so you absolutely must have a reservation. From the outside it doesn't really distinguish itself from many other bistros or small restaurants. BUT , this was highly recommended by the concierge staff at The Westin Palace Hotel and they were absolutely correct.  Inside, it is clearly a bistro in its appearance. Not fancy, just very pleasant. HOWEVER, the highlights are 1)the waitstaff who were some of the most pleasant people we have met and 2) the food. First, one can trust everything that the waitstaff tells you about each item as well as the wine. We had an outstanding tomato salad and a marinated salmon for appetizers. We both chose the same main course, the cannelloni with veal cheeks. The wine from Ribera Del Duerro region was Kairn (?spelling). Everything was OUTSTANDING. It was a welcome change from some of the more formal and more expensive restaurants. The price of the meal was extremely reasonable---about 60% less than some of the fancy restaurants.  Lastly, how good is it? It's the restaurant that concierge staff from The Westin goes to for their Christmas lunch every year. You can't help but love the experience.

review_full: I tend to be very strict on the 5* classification. This place is my 2° five-star rating. Food is simply amazing, very tasty and service and attention is top-notch. We had Oxtail croquetas, fried ceviche (2 entrees), a rice dish, duck, slow cook lamb and slow cook chicken (4 main dishes). Everything amazing. I'll for sure be back to try more dishes. 4 persons with wine and no deserts and we paid 120€. The only thing that I have to pinpoint as downside is the fact that the place is very small. But food compensates. If they had a bigger place with large windows and street views this place could be one of the top 10 restaurants in Madrid.

review_preview: Our party of 4 visiting Madrid was one hour late for our booking, due to delays driving into Madrid from France. We were so happy that they managed to accommodate us even though it was a busy Friday night. Not knowing what to expect, and...
review_full: Our party of 4 visiting Madrid was one hour late for our booking, due to delays driving into Madrid from France. We were so happy that they managed to accommodate us even though it was a busy Friday night. Not knowing what to expect, and the fit out of the small restaurant was casual, we were totally blown away by the creative and high quality gourmet food, at such reasonable prices. We enjoyed the crispy wontons, grilled octopus, the thai curry style fish and black noodles, mellow rice. The mellow rice has amazing rich flavour ( a truffle fan), but I think the saltiness can be dialled down a little. We are very impressed with the chef's talent. The service staff were friendly and helpful. We were surprised to find out that it has only been opened for about 6 months, already it is very popular as they had to turn away people at the door. A highlight of our stay in Madrid.

review_full: Tiny little shop not far from paseo del prado that clearly prides itself in the art of pizza. The pizza is outstanding with lots of eclectic choices. There is a thick by-the-slice format and a thin crust medium size pizza. The pizza maestro is always at work doing something new towards the back. The front cashier spoke excellent English and helped us choose. Not much seating, but who cares. Stand or get it to go. Really excellent food, service and overall "art of pizza" vibe.

I suggest taking your pizza to go and walk 1 minute to the lovely square and sit on a bench and people watch. It was too cold when we were there so we ate standing up. I never eat standing up, but it was worth it for the mushroom pizza.

review_preview: We just had our New Year's lunch in Pizzateca and both kids and adults had a great culinary experience.  We had to wait a bit for the restaurant to open at 1:30pm, but it was very worth it.  The pizzas are prepared by a friendly...
review_full: We just had our New Year's lunch in Pizzateca and both kids and adults had a great culinary experience. We had to wait a bit for the restaurant to open at 1:30pm, but it was very worth it. The pizzas are prepared by a friendly owner with a variety of fresh local ingredients. We tasted egg-plant, truffle, Spanish jamon and goat cheese with balsamic reduction containing pizzas. Absolutely spectac! Only thing missing was a glass or two of California Chardonnay or New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc to round off the taste sensation. The restaurant is very tiny, with only a couple chairs, so taking pizza to go is also a great option. Prices extremely reasonable at 6eur for 2 generous pieces and a drink.  I second another reviewer's comment: the best pizza in Spain after living here for 2 years. If you do not need comfort and only care about quality, this is a must.

review_full: We were hesitant to go since we thought, "we're not in Madrid to eat pizzas!" but since we saw the rave reviews here, decided to give it a go. Are we glad we did! The pizzas all had a touch of innovation. We especially loved the teriyaki chicken and the mushroom pizzas. And the crust! The crust is special and divine! When we commented to the owner that his pizzas are among the best we ever tasted, he was totally modest and said his home town of Napoli has better ones (ok our next culinary destination). The place is really small with only a few seats, but people tend to eat quickly and move on to free up space. Sit or take away, you have to try his pizzas when in Madrid!

And the desert of mango ice-cream on a chocolate brownie in a pool of white chocolate was so outstanding we ordered another one. Prices are moderate, and the atmosphere is friendly.

review_preview: This small restaurant is situated a short distance away from the down-town area but it is absolutely worth visiting.I arrived pretty soon after evening opening – so I was the only customer for a while. This gave me the opportunity to talk with the...
review_full: This small restaurant is situated a short distance away from the down-town area but it is absolutely worth visiting. I arrived pretty soon after evening opening – so I was the only customer for a while. This gave me the opportunity to talk with the owner and hear about his experiences, ideas and goals how to develop his restaurant. Now he is very committed to local producers, not only with food raw materiels but also with vines. The Market offers excellent courses. After their kitchens´ greeting I had ”Green Beans Salad, Mango, Bacon and Cava Foam”, which was not only tasty but also visually great. As my main I had “Sierra de Guadarrama” Grilled Veal Loin, Muhammara and Padron Peppers”, which also was delicious. Also the vines selected for my courses suited very well together with them.  As a final ”Mascarpone Panna Cotta with Roasted Quince Cream and Yogurt Ice Cream” topped my excellent dinner.  All in all I was very satisfied with my dinner, courses were well prepared, service was casual and friendly and last but not least, the prices were very acceptable.

review_preview: We went to The Market Madrid in May 2014 following some good reviews on tripadvisor. We were not dissappointed, on the contrary, we were completely blown away. The service was excellent and the food was even better. The menu was very inventive and we took...
review_full: We went to The Market Madrid in May 2014 following some good reviews on tripadvisor. We were not dissappointed, on the contrary, we were completely blown away. The service was excellent and the food was even better. The menu was very inventive and we took an adventure and ordered the most bizarre options that the restaurant offered - everything was spectacular: The starters were excellent and really opened our appetite. The main courses were perfectly cooked and seasoned and offered the perfect portion to leave room for dessert. Finally, the desserts were fabulous even though on the menu they seemed kind of odd, one of them had sweet basil pesto and a sweet cherry tomatoe. We were offered a Spanish red wine "Iuvene" that we afterwards searched in several stores - unfortunately we didn't find it, but it was great and highlighted the different tastes of the food. Going to "The Market Madrid" was the highlight of our vacation and we were sad that we didn't stay longer in Madrid to be able to return.

review_preview: After touring Spain for 3 weeks, we returned to Madrid before heading home and stopped at The Market Madrid for our last lunch. It was outstanding! Owners, Jaime and Norma remembered us from our first visit and welcomed us warmly. Jaime even left the restaurant...
review_full: After touring Spain for 3 weeks, we returned to Madrid before heading home and stopped at The Market Madrid for our last lunch. It was outstanding! Owners, Jaime and Norma remembered us from our first visit and welcomed us warmly. Jaime even left the restaurant for 5 minutes to help us coax a parking ticket from a nearby meter. The menu changes frequently based on market availability so we had a new set of tempting choices which Jaime explained to ensure we understood each item. The gals opted for two medio portions each while the men chose medio starters and full entrées. All choices were excellent. We decided this time to also have dessert. I cannot say enough about how excellent this restaurant is, so good that we were trying to convince Jaime and Norma to return to Seattle where they lived a few years ago. The four of us live in British Columbia and would gladly find an excuse to visit Seattle to go to this restaurant. Madrid, you don’t know how lucky you are!

review_full: I absolutely loved this place! It's small (so be sure to reserve) and not exactly in the center of town, but definitely worth the cab ride to get there. Our friends reserved there for a birthday dinner and I'm so glad they did!  The menu is short so very easy to navigate. Our waiter spoke flawless English and explained every dish. I had the brandade de bacalao, which won me over immediately: fluffy creamed cod piped into thick rounds of bread. One of my friends got the blood-sausage ravioli, which was an explosion of flavor. Then I had the pork cheeks with a mole sauce: the tenderest meat and fabulous spices. The prices are very affordable for a restaurant of this quality. The restaurant also offers half portions for appetizers as well as main courses. The wine list is very good and also affordable. For dessert, since it was my friend's birthday, the chef came out with something special: a basil poundcake with candied cherry tomatoes. Sounds weird, but it totally works! This restaurant is on my list for my next trip back to beautiful Madrid!

I was not a guest on that date however, the owner was very politely serving me and explained the restaurant/menus. The restaurant was smaller than I thought but I had confidence that our client would be amazed. The dining was amazing. This was due to not only food but also hospitality. review_full: If you are ever in Madrid and you are in deep need for a good steak, I recommend you visit the argentinean steakhouse "La Cabaña Argentina". It's located in the old part of the city, near Sol, and it's one of the best steakhouses in town, in my humble opinion. This restaurant is specifically located in "Ventura de la Vega" street, which is known as "the street of taste" (La Calle del Sabor, http://www.callesabor.es). The exact address is "Ventura de la Vega, 10" in Madrid.  It's owned and managed by argentineans, and I can confirm that the meat is prepared in the argentinean style of the "Parrilla". Most of the different steak options are very good and i prefer the "Bife Lomo Bajo". One of the most interest things is that you can even taste some of the argentinean specialties like "Molleja" (Sweetbread), which is quite difficult to find in this kind of restaurants in Europe. The area is surrounded by other restaurants and pubs so you can go out after finishing dinner, if you are able to walk after eating a regular argentinean steak of more than 400 grams.  If you are planning to go to this restaurant on a weekend night, i recommend you make a reservation because it would be full otherwise. However, the place is spacious enough so even if it's full, you can have a nice and quite evening.

Staff are inviting, not sure where the other reviewers got the idea that the waiting staff are rude, but I guess everyone can have an off day. The service style is quite traditional, different servers to tak the order, deliver and clear away. They tend to leave you alone and aren't over-friendly which might not be good for everyone. Personally I like a relaxed style of service.  My tips ... A starter is enough for two, so consider sharing.  Order a bottle of reserve Rioja to accompany your steak.  Sides aren't automatically provided. Choose some starch and vegetables/salad but again this is big enough to be shared.  Don't order chicken. Steak or nothing! review_full: Need to preface this with the following: I'm half Argentine -- the half that loves cows that are lovingly grass fed in the Pampas and get to soak up the sun. La Cabaña is the second best Argentine steakhouse I've been in my LIFE. If you're curious, my number one favorite is in Buenos Aires (La Brigada, get the entraña al punto). But I digress. La Cabaña's entraña al punto is the kind of meal I'll remember fondly years from now--just as I've salivated over memories of my dinner at La Brigada. Located walking distance from Plaza de Santa Ana, we got there at 9PM, which we thought was late enough. Dinner doesn't usually start until 11PM in Madrid, so bring the TUMS. By 10PM the restaurant was completely full (on a weekday), so reservations are recommended. It's so rare to get a steak so perfectly executed that it requires no salt, sauce, bread or fixings. Argentine steak is typically served at a perfect pink medium (al punto) with a crispy crust and mega moist middle. Our steaks were served on a communal platter that arrived sizzling and could have easily served 3-4. I said could have. We had no problems devouring it--every bite coupled with a head shake and close of the eyes to soak in the experience.

title_review: Decent steak, not exceptional.  Overrated and pricy.
review_preview: I wanted to love this place based on other reviews and the recommendation of my hotel. But the steak was only decent, not exceptional. The service was friendly and fast. It was overpriced.TIP #1: they really undercook the steak here. I normally order my...
review_full: I wanted to love this place based on other reviews and the recommendation of my hotel. But the steak was only decent, not exceptional. The service was friendly and fast. It was overpriced. TIP #1: they really undercook the steak here. I normally order my steaks medium rare and I can handle red centers and blood. I ordered it medium here and it came out quite rare. If you like your steak actually medium (warm pink center) then I would order it well done here. TIP #2: The steaks come with NO sides whatsoever. You'll need to order any sides. Most of the sides I saw being brought out to other tables looked large, so two sides would probably suffice for two people. I had the smaller ribeye (350 g; Bifo Lomo or something like that) and it was decent tasting but nothing exceptional. Since it was from Argentina I expected it to be exceptional, but it really wasn't. Most of the 28-day-dry-aged ribeyes that I get in North America taste far better than this steak. The ribeye at this restaurant was only decent and needed a lot more marbling to be a good ribeye. The mixed salad (Mixta) was actually quite decent. I have a lot of trouble finding regular salads in Europe, i.e., those with lettuce and tomatoes. Normally European salads seem to contain pickled asparagus and other weird ingredients. Fine if you want to try something new, but what if you just want lettuce and tomato? The mixed salad here had lots of very fresh and tasty lettuce and tomatoes. The bread that came with it was decent. The service was quick and friendly. I might try this restaurant again. But it wasn't cheap and the steak was only decent, so I'd try other places before returning. Again, it was decent, but I left disappointed whereas I went in excited.

review_preview: I just had lunch at Angelita after reading the TripAdvisor reviews of several places in Madrid I might have missed during this and previous trips here.  I was at the door at 1:30 when they opened; by 2:00 they were full, the staff all now...
review_full: I just had lunch at Angelita after reading the TripAdvisor reviews of several places in Madrid I might have missed during this and previous trips here. I was at the door at 1:30 when they opened; by 2:00 they were full, the staff all now at work at full speed. I sat at the bar, since I was alone, though they offered me a table if I wanted one. I chose small portions of the day's three specials: a single oyster on the half shell, perfect, fresh, great texture, like it had just been pulled from the sea; tomatoes from the family farm with little green pepper and anchovy adornments, which were the best tomatoes I think I've ever eaten, though one of the young owner brothers lamented that his parents thought these not the best of their crop this year; a rice dish with cod cheek chunks (which I brought most of home with me for breakfast tomorrow, since I wanted to save room for dessert); and a roasted vegetable dish that I can only describe by telling you to order it for sure. A new bartender named Luis arrived after my oyster and all things from there were magic: hyper-vigilant, Luis is entertaining to watch and has great personality and taste in wine pairings. I just let him pick, and am grateful that he did. Dessert was an unusual porcini mushroom mousse with fresh fruits and a thyme crumble, just wonderful with the cream sherry Luis said was meant to be had with it. So don't overthink this one--just go.

Unfortunately we didn’t know you ought make a table reservation in advance, otherwise you won’t be served. Alternatively they told us we can go downstairs for a drink and some snacks if we fancy. I can only say it was fab!. Every single detail was cool, pleasant, cozy, warm... and the goods were outrageous. The staff members were great. Very kind, warm, polite... they really make you feel comfortable. Decoration was great. Wide sofas, poor lit room gives you intimacy, surrounded with spirits bottles everywhere and some vintage pictures. We ordered a fantastic red wine, I must recommend; ‘Yotuel’, although it’s name might evoke a joke, it was magnificent. 1). Tomato salad: nothing simpler than fresh and tasty tomato served on a plate. Some kosher salt, anchovies and jalapeños were aside just in case you wanted to mix them up. But plane tomato with some salt on top was pretty good. 2). Cheese sample board: around 9 different cheeses were presented to give them a try. Varieties such us: aged Gouda, Roquefort, Brie, Canarian cheese from Alegranza... although each has something unique, I would say Alegranza was one step over the rest. It was smoked and covered with truffle. Absolutely astonishing!. 3). Tacos: we tried pulled pork and langoustine taco. The first was warm, juicy, soft... very good one. The latter was cooler and you could feel avocado, coriander and the crunchiness of the langoustine. Wonderful! 4). Truffle mushrooms?: to be honest, I don’t recall the name of it. But I can still feel the fantastic mix of flavors in my mouth.  Basically consisted in a mushroom filled with a truffle sauce, and decorated with a fried quail egg. My goodness, what a wonderful bite!!! 5). Desserts: At this point we didn’t want eat any more, but somehow we decided to finish such a great dinner with some sweet. Chocolate coulant and black Forrest: the coulant is bizarre. The way the hot and cold merge in your mouth is a dream come true. The cake was performed differently. We could say it was their version of it. A sort of chocolate  Fudge with cream or truffle on top, and some berries ice cream aside. If you combine them you get a very interesting bite. Without any doubt, I must go. Do not hesitate for a second. I can’t wait to come again. Fabulous experience.

review_full: The ingredients used here are very fresh, and, while not top-level, this is likely some of the best pizza to be had in Madrid! The owner is wonderful to interact with; he clearly takes great pride in his restaurant. We ate here twice, and had some of the more 'standard' options -- margherita, la diabola, and la rucolona. Unfortunately, there isn't a lot of turnover, so the pizza selection is often limited to what's been made that day, and it isn't right out of the oven. That being said, the owner lovingly rejuvenates the slices on demand, and they do taste quite good. It's worth noting that the square slices that are made to be sold by the slice are significantly better than the mini round pies you can get to go, as the latter tend to be thinner crust and a little soggy near the center of the pie.

title_review: Good Food - but a thoughtless Chef spoiled our enjoyment!
review_preview: This was another restaurant we had reconnoitred near the excellent "Catalonia Las Cortes" hotel, and duly booked with a courteous and pleasant young lady. It looks well from the street, and the internal decor, while conservative, is pleasant. The heavy emphasis of the Menu is...
review_full: This was another restaurant we had reconnoitred near the excellent "Catalonia Las Cortes" hotel, and duly booked with a courteous and pleasant young lady. It looks well from the street, and the internal decor, while conservative, is pleasant. The heavy emphasis of the Menu is BEEF, and perhaps not surprisingly, there are very few "Whites" on the Winelist, but no "big deal" about that, we felt, as we contentedly settled-in to relax and enjoy ourselves, with only a handful of people around us. Our Server, as we look back on it, may have been a Trainee - unlike the very competent woman I had met when booking, she had no "Name Badge", and was not particularly self-assured. We ordered 1 Starter (to share) and a Main each, as well as some White (Rueda) & Red (Rioja) wine. So far, so good. We had barely sampled our Starter when our Server arrived at the table, somewhat agitated, asking "can I bring the meat?", to which our natural response (in words + hand signals), was "not yet - give us 10 minutes!". To our total amazement, she almost immediately landed-back bearing our Mains! We were practically speechless, and not surprisingly, our Server seemed suitably embarrassed. Between us all, we pushed aside the Starter so that our Mains could be pressed on us. To be fair, my Beef Milanese & my "Better Half's" Beef Tenderloin were both very good. But sadly, the quality of the food could not compensate for the grossly insensitive treatment we had just experienced - basically the Chef had forced the Mains on us to suit himself, not us! We eat out to savour and enjoy, not to have food stuffed down our throats at the whim of one thoughtless individual!! Anyway, having consumed the "force-fed" Mains, we requested "La Cuenta", declining an offer of Liqueurs. Our Server at this stage was apologetic, and we tried to convey to her that we did not blame her for what had happened - we asked could we speak to a "Jefe", but were told this was not possible. While not saying this to her, our feeling was that whoever was in charge lacked the "cojones" to face us! We paid our Bill of Euro 85-69 (not excessive, but perhaps at least the restaurant could have deducted the Starter charge?), without feeling inclined to add any gratuity. 'Shame - this restaurant has a basically good product, but surely customers shouldn't have their food rammed down their throats at the thoughtless whim of a Chef? And if you do "screw up", surely you should have the intestinal fortitude to face the aggrieved customer, and at least apologise?

review_preview: Greatly disappointed from our dining experience in La Cabaña, after high expectations.  Having come across it originally in passing the week previous, we liked the look of the it and based on the rave reviews from TripAdvisor, we agreed to return.  We felt the menu...
review_full: Greatly disappointed from our dining experience in La Cabaña, after high expectations. Having come across it originally in passing the week previous, we liked the look of the it and based on the rave reviews from TripAdvisor, we agreed to return. We felt the menu was a little pricey at first however, as our stay was nearly over in Madrid, we thought we'd try it nonetheless and agreed that we would all be willing to pay for a good quality, well-cooked steak. What we were served however, was far from impressive. Yes, they were cooked to our varying preferences and were enjoyable but for €17/18 for a steak alone- no sides included- I would've expected something significantly better and am confident I could produce something of similar calibre myself... For much, much cheaper; quite surprised to read other reviews citing them as "the best steak ever" - far from it, actually. Also worth noting is the extra 10% IVA (tax) charge on the total bill, something which seems to be excluded from the menu prices quite slyly. We were not impressed either by the €3.50 water bottle charge for the table (despite asking for just a glass), nor the extra €1.70 for bread - per piece, per person; adding this up for our party of five comes to €8.50 extra on the bill (excluding tax) which is extreme for something we never asked for and believed was complimentary, especially in a restaurant that pitches itself so 'up-market'.  If it were based on the steaks alone, I would rate about average although the main cause of our discontent arose from an issue with two of the main courses coming out as the wrong order. When asked upon serving if these were the correct dishes the waitress replied that they were however, after a few seconds examining the plates we could evidently see that they were not.  Upon clarifying this with the waitress, she took back the dishes and informed us that she will bring back the correct orders. After 10 minutes waiting, watching the rest of our party finish their steaks, the waitress reappeared with what appeared to be the correct order. It was not long though until we realised that in fact they were the same pieces of meat as the previous plates, topped with cheese and the other listed ingredients and cooked further in the oven. With no desire to eat over-cooked or re-heated meat, both plates were abandoned after a few bites. When asked to speak to a supervisor, we were told by the same waitress that she was his wife and we could explain the issue to her. She claimed that we ordered the incorrect main courses and explained this to another female colleague in Spanish (who was apparently another supervisor but turned out to be no help in the matter)- strange given the fact she failed to mention this when we raised the issue with her first- and suggested we were lying. She confronted us with a very aggressive and moody attitude and when requesting the bill, mentioning our desire to not be charged for the two main courses, she then made a snide comment about both plates being "half eaten". I have never encountered a waitress with such an attitude in any restaurant; the fact she claimed to be the wife of the supervisor says very little for the restaurant as a whole. No apology was received from any member of staff. At all. Would certainly not recommend visiting until they reevaluate their customer service.

review_preview: After eating nothing but finger food whilst attending a 4 day conference in Madrid, we were in desperate need of some real food.A quick Google for ‘Steak houses Madrid’ and the top of the list was La Cabana, Argentinian restaurant.No wonder it was...
review_full: After eating nothing but finger food whilst attending a 4 day conference in Madrid, we were in desperate need of some real food. A quick Google for ‘Steak houses Madrid’ and the top of the list was La Cabana, Argentinian restaurant. No wonder it was top of the list, this place is fantastic. We arrived without a reservation, but it was a Wednesday night, the staff promptly arranged our table for 8. The staff were very welcoming and attentive even when it became busy. There’s a small bar area as you enter the restaurant which became quite busy as the World Cup was on and they were showing the Argentina vs Holland game. The atmosphere in the place was fantastic. We all ordered steaks some Fillet, some Ribeye, and they we all cooked to perfection, with the exception of the ‘Well Done’ one which wasn’t ‘Well Done’ enough, so they quickly took it back and killed it some more. The wine list was pretty good, I’m not a wine snob but apparently you must have a Malbec with your steak and there was plenty to choose from and very reasonably priced (for a restaurant). I would definitely recommend this restaurant and will probably visit again if I’m ever in Madrid again.

title_review: Is this the best steak place in the world??
review_preview: Wandered in last night - no plan - and had the best damn ribeye I've ever had.  Bar none:  USA or Argentina.So good I couldn't believe it, so I came back tonite & tried the strip steak.  Again, amazing!I've eaten at all the...
review_full: Wandered in last night - no plan - and had the best damn ribeye I've ever had. Bar none: USA or Argentina. So good I couldn't believe it, so I came back tonite & tried the strip steak. Again, amazing! I've eaten at all the great Cathedrals of Beef in the USA and many in South America...but if 2 visits are any indication this place is the winner. (And the service is terrific too!) Never thought I'd fly 4000 miles to Madrid to eat at an Argentine restaurant that KILLS the steak experience...but these guys do. If you're in the neighborhood, don't walk - RUN - to this place.

review_full: I had the Monkfish & Prawn kebab - three tiny prawns and same size pieces of monkfish €17.50 with no side dishes. It should have been described as a mixed pepper & onion kebab as I had to look for the fish! However my partner had the steak and said it was reasonably priced in comparison to prices back home.

review_preview: This was a very nice place to enjoy a meal with friends.  The staff were very attentive and the atmosphere was very relaxing.   I was lucky enough to not pay the bill (someone else did..) so I can't comment on the prices; however, the meat...
review_full: This was a very nice place to enjoy a meal with friends. The staff were very attentive and the atmosphere was very relaxing. title_review: Amazing Cocktails, Stunning Food with Great Service
review_preview: Went for drinks in the downstairs cocktail bar and stayed for dinner in the restaurant upstairs. The cocktails are well thought out and use different ingredients and methods, not the normal drinks that you can find in any bar. The bar food is a wow,...
review_full: Went for drinks in the downstairs cocktail bar and stayed for dinner in the restaurant upstairs. The cocktails are well thought out and use different ingredients and methods, not the normal drinks that you can find in any bar. The bar food is a wow, these Bao buns stuffed with mushrooms & truffles and topped with a quails egg is my new favourite thing. Dinner upstairs is insane with beautifully prepared local ingredients that are all in season and paired with wines that you will not find by yourself- it just works! Not cheap, but excellent food and service is not, so splash out on this one.

review_preview: Authentic Spanish cuisine with outstanding service, remarkable Spanish wines by glass, half-glass (for tastings) and of course bottles, selected and paired if so desired by a sommelier who is one of the brother-owners), celebrating their mother. review_full: Authentic Spanish cuisine with outstanding service, remarkable Spanish wines by glass, half-glass (for tastings) and of course bottles, selected and paired if so desired by a sommelier who is one of the brother-owners), celebrating their mother. review_full: Tapas, some traditional and others not, dominate the menu but they also have main courses. Since I was eating alone, I gravitated toward the mains. I chose steak tartare which was fabulous. They’ve got a wide selection of excellent wines. Service was attentive and knowledgeable.

title_review: Delightful staff, perfectly pitched food with matching wines

title_review: Angelita, must to go place if you are in Madrid!
review_preview: We went there for dinner tonight. This place compared to Arzabal Market place, it is heaven and hell apart, though the price is not tha apart. All the ingredients are locally sourced, fresh and the best. The tomato with sea salt and Olive oil is...
review_full: We went there for dinner tonight. This place compared to Arzabal Market place, it is heaven and hell apart, though the price is not tha apart.  All the ingredients are locally sourced, fresh and the best.  The tomato with sea salt and Olive oil is must have.  The caramelized salmon tartare melts in your mouth giving you heavenly sensation. The grilled pork in sweet potato source is the best pork we ever have.  Best of all, the waiting staff are very professional and knowledgeable, making great recommendation. Our server David, he is extremely patient and helpful, he patiently and enthusiastically let us taste few wines before we settling at three different wines before the meal, then made a fantastic choice for bottle going with our meal.  The restaurant is simply a must go, if you are in town. We have to go back there because the menu is long and and changing based the availability of its ingredients.

title_review: Sweetest sisters, great, and cheap, food
review_preview: I was happy to find this hidden gem through tripadvisor. It was not too crowded (3/6 ish tables filled when we were there around 10 pm on a Monday). The sisters really wanted everyone to have a great experience and talked to us for a...
review_full: I was happy to find this hidden gem through tripadvisor. It was not too crowded (3/6 ish tables filled when we were there around 10 pm on a Monday). title_review: Disappointing after reading the other reviews
review_preview: We came here to celebrate my 60th birthday having booked online in advance and really were keen to love it. Descriptions of the hosts were accurate and they were solicitous and helpful but the menu was difficult to fathom and the food was disappointing -...
review_full: We came here to celebrate my 60th birthday having booked online in advance and really were keen to love it. Descriptions of the hosts were accurate and they were solicitous and helpful but the menu was difficult to fathom and the food was disappointing - very fatty and too salty for our taste although nothing one could say was particularly bad. It was pricey (€45 a head) for two courses and a bottle of house wine and water.

review_preview: To be frank, I was a little hesitant when first entering the small restaurant up a short flight of stairs. The look of the restaurant is as if it has been set in a person's living room - I was also a little dismissive as...
review_full: To be frank, I was a little hesitant when first entering the small restaurant up a short flight of stairs. The look of the restaurant is as if it has been set in a person's living room - I was also a little dismissive as to the amount of sweetbreads on the English menu. There was only one other couple in the restaurant and we were dining fairly late which, I think, can be worrisome. That said, we were made to feel welcome immediately, with a friendly smile, and the owner recommended some dishes to us.  The restaurant soon filled up, however, and the restaurant had a pleasant atmosphere - striking a good balance between being somewhat private but not too isolating! We were brought some small appetisers to keep us going and we had a bottle of wine that was so delicious we end up having another! Food was fantastic and the service was great.

review_preview: We ate here after a long and testing day at work, and it was the perfect antidote. The two sisters are great fun! Food was delicious and the dining room feels very homely.
review_full: We ate here after a long and testing day at work, and it was the perfect antidote. The two sisters are great fun! Food was delicious and the dining room feels very homely.

review_preview: we had one night in Madrid and happily I found Algarabia online.  This is one of my top dining experiences ever, anywhere!  You must eat here.  The food is delicious, the setting beautiful and the experience with the two sisters is the pure joy of...
review_full: we had one night in Madrid and happily I found Algarabia online. This is one of my top dining experiences ever, anywhere! You must eat here. The food is delicious, the setting beautiful and the experience with the two sisters is the pure joy of dining at Algarabia. They have a passion for pleasing their customers and they spent time visiting with us. You cannot miss with your choices from their menu, but the asparagus is one of the most delicious items I ever put in my mouth. Their house wine is fairly priced and delicious as well. The next time in Madrid, I will run back to this restaurant and I hight recommend it. My comment to them is that the food was what you expect from a grandmother's kitchen--delicious and full of love of the food and presentation. This is not a touristy place to eat, but a real Spanish dining experience. You owe yourself this experience, so just go!!

review_preview: I came here with my girlfriend for dinner on January 24, 2015. The dinner card, at a first look, seems quite simple and typically spanish (with some specialities from La Rioja Province)However, the food tasted excellent and it could not have been better. We...
review_full: I came here with my girlfriend for dinner on January 24, 2015. The dinner card, at a first look, seems quite simple and typically spanish (with some specialities from La Rioja Province) However, the food tasted excellent and it could not have been better. We were offered some aperitives along with the food we ordered. The starter I had was great and so was the menu and the dessert. What I liked the most is that there were very few tables in the restaurant, so not many people can dine here at the same time. Therefor, the atmosphere was quiet and it made you feel like you are dining at home. The interiors are like in a house and lit with candles, so you feel very comfortable. The two sisters that run the restaurant are very friendly and talkative and will come to the table to ask you if your enjoying your dinner. It was a different dinner experience, due to the small size and the "home-feeling" the place transmits to you. Would recommend it to couples.

review_preview: We were a group of 4 in Madrid for new year and 2 of our friends had suggested this lovely restaurant to us. Booking by email was easy and the restaurant easy to find. Whilst it does feel like you are in someone's front room...
review_full: We were a group of 4 in Madrid for new year and 2 of our friends had suggested this lovely restaurant to us. Booking by email was easy and the restaurant easy to find. Whilst it does feel like you are in someone's front room rather than a restaurant, this just adds to the atmosphere and anything else would feel wrong. Isabel, our host, was lovely and explained all the dishes including which ones our gluten intolerant friend could not have. The food is very Spanish and the asparagus is to die for!!!! Food was lovely and good value but what makes this place is Isabel and Pilar. Such a friendly atmosphere. It's quirky but we loved it!!

title_review: Two sisters from Rioja with good food in a small restaurant experience
review_preview: This place is unusual and very pleasant. It is run by two sisters with strong links to Rioja-land.  One is the chef (who also takes lovely photos when she travels!) and the other is front of house. This is not your mass-market chain and is...
review_full: This place is unusual and very pleasant. It is run by two sisters with strong links to Rioja-land. One is the chef (who also takes lovely photos when she travels!) and the other is front of house. This is not your mass-market chain and is highly one-of-a-kind.  We turned up a touch early at 9:25pm and had to ring the doorbell because they do not open till 9:30. Inviting open dining room that does look like a family's front room. Probably only 8 tables and on this evening it was half Spanish and half foreigners though suspect normally more Spanish regulars.  Booking was easy by email or online.  The two ladies spoke good English and there are some menus also in English.  The food was good - though a touch confusing on what was 'meant' to be a starter or a main. All was consistently high quality. One of our party had snails, another superb asparagus and I shared excellent jamon with my wife. I had baby squid as a main course.  Wine list was short and geared around their house wine from Rioja. Full bodied and suited to the food.  The service was a delight and fun - like a mother checking on her extended family at the various tables. By the end you almost feel like old friends. Lovely for an evening out with friends or as a couple but maybe not if you plan for a very quiet meal to propose!?  No music though which is great and tables have very reasonable gaps between them.  Whole meal with three courses for four of us with two bottles came to 200E.

review_full: Exceptional Spanish cuisine served in an intimate and very homely environment. Family run with a great service and attention to detail. Highly recommended

review_full: We were fortunate to get a reservation for a late lunch. We were the only folks there and the two hosts were really friendly and sociable. Despite our best effort not to order too much food, the recommendations won us over. The appetizer cucumber soup was very refreshing, I can imagine eating this for summer too. The most memorable dishes were the stewed squid and the quail thign. The freshly made pasta with mushroom and bacon was also a hit. It was simple and delicious, something that Mum would make anytime. The desserts were rather homely, with the mousse really light and sweet, but not cloying so. I'll come here again if possible!

Highly recommendable small restaurant, deswegen at least one Michelin Star .

review_preview: Fantastic meal some of the best food that I have had anywhere. The menu is short but this is so as not to dilute the skill, care and passion brought into each dish. Before the visit was concerned there was not enough variety but so...
review_full: Fantastic meal some of the best food that I have had anywhere. The menu is short but this is so as not to dilute the skill, care and passion brought into each dish. review_full: I live nearby but always have to book ahead to eat here, no doubt because it is very special in a low key high quality sort of way. You get a full description of all that you consume and you can tell all are very proud of what you are being served. A table by the window is always my choice.

review_preview: We made a reservation a few weeks ahead and were glad we did. The location is within walking distance of the Prado, down a small street. Once inside the restaurant is an oasis. The chef is also the host, and is very welcoming. His passion...
review_full: We made a reservation a few weeks ahead and were glad we did. The location is within walking distance of the Prado, down a small street. Once inside the restaurant is an oasis. The chef is also the host, and is very welcoming. His passion for the food comes through in his explanations. The food itself was delicious and not outrageously expensive.  The only strange thing was that several people came off the street and were turned back because they didn't have a reservation; however, over the two hours that we were there there were multiple tables free.

review_preview: We tried to have lunch here a couple of days ago and were fortunate to have a few more days in Madrid to book our lunch today. We loved the personal, attentive service and the love for simple, authentic food. We let the owner choose...
review_full: We tried to have lunch here a couple of days ago and were fortunate to have a few more days in Madrid to book our lunch today. We loved the personal, attentive service and the love for simple, authentic food. We let the owner choose our food and wine and everything was delicious. The sous vide leeks were probably the simplest but most delicious dish but nothing disappointed. We watched at least six groups being turned away so book if you can. Considering the quality of the food and the central location €74 for two was very reasonable for six tasting sized courses and matching wines. A perfect way to end a morning at Reina Sophia.

review_full: Really enjoyed our meal here for a late lunch. We hadn't reserved in advance and they worked to accommodate us. The atmosphere is great. Staff friendly. Lovely vibe. Great artwork too.

We had a beautiful tomato salad of a particular variety that was in season with just sea salt and olive oil and of course incredible bread. Then on to their ratatouille (pisto) that was fresh from their great produce and had the oxtail cannelloni for the main. Every dish came out at the right pace. Not too fast or slow. Also do not forget to ask for wine suggestions. This is a wine bar as well so they have everything by the glass. Each selection commended was superb. To top off the great food I would be remiss to not mention how professional and obviously proud of their product and how nice the staff was. What a terrific experience in Spain. Next trip I will most definitely return.

title_review: A perfect evening in all respects
review_preview: Hosting guests who've not been in madrid before, I went looking for new options and found this delightful restaurant.  Thank you TA!After an initial glitch with the reservations, it was all great!  Any good restaurant relies on a combination of front of house and...
review_full: Hosting guests who've not been in madrid before, I went looking for new options and found this delightful restaurant. Thank you TA! After an initial glitch with the reservations, it was all great! Any good restaurant relies on a combination of front of house and kitchen skills ... these sisters have it down pat!  The lovely lady in the dining room guided us through the menu (encouraging my friends to be more adventurous ... "why would you come to Madrid and order pasta") First two lovely hors d'oeuvres: a hake terrine, light as can be, and a porcion of one of the richest pates I've had the chance to sample in some time. At the hostess's suggestion we stuck with the house wine, a lovely crianza. For first courses we sampled the sardines, lovely, meaty and just briny enough; the duck confit with leeks (served instead with white asparagus and exceptional); a beautiful salad with perfectly cooked pulpo; and the croquettas, a bit cheesey for me, but my friends loved them. Entrees brought oxtails, so simple so rich in a gorgeous broth/gravy and topped with matchstick fried potatoes; the solomillo pork sirloin, served with an intense reduction of onions that had friends wiping the plate; and an order of the pasta with bacon and mushrooms (though she discouraged it, my buddy wanted pasta and he was quite happy with this take on carbonara).  There are 3 desserts on the menu so we sampled them all ... the rice pudding was more of a custard with less rice than anticipated; the apple/toffee confection was incredible and the chocolate torte was rich and dark We were among the last tables and the chef came out to chat with us ... such a treat! This is a restaurant that goes out of its way to make you feel welcome. you simply have to try it!

review_preview: We really enjoyed this restaurant. Very cozy and we felt as if we were in someone's house. We chose the following: asparagus in pastry lightly fried, sardines in a light tomato sauce with pistachios, cod in tomato sauce, and a house specialty, braised pork, braised...
review_full: We really enjoyed this restaurant. Very cozy and we felt as if we were in someone's house.  We chose the following: asparagus in pastry lightly fried, sardines in a light tomato sauce with pistachios, cod in tomato sauce, and a house specialty, braised pork, braised and slightly blackened. Dessert was a lovely dark chocolate raspberry cake as well as an apple mixture topped with a flavored whipped cream. Very satisfying meal and since we split the cod, pork, and dessert (split in the kitchen), we weren't stuffed. I had white wine, my husband red, and both were wonderful.  Arriving at 9ish made sure we were in the company of other tourists. We were all well received. The sister who is a chef came out to say hello and both sisters were so cute. Worth the visit for a simple but wonderful meal!
