We had booked a tabled for 9.30 and got to the door at 9.25, after knocking the door was opened, we said we had a reservation for 9.30 and the lady said 'well its only 9.25!). We realised later that the place didn't open until 9.30. However, we were allowed in and were the only diners there until another group came in as we were leaving at 11.00. It is rather liked being in someone's home and after eating the two sisters engaged us in deep conversation about politics, the EU and other weighty matters for some considerable time. The food was good, albeit from a very short menu list, the sisters very pleasant and interesting and the experience was somewhat out of the ordinary which added variety to our stay in Madrid. We found the pricing to be a little on the high side considering that we did not have a dessert. I suggest you go there if you want some very nice home traditional cooking and a different kind of restaurant experience. Maybe avoid it if you have kids and/or want a more typical restaurant evening. We were glad we went.

I am surprised now at the great reviews this restaurant gets as certainly not deserved in our opinion. Not sure what happened? Would not recommend to others. title_review: charming small restaurant, not for picky eaters
review_preview: Intimate and warm little restaurant run by two sisters who are very involved in your dining experience.  In general, this could be a good thing.  Food was good -- the oxtail and octopus salad both delicious.  Homemade pasta also delicious.  Did not love the bacalao...
review_full: Intimate and warm little restaurant run by two sisters who are very involved in your dining experience. In general, this could be a good thing. Food was good -- the oxtail and octopus salad both delicious. Homemade pasta also delicious. Did not love the bacalao with tomato sauce -- too fishy in taste for us, and we eat a lot of fish.  However, be careful in selecting this restaurant if you have young kids who are picky eaters or who may not enjoy the lengthy dining experience of a formal meal. Our experience was ruined by the overly obnoxious comments from the hostess who reprimanded us about our picky eater. On the plus side: they reluctantly agreed to make an existing menu item (fresh pasta with bacon and mushrooms) as plain pasta with nothing on it for our picky eater. We appreciated this gesture, and were willing to have him sit with no food rather than inconvenience the restaurant if it was too much trouble to make the plain pasta. (Which we explained in Spanish when we ordered. We recognized we were asking for a favor.). On the negative side: the hostess insulted our child, our parenting, and our unwillingness to force him to eat more diverse food at the restaurant several times. She justified these comments by saying she was like a grandmother, telling us what she thought. Our child was not loud, disruptive, rude, or in any way bothering any other diners in the small dining room, so her comments really were about her own personal feelings not about ensuring other diners in the restaurant had a nice time. Also when I did not care for the bacalao, so did not finish it, her comment was that Americans eat a lot of food ('always eat so much') so why wasn't I eating it. Essentially the insults-based service got old by the end of dinner. This would have been valuable information for us to know when booking the restaurant because I would not have chosen to make a reservation here had I known that they were not tolerant of kids. Come here as a couple for a romantic dinner, or for a more adult dining experience -- the interactions with the sisters provides a unique experience of the culture, and I'm sure the hostess would be more enjoyable then.

review_full: Isabella and Pylar, I hope I have the spellings correct, are two wonderful sisters. Our wonderful evening started by Isabella answering the door and informing me that there had been some SNAFU regarding my reservation and they were closed due to a private party. After viewing my displeasure at not being able to enjoy their hospitality, she said OK just come in and we will make it happen. And make it happen they did with great aplomb. Isabella made us feel right at home, gave great suggestions and overcame our inability to speak Spanish. Such great food, wine with their own label and great conversation. We ended up closing the restaurant after the private party broke up and totally enjoyed visiting with both sisters. If we ever visit Madrid again this will be the first and only restaurant we will visit. Truely Exceptional!!!

title_review: We liked it so much that we went back!
review_preview: We enjoyed our first evening with Isabel and Pilar so much that we decided to return to Algarabia the night before we had to leave Madrid.  We were honored that they greeted us like old friends.We concur with other reviewers who have described better...
review_full: We enjoyed our first evening with Isabel and Pilar so much that we decided to return to Algarabia the night before we had to leave Madrid. We were honored that they greeted us like old friends. We concur with other reviewers who have described better than we can Pilar's excellent cuisine and Isabel's warm, graceful hospitality. Their ability to converse with their guests in Spanish, English, Italian and who knows what other language is astonishing. They turned our entire experience of Madrid into a warm welcome, one that we hope to repeat in the coming years.

review_preview: This is an intimate,special restaurant in a small street near Opera in Madrid. The 2 sisters know exactly how to make diners welcome, Pilar is an excellent chef, her knowledge and ability is second to none, very dish is delicious and beautifully presented, it tastes...
review_full: This is an intimate,special restaurant in a small street near Opera in Madrid. The 2 sisters know exactly how to make diners welcome, Pilar is an excellent chef, her knowledge and ability is second to none, very dish is delicious and beautifully presented, it tastes as good as it looks. I recommend the eggs and chorizo starter, the pork loin and the ox tail dish gets a huge rap from us. Desserts are all great and the wine delish. Isabelle runs the front of house with elegance and grace, she is a delight and made us very welcome. This was our final special meal in Spain, and it was a fitting end to a special trip. Thank you Isabelle and Pilar, we hope to return next year.

review_preview: A hidden gem situated around a quiet corner from the Opera station ran by two sisters (Isabel and Pilar) serving authentic cuisine.It is a very small restaurant and Isabel was very welcoming and attentive during the meal. It's definitely a place to visit if...
review_full: A hidden gem situated around a quiet corner from the Opera station ran by two sisters (Isabel and Pilar) serving authentic cuisine. review_preview: My girlfriend and I visited La Pizzateca a week ago on our last evening in Madrid, after reading the many praising reviews. And we did not regret it! It's a pretty small take away restaurant, but there are a few spots where you can sit...
review_full: My girlfriend and I visited La Pizzateca a week ago on our last evening in Madrid, after reading the many praising reviews. And we did not regret it!  It's a pretty small take away restaurant, but there are a few spots where you can sit to eat your order. We both had a pizza with two different halfs, so we got to taste four different kinds of pizza; romana (with potatoes and truffle cream), napolitana (anchovies), roja (bolognese) and genovesa (pesto). All of these were very good, but the romana was absolutely amazing. I never had a pizza with potatoes before, but seriously, you should order this one!  Prices are fair, restaurant is nicely decorated and the owner is very friendly and dedicated to his job. Would definately recommend and will surely come back the next time I'm in Madrid.

title_review: Sin duda la mejor pizza en el centro!
review_preview: (english below!)¡10/10 LA PIZZATECA ES EPIC!Vengo aquí dos veces semanalmente ahora porque la pizza es TAN buena que no puedo evitarla x los findes. Empiezo cuando termino la semana de trabajo y vuelvo con una amiga casi siempre.Las pizzas llevan ingredientes muy...
review_full: (english below!) ¡10/10 LA PIZZATECA ES EPIC! Vengo aquí dos veces semanalmente ahora porque la pizza es TAN buena que no puedo evitarla x los findes. Empiezo cuando termino la semana de trabajo y vuelvo con una amiga casi siempre. Las pizzas llevan ingredientes muy frescos y bastantes deliciosos. Cada pizza, incluso los para llevar o comer en la barra en frente estan hechas con amor y atención. Nunca he pedido una porción, da igual de que parte de la bandeja era, que era mala. Si tienes el tiempo, déjate sentar y comer porque las pizzas hecho del momento son aún más riquísimas! Con una Alhambra para acompañarla, la pizza de La Pizzateca ha ganado la posición más alta y favorita en mi corazón de toda la capital (y tengo bastantes amigüitos Italianos que hacen una buena pizza, eh?). Los empleados son cariñosos y atentos, bilingües (por se a caso), y los jefes son majísimos! Vete prontísimo a La Pizzateca, ¡¡no lo vas a lamentar!! ==English== Disclaimer: I eat here twice a week now because my typical once a week has become insufficient!! La Pizzateca has become my favorite pizza joint in the entire capital region and I have quit a few Italian restaurant-owning friends! The pizza has fresh delicious ingredients, made fresh all day long, and I have yet to find anything comparable in tastiness and quality of ingredients and texture/crispiness etc etc. New Yorkers and lovers of that style of pizza (personally I'm a Sicilian guy, i like doughy thick pizza) will LOVE this stuff! I do too (call me a convert!).  With a great drinks menu, a slew of pizza and food choices, super kind and friendly (bilingual!) staff, and owners that care about their customers and employees bringing a much welcomed and rare family vibe to their business, I can't stress enough how much you need to go to La Pizzateca ASAP.  Forget papizza and these pop up 2€ tiny slice fast food chains and get yourself what your mouth and stomach deserve!

title_review: The Best Meal of Our Vacation
review_preview: My best friend and I toured Rome, Seville, Madrid, and Barcelona, and this meal was, by far, the best meal we ate in our three week European vacation. The restaurant is run by two adorable sisters, and when you enter, it feels like you are...
review_full: My best friend and I toured Rome, Seville, Madrid, and Barcelona, and this meal was, by far, the best meal we ate in our three week European vacation. The restaurant is run by two adorable sisters, and when you enter, it feels like you are dining in the sunroom of their home. One sister runs the front of the house while the other prepares the food as it's ordered. We ate a variety of dishes, including the ox-tail and the sweetbreads with leeks and fava beans. Amazing! But the standout dish was the fresh pasta with bacon and mushrooms. It was a simple dish, but the flavors were unbelievable. The pasta here was better than any pasta dish we ate in Rome. And the sisters are a delightful pair, indeed! They both seemed happy to learn I live in Atlanta, Georgia, because the chef is a fan of "Gone With the Wind." We talked for a bit after the meal was complete. I would recommend to anyone: don't leave Madrid without dining at this wonderful restaurant!

title_review: A restaurant with soul and cooking with passion
review_preview: A rarity.  A restaurant that exudes soul.  And cooking with passion.  It's small, quirky and indy - and all the better for it.  Home cooking at its best.  Complimentary pate as an amuse bouche (the most delicious pate de foie I have ever tasted).  I...
review_full: A rarity. A restaurant that exudes soul. And cooking with passion. It's small, quirky and indy - and all the better for it. Home cooking at its best. Complimentary pate as an amuse bouche (the most delicious pate de foie I have ever tasted). I had white asparagus with iberica ham to start followed by melt-in-the-mouth oxtail. The pudding of apples with caramel cream was a perfect ending. All washed down with house Riocha. The owners - two sisters - show a genuine interest in and for their guests. I wish there were more restaurants like this! Heart warming in every respect.

review_preview: We were recommended this restaurant by a local on a TA forum. We booked in for lunch and happened to be the only people dining, this was a shame, it lacked the atmosphere and ambiance from having other diners around you, though they were good...
review_full: We were recommended this restaurant by a local on a TA forum. We booked in for lunch and happened to be the only people dining, this was a shame, it lacked the atmosphere and ambiance from having other diners around you, though they were good enough to take our booking based on us being their only booking that day, apparently they have more in the evening, however sittings didn't start until 9:30pm and we had to be up early the next day. The restaurant was like you were entering some-ones house, this in intentional and adds to the character. The two sisters who run this place are very friendly and welcoming. Lots of chatter at our table. The food is decent home cooked food. We had their tasting menu. The pate was very good as were the chargrilled baby tomatoes. The cod was ok, cooked well, but quite fishy, soggy skin and a tomato sauce that doesn't come close to the one I cook myself at home. The pork with caramelised onions was ok, though the large medallion (few different sizes on the plate) was still raw in the middle. I assume this was intentional, though too underdone for my taste. My husband ate it and has lived to tell the tale. I probably wouldn't go back here, I love rustic home cooked food, but this could have been tastier. I would also recommend a visit in the evening - for more ambiance.

review_preview: We dined here during a conference and we were not an easy group as our numbers kept changing and there were 2 vegetarians in our party.  We went from a table of ten to a group of 20 which is the maximum the restaurant can...
review_full: We dined here during a conference and we were not an easy group as our numbers kept changing and there were 2 vegetarians in our party. We went from a table of ten to a group of 20 which is the maximum the restaurant can take at one time and we all arrived at once which was a challenge for the restaurant as there are only two people in the kitchen and two serving but they managed magnificently. The restaurant is a little house and so it is just like eating in someone's home. Our group loved it and some of them wanted to go back the next night and were disappointed that it was closed. This included one of the vegetarians who was so pleased to have been especially catered for. This is not four star Michelin dining but you really do get the feeling that you are eating in Spain. The food is Riojan from the area where the sisters grew up and is the food of the countryside there. Isabella, the sister who is front of house is quite a character and put up with a lot from us that night but we all had a great evening and left the staff completely exhausted but still smiling.

review_preview: So I can't say that I know authentic Spanish food to challenge it.  What I do know is delicious food.  We had homemade pate, crisps, and my meal, the ox-tail was spot on.  The most amazing part of this was the personal touch.  This is...
review_full: So I can't say that I know authentic Spanish food to challenge it. What I do know is delicious food. We had homemade pate, crisps, and my meal, the ox-tail was spot on. The most amazing part of this was the personal touch. This is not a restaurant you want to go to, if you want to be left alone. The two sisters working there definitely were interactive, wanting to know where we were from, and to practice their English. This isn't a fancy restaurant, or a trendy restaurant. It's a family restaurant, with people who try hard, and do very well. Definitely a highlight on our visit.

review_preview: My husband & I made reservations (needed!) for our last night in Madrid and I am so glad we did!  This is a small, intimate restaurant run by two sisters who coddle their guests- trust whatever is recommended, including wine choices!  I had an amazing...
review_full: My husband & I made reservations (needed!) for our last night in Madrid and I am so glad we did! This is a small, intimate restaurant run by two sisters who coddle their guests- trust whatever is recommended, including wine choices! I had an amazing octopus salad as a starter- clean, fresh coins of octopus over wilted arugula- SO good I polished off the plate and would only give my spouse one bite! He started with a salad of mixed greens with dried venison, pine nuts & raisins. Also good! Then he got the oxtail- which was a stretch for us but turned out to be delightful! Super tender with a savory sauce- yum. I got pork with braised onions and loved it! Go with the older version of the house Rioja (older as in aged longer)- it was amazing! Then we had yummy coffee with roasted apples with a toffee cream for me and an unusual chocolate dessert for hubby, it was like chocolate toffee- really good! The entire meal was under E100! There is just one setting per night, it opens at 9:30, I suggest making reservations for that time and plan on a 3 hour dinner! It's small enough that we ended up chatting with 2 other tables, which was fun too!

review_preview: We are not used to eating as late as they do in Spain.  We had planned to go to another restaurant but it was not open.  We later discovered it opens at 9.00 p.m which is too late for me.  This place was open, looked...
review_full: We are not used to eating as late as they do in Spain. We had planned to go to another restaurant but it was not open. We later discovered it opens at 9.00 p.m which is too late for me. This place was open, looked nice and the menu suited us so we went in. We chose a pasta dish each, I had ravioli and my husband had cannelloni which we had with a salad and a glass of delicious red wine (Malbec). I realise this was an odd choice for an Argentinian restaurant but we wanted something light. Both dishes were nicely cooked and the service was good. The price was reasonable for a capital city, so a couple of days later we chose to eat there again. This time my husband had a steak with Roquefort sauce and I chose chicken with tomato and mozzarella. My husband's port was generous enough but mine was simply huge! I ate a good part and my husband helped me out but it was just too much. If like other places you can share I'd suggest you do with this and maybe order their roasted red peppers or a salad to go with it. Because we are so early it was very quiet and so it is difficult to comment on the atmosphere but it was nicely laid out and the service both times was very friendly and professional.

review_preview: This place has actually produced one of our favorite pizzas of all time!  We figured it may be touristy as it was located near some of the hotels and museums, but there were a handful of locals in there.We stopped in for dinner on...
review_full: This place has actually produced one of our favorite pizzas of all time! We figured it may be touristy as it was located near some of the hotels and museums, but there were a handful of locals in there. We stopped in for dinner on a whim. The pizza was amazing...and we only had the vegetarian fare. If you are specifically expecting New York or Chicago style pizza, you are not going to find that. What you will find, though, are unique flavor combinations and very fresh pizzas. I believe we tried four slices: cheese, margherita, mushrooms/truffle oil, and potatoes (I've never had anything like the potato pizza). The crust, cheese, and sauces all tasted very fresh. What puts this place over the top is the owner. A very nice guy, if not a little quirky, and you can tell he is passionate about his craft. It shines through in his pizza. From the outside it looks quite quiet but don't let that fool you - eating here is like being welcomed into someone's home and treated like an honored guest. The manageress was full of helpful suggestions and funny comments and makes you feel incredibly welcome, even when I accidentally broke a lamp bulb. We shared two starters and then had a main each which includes some amazing canapes and 'warm up' dishes, and with a couple of glasses of wine each it came to around E80 for dinner for two which felt like a great deal. The cooking is from the Rioja area with dishes as simple as sardines in oil through to a complex octopus stew and oxtail that melted in the mouth.  Honestly, give it a try, they deserve to be fully booked every night.

review_full: Reading the reviews from other visitors (which we used as a base to book the restaurant) we expected quite a bit more.  Pretty much everyone at the restaurant was foreign. No problem there but the lack of locals provided a first indication.  The table we were sat was bouncing. The owner's response was: "you can't lean your arms on the table". No fix here.  Wine menu came (had to wash my hands afterwards). Bottles that had not been updated in years. We asked for a 2001 reserve and were told that the only available was a 2008. "So, there must be a difference in price then? (I asked). Answ: No, years don't matter, the only thing that matters is the price".  The menu was brief, but quick and concise better than extensive and undeliverable, Right?. No. when the food came is was served on plates that had seen better days and well below average. €14 for a french omelet. 2 tiny new potatoes with my cod which should have been swimming in sauce but had less than butter on a toast.  Bathrooms ... clearly trying to be carbon neutral here. The light was on a timer that did not last more than 30 seconds. Keeping in mind that the lid had to be kept up with the left hand, right hand busy, light off ... pitch black adventure.  All in all .. an experience ruined by lack of professionalism, over-inflated ego and below average food.  I will certainly not forget the place but for the wrong reasons

review_full: First, the "wine bar" upstairs: really a restaurant and wine bar. Whether you sit at the bar or take a table, the food is high quality and fun, the service is friendly and engaging, and the wine list and wine pairings are on a different level altogether. I would recommend any winelover to just leave yourselves in the hands of the staff to try wines by the glass and half glass with different dishes. Not only will they give you some really high quality, fun pairings, they will also explain them to you and have no problem whatsoever adapting to personal tastes. And if there is one other area in which they excel it is cheeses: you must leave room for cheeses. Again, a fantastic offering, beautifully presented and explained.  Then the American Bar downstairs: one of Madrid's very top cocktail bars. Plenty of room to sit, perch or lean, and a fantastic combination of classic and updated cocktails of every kind, with some really fun presentations. Top recommendation - go to the bar and watch the boys in action. As good as anything you will see. And if you prefer your booze neat, you won't believe the collection of old bottles they have.  One of my favourite places anywhere in the world. Really outstanding.

review_full: This is a place that cares about wine and can give you an excellent introduction to the many terrific wines of Spain that take you deeper into both terroir and grape variety. And they also have a very interesting and impressive set of natural wines too - wines made with natural yeast and fermentation and the minimum of sulphites.  If you have never tried them this is a good place to begin. Davide and his team know their stuff and are happy to share their knowledge and enthusiasm. Accompanying the wine are small plates to share. Every one we had from pepper salad with smoked sardine, via mushrooms to a tartare and sashimi was perfectly judged and presented. Don't go here if you are looking for huge heavy dishes. But if you enjoy good, fresh, light food, this is the place to taste the new Spain

A wonderful experience and a must in Madrid and mandatory visit for all our future stops in Madrid. Thank you Chef Matias and staff.

title_review: Came here for late night dinner
review_preview: My husband and I came for a late night dinner. We were very excited to visit after hearing that it was one of the top rated restaurants in Madrid. We also liked the cool minimalist decor and overall ambience. The dinner started off great. Nice...
review_full: My husband and I came for a late night dinner. We were very excited to visit after hearing that it was one of the top rated restaurants in Madrid. We also liked the cool minimalist decor and overall ambience.  The dinner started off great. Nice olives, lovely wine, smooth vermouth on ice, and affable waiter. But then it went downhill.  We ordered the special "tacos" and hake. There was some miscommunication over what was in the tacos. The waiter described it as salmon but it turned out to be pigs ears. This is a significant difference. Had we been into pig's ears (chewy and fatty) I'm sure we would have appreciated them but that is not what we thought we were getting into. Out for a fun time, we were in great spirits and found the situation funny! A surly waiter who we explained everything to had zero sense of humor or empathy and simply removed them from our table.  Next came the hake, which was described as in a seafood broth with a seaweed (I think) foam and some sort of aioli. Mmm we were excited. The dish, however, was trying way too hard. Although very artful it was a molecular gastronomic disappointment. The seafood "broth" was more of a gooey paste at odds with dabs of an angry chipotle sauce and yellow boring mayonnaise; the thin foam had as much flavor as a glass of aqua con gas; worse, the "foam" was dampening in a few minutes what was probably once crispy fish skin; the fish underneath was slightly undercooked and bland. A few dense fingerling potatoes rolled around on the plate in a blind quest for some salt. The dish was also lukewarm. It was a fail.  Needless to say we did not finish the dish. Surly waiter came back, asked us how it was, and we tried hard to be nice. He was not pleased. Neither were we!!! We passed on dessert. The check returned, inclusive of the unfinished pigs ears.  We are from New York City and we are not gastronomic neophytes. Plus, we travel a ton. We know what's going on in the food world (btw, foams are so five years ago!). Aside from the lackluster food, what really got us was how rude the waiter was. He knew we were unhappy, and with a few simple gestures he could have easily turned it around. It was just so crappy. So much of Spain and Madrid have fantastic food experiences and this was not one of them. What a waste of a night out.

review_full: Well my oh my this was pleasant. I went here on a recommendation from a client on one of our tours. I liked the name - vaguely meaning cacophony in the Moorish tongue - and the idea that it was a family run Riojan bar. I. Love. La. Rioja. So I took my friend and his partner there for a birthday lunch.  We stayed for about an hour and a half or more. The lady running, and I'm disappointed I've forgotten her name - lots of good wine, which by the way is unique to their bar and comes from David Moreno's estate - was a chirpy and bolshy Riojan lady who talked to us, joked with us, and made us feel like we were in her home. Her sister, who came out a little later from the kitchen, was equally as pleasant and passionate about the food they were serving.  The food then: we were served some creative free little tapas first and then moved on to the ordered food. Delightful sticks of asparagus wrapped in a crunchy coating served with a mojo picon sauce. Delicious and light. Then the best croquetas I have ever had. Small yes, but so creamy and made with red shrimp. Then I opted for the chumarro - a whole sliced and perfectly grilled pork loin - served with caramelised onions. Light and fragrant and meaty. Perfectly cooked.  The desserts were nice enough, a sort of toffee thing on an apple thing and a decadent dark chocolate slice. I can't remember to be honest. I was having too much of a good time by that point. Price. A little high, not crazy, for the portion size. But the quality spoke for itself.  This is not a place for a casual lunch. This is something a little nicer, a little more special. A place for a romantic dinner or a celebration or a time when you fancy something with a touch of class.  Really very good indeed.

review_preview: I went several times for dinner in August.  It's a unique experience.  The cozy dining has a casual, ramshackle, informal elegance to it.  The food is top-notch:  the bright, sassy, warmly welcoming, and riotously funny sisters who run this restaurant (Isabel in the dining room,...
review_full: I went several times for dinner in August. It's a unique experience. The cozy dining has a casual, ramshackle, informal elegance to it. The food is top-notch: the bright, sassy, warmly welcoming, and riotously funny sisters who run this restaurant (Isabel in the dining room, Pilar in the kitchen) like to think of it as traditional food from the Rioja. And it is certainly that, backed up by absolute freshness and care in preparation. But this is to do Pilar's cooking a disservice: she brings a creative touch to everything she makes, drawing freely on other Spanish culinary traditions (the Catalan romesco sauce with the divine batter-fried asparagus spears) and on her own inventiveness (a rice pudding that's almost mousse-like in its lightness because she puts the the grains of rice through a grinder--ask Isabel to tell you the story of why Pilar came up with that twist). A delightful, very Madrilene combination of wit, warmth, tradition, and innovation.

review_full: Let's get one thing out of the way when reviewing restaurants in Madrid: The design and service will always be implacable, it's just something you come to expect from good restaurants in this city.  Arguably, Algarabia (loud joy in Arabic) takes it to a whole new level. Charming doesn't even begin to describe it. It's an experience on its own.  The food, however, is average. The Asparagus were brilliant but the croquettes were mediocre. The oxtail was amazing but the pasta was nothing to write home about, and the crunchy chocolate cake was simply awful.  So, where all that leaves us? Sadly to say, right in the middle. It's a unique experience, but in this price range, and especially in a city like Madrid which is dirty cheep, this is nice but probably not enough.

review_preview: We had such fond memories of the evening we spent with Pilar and Isabel at Algarabia our last time in Madrid that we decided to dine there again on our first and last evenings in Madrid. We walked from our apartment on a very cold...
review_full: We had such fond memories of the evening we spent with Pilar and Isabel at Algarabia our last time in Madrid that we decided to dine there again on our first and last evenings in Madrid. We walked from our apartment on a very cold but clear night, past the resplendant Royal Palace and Teatro Real, both virtually at the restaurant's doorstep. As we stepped inside the always stylish and beautiful Isabel welcomed us with a warm embrace and a kiss on both cheeks reminding us why we were so looking forward to our return visit..Isabel even remembered to seat us at the same table for two by the window! Pilar, busy working her magic in kitchen, stuck her head out and blew us a kiss as we settled in for another wonderful evening in Rioja. Many of our favorites were still on the menu such as Pilar's signature Rabo de Toro and the exquisite Trigueros Crujientes, along with new dishes such as the Salad with Boar Sausage and the Rabbit Ragout, a marvelously light and succulent take on Ragout a la Bolognese. Algarabia's David Moreno Rioja is smooth and elegant and pairs wonderfully with the Rioja cuisine. The mood is quiet and ever so romantic. The restaurant's setting in the parlor of an old Madrileño house exudes warmth and elegance, a perfect combination of mood, Rioja and great food. Later (much later, this is Madrid) Pilar joined us for a glass of wine at our table and we chatted like old friends before enjoying dessert and 'chupitos' of their wonderful herb Aguardiente. Algarabia remains our favorite restaurant not just in Madrid but in all of Spain. When in Madrid, come to Algarabia and let Pilar and Isabel take you on a delicious journey to Rioja ... Mil gracias chicas, hasta la proxima!

review_full: My wife and I went about two weeks ago. We had our hotel make the reservation, which, we've learned, usually gets you a decent table, good service, etc. After 25 minutes of sitting at the table with no one paying any attention, I got up and went to where all the servers were congregating to get some help. The service did not get any better than that. We ordered steak and they served my wife a rare tenderloin, which was not how we ordered it. I again had to get up with the steak, walked it to the kitchen, and gave it to another server who was there. They did replace it with a nicely done tenderloin. Restaurant was also very loud, which didn't help matters. I think we'd skip this one until they get their act together.

review_full: We dined at this restaurant in late June and were delighted to have the opportunity to eat in a quaint, family run establishment in the center of the city. Their benevolence was affirmed when they recommended other restaurants to us in other cities. Travelers who are yearning to detach themselves from the chaotic maelstrom of touristic dining will appreciate the sentimentality and authenticity of this dining experience.

review_preview: Situated up a short side street close to the Royal Palace,this small restaurant (about 7 or 8 tables) is run by 2 sisters.Pilar cooks fantastic food and Isabel provides front of house duties.It is what i would call a traditional spanish restaurant.There is an english...
review_full: Situated up a short side street close to the Royal Palace,this small restaurant (about 7 or 8 tables) is run by 2 sisters.Pilar cooks fantastic food and Isabel provides front of house duties.It is what i would call a traditional spanish restaurant.There is an english version of the menu,but Isabel will explain more about the dishes to you if required.The choice of dishes is quite varied.I chose pork loin with caramelized onions for my main course whilst my wife had a pasta dish.Bread comes with your meal (normal in Madrid restaurants).We were given a complimentary pate and toast and a biscuit with some fish on them whilst we waited for our food. Pilar came out of the kitchen at the end and chatted to us for a while (not understanding each others language we got by however). It happened to be her birthday so everybody gave her their "happy returns".We enjoyed our meals,the experience,and the friendly atmosphere created by the owners.Make sure you book before you go!!!

The food was great and very authentic. We felt very special with the excellent service and personal attention given us by sisters Pilar and Isabel, the chef and owner. Having dinner in Algarabia was one of the highlights of our holiday in Madrid.

review_preview: I wanted to take a visiting American family for a "local" dining experience and tried Algarabia (based on Tripadvisor reviews).  Pilar and Isabel, the two charming sisters behind the place, treated us like family and we had a memorable evening.  This is a quiet small...
review_full: I wanted to take a visiting American family for a "local" dining experience and tried Algarabia (based on Tripadvisor reviews). Pilar and Isabel, the two charming sisters behind the place, treated us like family and we had a memorable evening. This is a quiet small restaurant with a very homelike feeling.  The food is northern Spanish and a goes a bit further in terms of sauces and creativity than the standard Madrid fare. The menu is not large, but there are daily specials which change. To be honest, between the chatter and Rioja, I can't remember precisely what everyone ate, but it did span from seafood to duck and we all enjoyed what we ordered. I'd say it was moderately priced and good value for the money. I'll definitely return.

I asked if I could sit at the bar she said yes! She didn’t give me a menu or anything. The restaurant for its size wasn’t staffed appropriately. One bartender, 3 servers and no hostess. I sat at the bar watching the bartender sweat while making drinks, this is the first restaurant I’ve been to in Madrid where the wait staff look like they hate their jobs. Finally after waiting at the bar without an acknowledgement or a menu, the bartender asked if I needed something. And I replied with yes I’d like to order food and drinks but I don’t have a menu. He brought one over and blamed the waitress for not letting him know. I made it very easy and asked for a Tinto de verano as my drink. For food I asked what the cheeseless options were and I took his recommendations. I specifically asked for items without cheese. I watched him make my drinks with 90% Fanta and a splash of wine. It was terrible, I didn’t finish it. My pizza came out fine but he ordered me a dish that was covered in cheese. It wasn’t until I sent that back that the wait staff started to be nice to me. I hadn’t eaten all day and you would expect this to be the most amazing pizza ever. It wasn’t. I even heard other tables complain/comment “this better be the best pizza I’ve ever had.” At the bar I asked the bartender if I could pay he heard me but ignored my request since he was so slammed. It wasn’t until I got out of my seat that he went and got the terminal to charge my card. The whole experience was complete and utter garbage. Never again.

I ordered the beef tenderloin with peppercorn sauce and my partner had the 500g ribeye.  The steaks were cooked to perfection, after hearing they tended to come slightly rare we opted for medium which was cooked beautifully, you could practically cut them with your spoon . There was no fat or gristle just soft, brilliantly seasoned meat and the fries (I had the garlic and parsley ones) went fantastically. Paired with a glass of red wine I can honestly say it was the best meal I've ever had.  The staff were excellent and switched between Spanish and English with no hesitation and the whole place had a relaxed yet vibrant atmosphere.  I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting.

review_full: My mother and I came here late in the evening on our first night in Madrid. It was close to the hotel, had great reviews, and we wanted a break from all of the jamon and tapas we'd been eating in Spain. We absolutely loved it. We ordered the la diavola, a glass of wine, and a small beer. The pizza was so good that we ate the lightly crispy yet slightly chewy crust with no sauce. Anyone who's eaten pizza knows that good crust is not easy to find. Even at good pizzerias you'll see bits of crust left on the table. But here our pizza was perfectly cooked and we ate every last bit of it. In fact, we loved the food there so much that we came back 2 nights later! And for a second time, we had an excellent pizza that was cooked to perfection. But what makes this awesome little pizza joint so great is how reasonably priced it was!  So if you're looking for a spot to grab a relatively cheap but great pizza, come here!

They also rip you off by giving you bread without asking you if you want it then charging you €1.90 per person for it. We didn’t want the bread, didn’t ask for it, we were never asked if we wanted it and we didn’t eat any of it. It was just plopped on our table by a passing waiter so we didn’t even have a chance to say we didn’t want it. Definitely felt like a scam and although it was only a couple of euros each, given the meal was already overpriced, this place is obviously a tourist trap. When I complained about being charged for bread we didn’t want, the manager kept arguing that it’s normal in Spain. In our experience, this is not the case. They should at least ask you if you want the bread as in a lot of other restaurants (in Spain and other European countries) they don’t charge extra for bread, and if they do, they will ask you if you want bread or only bring it if you order it

review_full: So we chose this place based on reviews and our location that evening (not too far from Retiro Park where we went for a long walk that evening). The food was excellent and the staff were very friendly and spoke good English. A thing to note beyond the Spanish eating lunch and dinner later than most of us are used to doing is that restaurants that close after lunch and re-open at dinner don't really open early or even right on time. If they open at 7:00, you should expect on going around 7:10-7:15. We went at 7:00 and visited a couple tourist shops on the street (very eclectic shops on this street) and around 7:15 went to eat and were the first to walk in. We had a serving of the fried mozzarella and it was fabulous (although not healthy at all I imagine) and a couple pizzas. It was excellent pizza and better than any pizza I've had in Europe outside of Italy. Fair prices and, as I mentioned, friendly and attentive staff. Highly recommend the place.

title_review: Some of the best pizza we have ever had, even in Italy
review_preview: After some lazy nights eating preservative-laden sandwiches from the local VIPS, we were looking for something to take to the hotel in walking distance and not croquetas or bocadillos de jamon again. Looking at the map, we found this place and got the Napoletana (anchovies,...
review_full: After some lazy nights eating preservative-laden sandwiches from the local VIPS, we were looking for something to take to the hotel in walking distance and not croquetas or bocadillos de jamon again. Looking at the map, we found this place and got the Napoletana (anchovies, black olives, cheese, tomatoes, oregano). It was terrific, probably better than any other pizza we have had in terms of pure flavor, including those we've had in various spots all over Italy. The crust is a tad thicker and less wet than Italian pizza, and the toppings were of the perfect amount--not too much like in the US and not as minimalistic as in some Italian places. We will return at least once more for the Romana (with roasted potatoes). There's a deal of two portions of whatever selections are available that night and a drink for around 6 euros and one can get whole pies from 7 to around 9 euros..

review_preview: From the outside this looks like a fairly ordinary small shop selling squares of takeaway pizza. Yes it does sell good quality takeaway pizza but past the counter you can also find a delightful, bright, small restaurant area. In the restaurant you can choose the...
review_full: From the outside this looks like a fairly ordinary small shop selling squares of takeaway pizza. Yes it does sell good quality takeaway pizza but past the counter you can also find a delightful, bright, small restaurant area. In the restaurant you can choose the pizza on show in the shop and there is also an extensive separate menu mainly featuring pizza but with a few other choices.  The reason to go here is the excellent quality of the pizza. We cannot ever remember such a light and crispy crust, and from the restaurant you can partly see the kitchen where everything is clearly prepared with great care and attention resulting in a delicious meal. Wine also decent and good value.  We ate here 3 nights during a 6 night stay in Madrid. Given the practise in Madrid that you almost always get a snack with any drinks you buy in a bar it was a great way to start the night sharing a pizza and a bottle of wine (for about 20 euros) without ever getting over full. Finally all of the staff we met - waiters, cook and the manager - were super friendly and efficient.

title_review: Good for simple /elegant meal - would have liked more contrast in flavors
review_preview: I went here based on the trip advisor reviews.  First off:  the service and decor were lovely.  The food was really well prepared, but flavors seemed a bit of one note.The menu looked really interesting - we tried a tomato salad, pig ear and...
review_full: I went here based on the trip advisor reviews. First off: the service and decor were lovely. The food was really well prepared, but flavors seemed a bit of one note. The menu looked really interesting - we tried a tomato salad, pig ear and sea bass. They sent a complimentary salmon tartare that was over the top. If i could have ordered that as an app, i would have. It had salt and JALEPENO!!!! I realized i had been missing heat in my food and this was spectacular. The flavors were balanced, and well contrasted, yum. So, my expectations were high - the tomato salad - eh. Nice tomatoes, needed something else in flavor contrast. The pigs ear weren't my thing - but i tried them. They were supposed to have a spicy sauce - Crispy, but again, the flavor seemed one note and not spicy. Sea bass was cooked perfectly, but again, no contrast. I really wanted an acid (lemon/vinegar) or an element of surprise.  Maybe we didn't order the right items to show the talent of this place. Clearly they have skill and know what they are doing. If you like a simple well cooked meal, it is worth a try.

review_preview: After reading the rave reviews I knew I had to go have some pizza at La Pizzateca. It´s an unassuming place located within a 10 minute walk from the Center of Madrid. It sits 5 to 6 people so it´s best to get your pizza...
review_full: After reading the rave reviews I knew I had to go have some pizza at La Pizzateca. It´s an unassuming place located within a 10 minute walk from the Center of Madrid. It sits 5 to 6 people so it´s best to get your pizza to go and eat outside now that the weather is nice.  You can either get a whole pie made for you (have to wait 15 minutes or so) or eat one of their pre-made slices that they will graciously heat in the pizza oven. We went for the 2 slices + beverage combo each and we ended up with quite a lot of pizza to eat. The crust was thick, crunchy and had a great hand made flavor. They had quite a variety of flavors so we got one of each: arugula, goat cheese and balsamic pizza, 5 cheese pizza, mushroom and truffle oil pizza, sweet onions and bacon... They were all delicious and the price was unbeatable. 6 slices (each slice is split in halves so you end up with 12 small portions) + 3 bevarages: 20 Euros. My girlfriend complained that we had to wait a bit for the pizzas to heat but it wasn´t an issue for me.  If you are craving a slice of pizza do yourself a favor and drag your behind to this place, it will be worth it.

review_preview: Compared to other parts of Spain, Madrid can feel more expensive. But then you don't mind paying more if the meal is truly special. A meal at Angelita is just this!Visiting Madrid a couple of weeks ago with my husband and father in law,...
review_full: Compared to other parts of Spain, Madrid can feel more expensive. But then you don't mind paying more if the meal is truly special. A meal at Angelita is just this! Visiting Madrid a couple of weeks ago with my husband and father in law, we tried our luck to get a table on a Friday night. The restaurant was fully booked, but they had space at the bar. We ordered several dishes to share, as well as wine to accompany. The food - incredible. The vegetable dishes were incredibly tasty and the meat dishes cooked to perfection. The presentation of the food was very photo worthy! The wine list is extensive and the staff are readily available to suggest what might go well with your dishes. We opted for the cheese board for desert - what a lovely experience! We were invited to the cheese trolley where one of the team talked through each and every cheese, helping us to pick a selection. One of the ladies at the bar then helped us pick a desert wine to match. The staff/team who work at this restaurant are simply brilliant. Attention to detail, knowledge of dishes, wine etc really impressive. We had a throughly enjoyable evening, not just because the food was simply delicious, but because the whole atmosphere and experience at Angelita meant that for days afterwards we were talking about how much we had enjoyed it. Yes slightly more expensive, but yes definitely worth it. Be sure to book though!

review_preview: This restaurant is pretty tiny (only 11 or 12 tables) so it's worth arriving early evening when they open at 8ish to avoid disappointment, as half of those tables were already  booked-out the night we visited. The staff are really friendly and welcoming and provide...
review_full: This restaurant is pretty tiny (only 11 or 12 tables) so it's worth arriving early evening when they open at 8ish to avoid disappointment, as half of those tables were already booked-out the night we visited. The staff are really friendly and welcoming and provide English menus if required. The menu itself is divided into 5 veggie, 5 meat, 5 fish dishes and 5 desserts, and you can either order full portions, half portions or tapas portions. This is a great idea, as it makes it possible to enjoy many of the delights on offer, regardless of how hungry you are, and the waitress was happy to advise us on how much food we should order. Every dish that came was simply delicious, and I was surprised (not to mention slightly disappointed!) that 'half portions' would fill me up so much that I wouldn't be able to fit in my favourite part of any meal - the dessert! The final bill came to less than €26 between two of us - amazing value!! Can't recommend this place enough if you're looking for great value, simple cuisine that's cooked to perfection, in a friendly, laid-back place. If I ever find myself in Madrid again, I'll be seeking Taberna Origen out again for sure.

review_preview: I went to this tapas bar thanks to Tripadvisor for a dinner on saturday night. Luckily we arrived around 8.30 pm when the restaurant was about to open, because after 9.30 pm it got really crowd and every table was occupied. So my first recommendation...
review_full: I went to this tapas bar thanks to Tripadvisor for a dinner on saturday night.  Luckily we arrived around 8.30 pm when the restaurant was about to open, because after 9.30 pm it got really crowd and every table was occupied. So my first recommendation here is that if you are a group of people, it's better to get the reservation right away or just arrive early.  Located in a quiet street with nothing nearby, it seemed like the place is well known by the locals. It looks normal, nothing pretentious. But it is really at its best! However, the staffs were very friendly and attentive. They attended us with smiley face and very calm, unlike other typical spanish bar. They provide a menu in english and spanish (all the dishes and drinks). So if you don't speak spanish, it won't be a problem to order. Taberna Origen offers a selection of dishes, dividing into three sections: from the sea, the vegetable, and the earth. So the variety is limited, but trust me… regardless the number of dishes offered, they are all beautifully presented and from my own experience (I have tried 5)… all are well cooked and designed. The quality prevails over the quantity! Another good thing of this place is that they let you choose the size: full portion, half portion and tapas portion with different prices. This allows you to try different dishes. We were two and we ordered 5 of half-portion dishes and a dessert. A bit way too much.  We tried out:  - Cuttlefish burger with alioli of yuzu and arugula (6.5 euros) - for half portion and it came with 2 burgers, perfect for us, since we were 2!. The cuttlefish burger was great. The alioli blew me away.  - Meat mini burgers- the meat was perfectly cooked (6.5 euros), regardless it is very normal dishes, they are able to make it different!; - Rabo de toro (ox tail) - very tender and tasty (7.00 euros);  - Tartare of tuna with avocado ice-cream - the touch of sesame oil makes it to the top of my list. What a great combination of flavours! (9.00 euros); - Iberian cheeks with yucca chips - the sauce was great. The cheek was very soft and absorbed all the sauce. Yucca chips were a great idea to combine with the cheek (7.00 euros).  For the dessert: we were actually very full but my friend was like to try so we shared chocolate coulant with violet ice-cream (4.5 euros) - the coulant was light but very chocolatey. However, it is not cloying which is ideal! Violet ice-cream was creamy, rich in violet but not so sweet, so it adds a little freshness to the dish. I was full but I enjoyed it until my very last bite! The drinks were at reasonable price. I ordered a glass of Cava (3 euros) and two bottle of water (1.5 euro each). We ended up paying 46.50 euros for two and were about to explode by the time we leave. I would say that if you order reasonably, it should cost roughly 15-20 euros per person. :D During lunch time they do offer 2 tapas-size dishes (anything from the menu) with a dessert or coffee and a glass beer/ house wine for 7.95 euros. This is a hidden gem in Madrid. It's not so far from the city centre and it is walkable from Princesa Shopping Street and Plaza de España. So if you wanna try a modern spanish tapas with a lot of idea and love in it, you can't miss this place. I have had a great time there and definitely will go back!

She patiently explained each type of unconventional pizza (a nice change!) in the display multiple times to each of us before quickly grabbing our orders and popping each slice into the oven to warm up. She brought the pizza to our table promptly, and it was absolutely delicious!! I was worried about my 15 Euro budget, but it was only about 6 Euros for 2 large slices (got to sample 2 diff flavors!) and a drink. I was full and saved money! Would definitely recommend and come back again!

title_review: Not as vegetarian friendly as they say
review_preview: Went there for a business dinner with large group. I was one of the two vegeterians. Before anything else, lets be clear: the food is good and the staff is friendly. But for a place that claimed to be vegetarian friendly, i was disapointed to...
review_full: Went there for a business dinner with large group. I was one of the two vegeterians. Before anything else, lets be clear: the food is good and the staff is friendly. But for a place that claimed to be vegetarian friendly, i was disapointed to find it is the same story as is so many other places. The main course for those who chose fish or meat was copious, with a generous portion of meat and a reasonable side dish. For the same price, vegetarians got what i would call "only the side dish": a portion of candied vegetables.... topped with a few tiny fish fillets that looked like anchovies (have not tried those). The vegetable were excellent though. Dont claim you are vegetarian friendly if you cant make a balanced main course or if you think vegetarians are either rabbits or on a diet.

review_preview: Hello eveveryone! We have eaten at this nice restaurant two times, both diners. First time we had no reservation made, but they were very nice and provided a table for two given that we will take no more than 1h40min to eat.The atmosphere is...
review_full: Hello eveveryone!  We have eaten at this nice restaurant two times, both diners. First time we had no reservation made, but they were very nice and provided a table for two given that we will take no more than 1h40min to eat. The atmosphere is pleasant, the service is prompt and people are helpful and provide details on the dishes. A very good wine list to acompany the ....BEST STEAKS IN MY LIFE. I am a beef lover, I eat beef 2, 3 times a week, I cook my own steaks and I tried quite a few meat types, american, french, belgian, scotish, uruguayan, argentinian, japaneese, romanian etc. I had some really good steaks at home, and very good ones going out. But so far the experience here in Madrid was the best. After the first time we ate, i said we have to try it again. The tenderloin was melting in your mouth, the rib eye was pleasantly greasy and with the nice bbq flavor of fried fat. If you want the juicy beef, go for the 500g ribeye steak. If you want lean meat, the tenderloin is excelent. The pepper souce is also very good. I am by no means an expert in steaks, but as an amator eater I definitely recommend you to go and try this amazing steak house.

review_full: We turned up at this place on a Friday night at 8 without a booking and were told the first available table was 10-10:30pm so we booked for the next night. We had ordered the mixed grill which is a sharer for two for mains but while we were eating our starters we became aware of our waitress (who was otherwise lovely throughout as were the other staff) disconcertingly hovering, waiting for us to finish. I noticed that the mixed grill was waiting under their heat lamps so I don't know what was going on there! Everything was fine service-wise after that. On reflection we thought we should have ordered a steak because we've had better mixed grills. Some of the meat was a bit fatty for us and although we usually order our steaks rare we thought medium would be the safer call - but it was all pretty much bloody. The puds were nice and the atmosphere in the restaurant was lively as it was busy and it's well appointed. So not 5 stars but a solid 4 and, as I say, we would go for a steak next time because the ones our neighbours had looked scrummy.

review_full: Simply put this restaurant is worth your patronage! This was our last meal in Europe before heading back to the states and what a memorable one it was. We had tapas at three different restaurants while in the Barcelona and Madrid area and this was by far the best meal that we had. One of the things that made it so special was the very unique dishes with VERY fresh ingredients, vegetarian friendly and allowed you to have portion control. They had something for everyone. We ordered about 5 different dishes plus 2 desserts. Each of the dishes came out at a different time - you could tell that they were made on the spot that you were not getting anything that seemed to be prepared ahead of time. It was great because you had the chance to savor each one of the dishes before receiving the next and you were not rushed and could enjoy hot dishes hot and cold dishes cold. The bread was warm and tasty it was if they made it just for you! We had one or two meals from each one of the three categories in addition to our dessert. Make sure that you save room for dessert since we had a molten chocolate cake with lavender ice cream that was "to die for"! All that being said the wait staff was extremely warm and friendly... review_full: I am giving a lot of "excellent" reviews in Spain because Trip Advisor has been a wonderful resource for Madrid, Córdoba, Granada, and Malaga. Taberna Origen is several blocks into a neighborhood outside the tourist areas. It is just to the north of Plaza Espana, which is also a Metro stop. I would never have found it without TripAdvisor. We are making a short stop over in Madrid after almost three weeks in Spain, and the restaurant is just two blocks from our very quiet hotel in a very quiet neighborhood. The space is a bit odd. When we walked in, we though there were only two tables, both occupied, but a very enthusiastic waiter -- and maybe owner -- waived us into a back dining area with another 5 tables. We were in for lunch. My guess is reservations are a must for dinner. Very nicely decorated with white walls, dark furniture, and modern art. Really pleasant. This is a "fusion" restaurant, so knowing exactly what you are getting can be a challenge. They have an English version of the menu, which helps, but exactly what is cod fitters with pad Thai sauce? No one in the restaurant had good English, but we managed to get by with our limited conversational Spanish and a lot of good humor. We were adventurous, and the cod fritters we excellent. I am not sure what the pad Thai sauce was, other than it was light and a great accompaniment. The menu is tapas, media, and raciones, and you will not recognize a single item. Much to our delight, the menu had a number of vegetable options, including a cone of tempura vegetables with teriyaki sauce that was as fabulous as we had hoped. Our waiter helped us not over order by advising us to order media when our impulse was raciones. We were started with complementary tiny Spanish omelettes, which were a fusion of a German potato pancake and the ubiquitous Spanish omelette. Very delicate and an interesting twist. Cannot go wrong with potatoes in our book. A highlight for us was the boletus mushroom croquettes, which were all mushroom -- no cheese -- and just a burst of flavor. We also went for the tomato plate advised by several reviewers, and it was also surprising. What appeared were two beautifully vine ripened tomatoes still on the vine that were baked and had honey drizzled over them. Inside was a stuffing of sheep cheese chopped very fine. Amazing flavor.  In addition to the vegetable tempura and cod fritters, we also had a seafood lasagna with tomato, which included two very nice grilled scallops. I was expecting tomato sauce, but what came was deconstructed and had a cream sauce that beautifully played background to the seafood. The tomato was fresh slices with rounds of al dente pasta, almost like ravioli rounds. This was a meal of wonderful surprises that used the tapas format to great advantage without being greasy bar food. This is an inventive kitchen that loves food and knows cuisine. Total bill for two was €36, which is a bargain for two people. The overall menu, which we did not begin to sample, is organized into sections with vegetables, fish and seafood, and meat. We did not try anything from the meat section. The restaurant describes itself as fusion, and it is. It pays to be adventurous, because I am not sure that even with impeccable Spanish our preconceptions would have not carried the day. And this is the point of the restaurant: taking the dominant Spanish form and surprising you with wonderful food you could not imagine. I wish we had this restaurant in our home town. I just hope it's blooming success does not kill it.

We also ordered the suckling pig, which our son enjoyed, but not as much as I enjoyed the butter fish, which was very fresh and excellently prepared. The house made smoked tuna salads with gazpacho dressing were a standout. But the mains were even better - baked Guinea fowl served on roasted eggplant and Iberian pork in a sweet and sour sauce. We went on the Saturday night and decided to have the 7 course tasting menu at €34 per head. Every course was unusual, beautifully presented and explained in detail by our attentive waitress Michela. The service was very friendly and professional.  We had such a lovely evening that we decided to return again on the Sunday night. We again were looked after by Michela who when we said we would like the tasting menu again, spent time with us going through each course on the menu and made suggestions for different options. We ended up having a completely different tasting menu except for the cold soup starter and mango dessert which were both too good to not have again. The second tasting menu was even more incredible than the day before.  Taking into consideration the food, decor, service and price we both felt this was one of the best meals we have ever had and are only sad that the restaurant is based in Madrid and not somewhere in London where we can visit regularly! Highly recommended.

title_review: If you want to be EXCELLENT, try being consistently GOOD first!
review_preview: We had read about this downtown restaurant, liked the sound of it, and with the help of "recepcion" at the excellent "Catalonia Las Cortes" hotel, had booked a table for Friday night dinner. Still adjusting to local late-eating habits, we were the first to arrive...
review_full: We had read about this downtown restaurant, liked the sound of it, and with the help of "recepcion" at the excellent "Catalonia Las Cortes" hotel, had booked a table for Friday night dinner. Still adjusting to local late-eating habits, we were the first to arrive on the night - it's a modern, well-appointed premises on Calle Imperial, with predominantly black/white decor + beaty music. Our welcome was friendly, and we had the distinct advantage of being able to pick a table. The Menu indicated a reasonable choice of Starters : my "Better Half" M selected a "Hummus" dish, while I went for the "Home-made Foie Terrine". The choice of Mains was disappointing : Squid, an obscure Japanese Fish, "Spanish style" Sweet & Sour Pork, Steak Tartare, and, believe it or not, Hamburger! Em, we both felt our only reasonable option was the Hamburger, despite the fact that we've eaten in more than a few restaurants with widely varying influences. As for wine, we attempted to order the seemingly better of the Rias Baixas offerings, but had to settle for the lesser option, making us wonder how much of the presented list was actually available? Anyway, we ordered, and as a preliminary we were presented with a "Celery Mojito" - our Server glowingly talked this up (a practice we discovered is part of the restaurant's approach) and it was quite tasty. As for our actual Starters, M pronounced her Hummus "very tasty", and my "Terrine", while beautifully presented, suffered from being too chilled, obscuring the flavour. Style, presentation and description are clearly "big" here, and we'll come back to that. Our Burgers (!) were in a kind-of layered format : M's was cooked as requested, while mine was nothing like the "medium-well" I had asked for in both Spanish & English. With a bit of "theatre" my Burger was taken back and replaced - one of the layers this time was about right, the other not. We sampled one of the Desserts - an apple crumble - again introduced to us with elaborate, glowing descriptions of its ingredients, and it was fair enough. Before the end, we were presented with fancy pastille-type sweets, on a special piece of stone (of course!). Our conclusion about this meal + our experience at "Metro Bistro" is simply this : you're clearly aspiring to be something "different", but before you get to be "excellent", you need to consistently get the "basics" right. For example, your choice of "Mains" is poor, and if you insist on including Hamburger, get the cooking right ; secondly, ensure that when the customer needs cutlery, he/she has it ; thirdly, if you're bringing a meal course to the table, make sure the last course has been cleared, if only for space reasons. And above all, don't confuse "talking-up" and "fancy presentation" with delivery of a good food & service product! Our Bill (pre-gratuity) was a very reasonable Euro 66-60, and we would commend our main Server Michaela for her good-humoured efforts.

review_preview: We just returned from three weeks in Spain, and this was by far the best meal we had on the entire trip.  We had heard that Madrid rivaled Barcelona with regard to good food, but we had not been very impressed with the cuisine in...
review_full: We just returned from three weeks in Spain, and this was by far the best meal we had on the entire trip. We had heard that Madrid rivaled Barcelona with regard to good food, but we had not been very impressed with the cuisine in Madrid before eating here. We wandered in about 7:30, hoping to make reservations for another night. They offered to take us on the spot, provided we promised to be done by 9:30 p.m. - no problem!! The interior decor is very modern but in a warm and inviting way. The wait staff were all very good, but especially Miguel. He was amazingly friendly and helpful, explaining each dish as he served it. We started with the complimentary celery mojito, which was absolutely wonderful - wish we could make that one at home! I had the salmorejo, the tipico cold tomato soup, which was out of this world. My husband had roasted potatoes with three different "dips" - he was delighted with all three. There was also a variety of breads which were divine, and I'm not a big bread eater. We both enjoyed our main course - the lamb was especially good - and we even managed dessert. After three weeks of good to very good food, this was the first really magnificent meal we had - one night before returning home. Don't miss eating here if you are in Madrid, just off Plaza Mayor on C. Imperial. Be sure to make reservations because they are VERY popular. We were just lucky they took pity on us!!

review_full: This is the best meal we have had in Madrid. Excellent service, lovely decor, and -- most importantly -- excellent food. This was an impressive meal at the price point. The free celery mojito rimmed with sugar crystal starter was top notch. The carmalized goat cheese salad with figs was a perfect starter. We followed that with the potatoes and 3 sauces. We then split the sweet and sour pork, which was a perfect, subtle dish. We ended with the assortment of chocolates that offers 4 chocolate servings on a slate plate -- enough to sate any two chocolate lovers. We leave completely satisfied.

review_full: After reading reviews of Metro Bistro on Tripadvisor, we decided to try it. I asked about reservations via email and received a prompt and polite reply. Metro Bistro is on the far side of Plaza Mayor, but it doesn't have that tourist feel to it. We didn't want to go tourist, and MB most certainly was the best place we could have chosen. We started with a cheese plate and croquetas which were both great. I want to point out that we mentioned not liking bleu cheese, and they substituted for us. My husband had the pork, and i had the hamburger. I wanted the lamb but ended up with the burger because the veal/bacon combination sounded good. Both of our meals were delicious. We liked all of the breads, although we thought the cocoa/herb bread was a little weird. As others have mentioned, they started us with a celery mojito and finished the meal with amaretto and passion fruit jells. I have to say I loved the celery mojito. One note about service: We had two servers—a female and a male. The woman was kind enough, but she was not as warm and friendly as the man. I'm guessing the waiter's name was Ibrahim, although I'm not sure. He explained how he made the mojito, and when I accidentally fell getting out of the booth, he was right there to help me get up, get me water/wine/whatever. If we ever get back to Madrid, we will definitely go back.

title_review: WOW - Delicioso! And at such great value
review_preview: So this one evening my colleague wasn't keen on going out to dinner so I ended up dining alone. Booked through email a few hours before with no issues.Was a little concerned when I showed up at 9 pm and the place was practically...
review_full: So this one evening my colleague wasn't keen on going out to dinner so I ended up dining alone. Booked through email a few hours before with no issues. Was a little concerned when I showed up at 9 pm and the place was practically empty barring an American couple. But, I quickly decided on the 7-course menu degustacion (tasting menu) as I love chefs showcasing the best of what they can offer and I eat pretty much anything. Course after course of sumptious, delicious plates were put in front of me. Most of which didn't really look or feel much smaller than full sized plates (I compared with a couple of tables nearby who ordered ala carte). Here's what I got...(more or less since the waiter didn't speak too much English and my Spanish is basic at best). - Celery (and apple?) mojito amuse bouche: Delightfully refreshing shot - Salmorejo (typical cold Spanish tomato soup) with pesto oil and olive oil ice cream - 3 breads: Rosemary/chocolate/orange; White; Corn & chilli with rosemary butter and black olive butter. I only really liked the dark rosemary bread tbh - Terrine of foie gras and orange with a puree that tasted a little like plum - Stack of confit vegetables with salsa Romesco and some kind of fish slices - Squid stuffed with ham on a bed of black risotto and turmeric (or safron?) cream - perfectly cook and delicious! - Loin of pork that managed to be pink on the inside (sous vide?) and a bit crispy on the outside, with a red wine reduction, serviced with crispy filo rolls filled with red cabbage and a blueberry paste - Mango mouse, with mango slices wrapped around set yogurt - Death by Chocolate: Ultra light mousse, dense mousse, chocolate truffle and a small pot of warm chocolate sauce (I'm sure there's a more fancy word) with popping candy - loved loved the warm chocolate with popping candy! - Pastilles of amaretto and passion fruit I absolutely cleaned my plate. Some very accomplished (and technical) cooking and very few things that I didn't care for (mostly the bread). The price for all this? €32!! In the UK I've paid about £50 for the same quality and less food. Service was pretty attentive (they took time to explain the elements of the dish to me), although felt a bit rushed when the place filled up (after 10 pm). The clientelle is quite tourist based (probably both thanks to TripAdvisor and its location just outside of Plaza Mayor), but don't let that put you off, it really is excellent modern cooking with traditional influences. It's number 1 on my list of restaurants to come back to next time I'm in Madrid.

review_full: We were ready for something different. We found it at Metro Bistro. The restaurant is easily located in the Central part of the city, easy to find and get to by foot. We were greeted immediately by very friendly staff. They seated our party of 6 in the lovely back room that allowed easy conversation and a round table. We are a mixed diet party with one very strict vegetarian, four that prefer fish and vegetarian diet and one without limits. The menu here was suited for all but our very strict vegetarian guest. Were all disappointed by the choice of grilled vegetables when it arrived at her plate at room temperature and molded with eel on top. This was not described at all in the menu or by the waiter. We also were surprised by the house salad. The figs and lettuce varieties were nice, as was the dressing, but the goat cheese was a full round of cheese, and was far too much. We found a nice wine selection with prices ranging appropriately and many options. We enjoyed the appetizers: the bread selection, cheeses and the chef’s take on potatoes.  The main courses we shared included the Black Pearl—a scallops and black risotto dish with a curry sauce. This was delicious and fun but not the risotto you would likely expect. If you are not willing to experiment this might not be your choice. Two in our party ordered the Cod Casserole. The portion of fish was large. The sauce and vegetables were heavy and the fish was a bit overwhelmed by the surroundings. The Butter Fish was the best item on the menu. The fish was firm, well cooked and surrounded by a ginger and teriyaki based sauce. Very nice and a great treat.  But save space for the dessert. This was the gem of this visit. We ordered 2 for the table, the Chocolate and the Apple Tat. Our waiter recommended the proper order to eat the 5 separate chocolates and he was completely correct. WOW. The apple dessert was a great contrast. These are a must try if you choose this restaurant. After a 5 day visit, you should give it a try.

review_preview: The new hubby and I went out to Origen after watching the sunset at the Temple Debod. It was an unassuming place a few streets down but was already quite packed so we were seated at the bar. I was a little unsure about the...
review_full: The new hubby and I went out to Origen after watching the sunset at the Temple Debod. It was an unassuming place a few streets down but was already quite packed so we were seated at the bar. I was a little unsure about the tight space but the staff worked it very well!  We've been staying in an area where English is not prevalent so we again used (our terrible) Spanish to order but they offered us menus in English so we didn't have to struggle through the translations. We ordered the croquettes (not the shrimp ones), the cuttlefish burger, the steak tartar, and the oxtail to start with a bottle of wine (el bruja). They brought us some fresh bread and gazpacho of (I believe) beet juice and olive oil. It was extremely delicious and hinted at the delicacies to come! The croquettes came a few minutes after we had finished our starter and I was happily surprised to find they were stuffed with cream of mushroom! (Cream of mushroom is one of my favorite things ever invented). So if mushrooms are a favorite, the croquettes are definitely a must!! The cuttlefish burger, again came a few minutes after we had finished and our plates had been cleared, was amazing. The aioli was delicious with the fish (but not overpowering) and very tender fish. This was the hubby's most favorite. Next the steak tartar, very delicious and fresh! Seasoned similarly to a classical deviled egg with stone mustard and slightly sweet bits of pickle. The last "entree" was the only entree we ordered not tapas sized (because it was only available in 1/2 or full size). The oxtail was off the bone, and encased in a sausage casing and covered in sauce. I'm not a huge fan of shredded meat due to chunks of fat it it was tender and delicious! We had a little room for dessert so we ordered the cheesecake with the trio of jams. Delicious cheesecake (although I saw them microwave it quickly before serving which had worried me) and the jams were delicious but not necessarily the best I've had. The jams were an orange peel & honey, raspberry, and peach. The orange jam was slightly bitter on its own, but with the cheesecake it was more balanced. The raspberry was good and the peach was the hubby's favorite but I thought it tasted a little too sweet. Overall, we spent just a little under 50€ for the two of us and left stuffed so I thought it was reasonable but not the "cheapest" meal we've had (and we visited other restaurants that were amazing). I'd say definitely worth going and if you are looking to spend less, order a few tapas before visiting somewhere else for more food!
