review_full: My partner and I recently ate here, saving it for our last dinner in Madrid. We were seated quickly without a reservation at around 9:40pm on a weeknight. We ordered the variety of meats to share along with a side of garlic and parsley chips/fries.  When we were sat down we were brought bread and olives. There was a garlic butter too which was very tasty. The bread is not free which might have been naive of me to think so but worth the about €3.50 I believe it cost. The variety of meats were the perfect size to share and delicious. We were brought out the wrong side, a plate of vegetables and the waitress, Laury, who brought them seemed to get annoyed with us when I brought it to her attention that the wrong side had been brought. I understand I’m working with high school level Spanish and that a language barrier can be frustrating, but I was able to say that we had ordered fries in Spanish. I found the huffing and attitude of the waitress while I tried my best to remember certain words to be off putting and it made us not order dessert like we had planned to. Anyway, we were then brought out normal fries. A bit of confusion with the language barrier with Laury and another member of staff but finally the garlic and parsley chips made their way to the table. These chips are the only part of the food that I can fault. They were soggy and honestly seemed like they had been microwaved.  When the bill arrived (after asking for it multiple times), it was wrong. We had been charged for sides that had been brought out in the error of the restaurant. We were given some after dinner liquor as a result of the wait, much appreciated! Also, thank you to Sebastian who helped to sort the errors on the bill out!  We had ordered wine as well with our meal and were finishing it after the meal. The waitress came by our table picking things up in a rush and putting her arms in between the view of my partner and I. I understand that cleaning and picking up has to be done, but I’ve also eaten in enough restaurants to know there’s a more professional manner in which to do so. The food is good here and I try to not let one bad apple ruin it all but it can be hard to enjoy the food when the atmosphere is wrong.

Others have tried the bife de chorizo, and the skirt steak, and started thanking god. Usually the bife is my usual favorite (and was great!), but the skirt steak was out of this world!! It was just right, delicious,a and huge (and I'm a guy who had many of those in Brazilian churrascarias :)). The salad of the house, fries, stir fried veggies, all winners. The young ladies who service the restaurant, are kind and professional. The decor and ambiance just make you feel like the worries of the world are peeled off of you. Very recommended for all meat lovers, and pescetarians too (there is a cod on the menu, but we haven't tried it)

title_review: Quite simply the best. Steak. Ever!
review_preview: Having spent an amazing 2 nights eating tapas till we dropped, we decided to have a more formal meal and selected this restaurant from Trip Advisor. We turned up by chance at about 9pm and were fortunate to get a table. Apparently the evening before...
review_full: Having spent an amazing 2 nights eating tapas till we dropped, we decided to have a more formal meal and selected this restaurant from Trip Advisor. We turned up by chance at about 9pm and were fortunate to get a table. Apparently the evening before (Tues) was mobbed with scores of people turned away.  And it was fantastic. We had peppers and blood sausage to start along with some Roquefort butter and warm bread. Very nice but the steaks were definitely the star of the show. We both had ribeye steaks- one 500g and one 300g both cooked medium rare and they were a stunning. Perfectly cooked throughout with a well seasoned crust on the outside. We savoured every mouthful. Do yourself a favour and make sure this restaurant is on your list!

review_preview: We decided to visit last minute on a Saturday night and asked our hotel to book us a table. We were told they were full but that they would write our name on the reserve list. We turned up at 9pm as had been discussed...
review_full: We decided to visit last minute on a Saturday night and asked our hotel to book us a table. We were told they were full but that they would write our name on the reserve list. We turned up at 9pm as had been discussed on the phone and had a drink at the bar. It was extremely busy but luckily we got a seat at the bar area so it wasn’t too bad.  The frustrating thing for us was after an hour or so of waiting some couples that had definitely not booked got seated before us. The member of staff who was front of house clearly knew these couples after kissing and hugging them and made sure they got seated ahead of other people. More and more people started arriving and started complaining to the staff so it wasn’t just us.  The front of house guy was no where to be seen at times because he was too busy chatting away with his friends who he had sorted tables out for so the waiters were left dealing with the complaints. This was very poor from him and very unprofessional.  When we did finally get seated at 10.30pm we decided not to have a starter and just to have mains. We both went for the fillet steaks. I have to say that this was one of the best steaks I have ever had. I asked for it be medium and it was actually rare but as the steak was so good I didn’t mind too much. My partner asked for medium well and it was cooked perfectly.  I must also mention Sebastian who worked behind the bar who was English and dealt with any English speaking customers and took the phone calls if they were English. He was very polite, friendly and professional.

title_review: What a find off the beaten track but close enough to the bus route
review_preview: We stumbled across this place as we stepped off the tour bus route.  We wanted to get off just before the Grand Palace to avoid the crowds in the hope of finding somewhere more traditional - so glad we did.  As we stepped off the...
review_full: We stumbled across this place as we stepped off the tour bus route. We wanted to get off just before the Grand Palace to avoid the crowds in the hope of finding somewhere more traditional - so glad we did. As we stepped off the bus tour I turned to my reliable trip advisor app in terms of where was nearby and here we landed. It is off a wee back street so as you are walking down you are not too sure what to expect. When we walked in we were greeted by a very warm host who offered us a table and swiftly a menu and drinks. The menu was so varied we wanted to try quite a few things - they split it into things from the sea, garden and land which was a nice way to know what you were eating and how to split your choices. We got a variety of dishes and shared them - the highlights being stuffed potatoes with mushrooms and apricot, sea bass ceviche and the rigatoni pasta which was also amazing. For some of the dishes they have the option of tapas, 1/2 portion and full portion which was helpful when you may want a bit more of some dishes. The staff were very helpful in telling us what would be a right amount for us and recommending their local specialities. Would definately recommend this place for traditional tapas to anyone visiting madrid.

review_preview: We came across this restaurant on trip advisor and thought we’d give it a go based on the great reviews, and It certainly did not disappoint! This was hands down the best restaurant we have eaten on our trip to Spain. The flavours in all...
review_full: We came across this restaurant on trip advisor and thought we’d give it a go based on the great reviews, and It certainly did not disappoint! This was hands down the best restaurant we have eaten on our trip to Spain. The flavours in all the dishes we ordered were delicious. Stand out meals were the chicken taco, the tempura vegetables and the cheese filled tomato- to die for. We couldn’t skip dessert as it looked too good to be true - and it certainly was. The chocolate fondant with violet ice cream was like no other! The cheesecake with assorted jams is perfect for any sweet tooth. All staff went above and beyond for us, especially Alfonzo who offered many suggestions and even gave us a free shot on the house. Thank you for a fabulous dining experience and we look forward to returning in the future.

You will enjoy whatever you eat there. You will find classics with a modern interpretation (but keeping the soul of the classics). They serve “Metro Potatoes” with three traditional sauces; each of them is legendary, you should taste them. Croquettes, Cured veal meat, Braised butterfish were all perfect. Service is welcoming and friendly. Prices are really reasonable.

title_review: I didn’t think it could get better, but it did
review_preview: My husband and I have been in España for 5 weeks and we have eaten very very well each night, thanks to the guidance of TA. This was night #6 in Madrid so we’ve tried a few restaurants here and all over the country. With...
review_full: My husband and I have been in España for 5 weeks and we have eaten very very well each night, thanks to the guidance of TA.  This was night #6 in Madrid so we’ve tried a few restaurants here and all over the country. With just one night to go, Metro Bistro Plaza Mayor has to be número uno. And I didn’t think it could get this good.  We arrived back in Madrid a bit late and asked the hotel to book the other Metro Bistro as we had been there before and wanted to go again. It isn’t open on Sunday so we walked to Plaza Mayor to try this one.  At about 9:30pm the restaurant was able to fit us in for dinner - a plus for us - and so it was to be a great experience.  It is my husband’s job to choose the wine and me, the food. He chose a Martin Berlugo Tempranillo - a good choice. I chose the flaming prawns with mushrooms and the slow cooked egg with mushrooms to start - both were magnificent.  We weren’t particularly starving hungry so for main we shared the black rice with scallops and a salad with figs and cheese for main. Those were the best scallops I’ve ever had and the yellow curry sauce with the rice was enhanced by the red wine like you couldn’t imagine.  No room for dessert.  Very good value at EUR78, including refreshing agua con gas for 2.

review_preview: On a recent tour of Spain with a major tour company we enjoyed the company of two other couples and descended on the Metro Bistro.  You can skip Botin and go to the Metro.  The food was exquisite and the staff was very solicitous.  We...
review_full: On a recent tour of Spain with a major tour company we enjoyed the company of two other couples and descended on the Metro Bistro. You can skip Botin and go to the Metro. The food was exquisite and the staff was very solicitous.  We each had the 7 course tasting menu. The staff was very attentive to one of our groups dietary needs and they slightly amended the courses. Each couple ordered a bottle of wine. The meal was not rushed and at each course the chef (Matias Smith) came out to let us know what we were eating and ensure we well taken care of.  Highlights included a cold tomato garlic soup, scallops on black rice and roast pork. All dishes were wonderful. It was great to finish the meal off with a 4 chocolate dessert.  I HIGHLY recommend a visit to this restaurant. Everyone in our group agreed it was the best meal of our trip. The 7 course tasting menu was 38 Euros each. It did not include the wine.

review_full: Came here after not being able to get into another restaurant, overheard the waitress suggesting this place to other parties in Spanish so we thought we'd give it a try.  We are seated easily around 8:45pm on a Saturday. Ordered two entrees, dessert and a cheese plate to share. The flavors here are really interesting, nothing is "plain" but also nothing is special without being delicious also. Even the butter that comes with the bread is flavored (we had one sage and one olive). Or entrees were the fish and the scallops, both of which had some hint of eastern flavor. Scallops were my favorite. The service was so lovely - so friendly and welcoming. They were giving tables samples of a cucumber drink they made. Our table ordered one. After we paid our check there were also extra sweets and another round of drinks on the house. Would definitely recommend for someone dining late in the Plaza Mayor area. Really great value for very good good in a touristy area.

review_full: If you want the equivalent of a fine dinning meal without the fuss and price in a really friendly relaxed atmosphere then definitely try Taberna Origen. Oh David thank you so much. The white asparagus was to die for! We also had finely sliced rare Ox and pigs trotter. All the food was sooo good and the wine excellent. All the staff were really friendly, personable and fun. They made us feel just a little bit special. However, what was special is Taberna Origen. We have now left Madrid to continue our journey but how I miss you Origen. We ate in the small front bar section but there was also a restaurant in the back area which I noticed took bookings. We met the chef and I wanted to genuflect!

review_full: Originally planned on having a quiet dinner for our final night in Madrid, so we decided to head to a Portuguese restaurant on Calle Mendizábal, but it was closed for the summer. Luckily, I remembered seeing rave reviews about Origen (which was on the same street), so we ate there instead, and what a blessing it was. Ordered everything David, one of the wonderful servers there, recommended, and everything was superb. The ceviche, beef gyoza, and beef tartare(?) were notable, but the stars of the show were the huge sardines on toast and the cuttlefish burgers. But beyond that, there wasn't much else this restaurant can be complimented on. Of the four mains we tried, the fish was very plain, the Spanish sweet and sour pork ok but nothing fantastic (but probably the best out of the four we tried), the volcano rice good, but have had much better and oh, the chicken? It wasn't cooked through. When we told the waiter, he said that it was ok to eat (though I will add he was very nice). Not sure about Spain, but where we're from, chicken isn't like steak, where rare or medium rare is ok; chicken should be cooked through. Anyway, the manager was called over, looked over and apathetically asked if we'd like the chicken to be cooked more. There was no apology, no nothing, and when it came back, it was so salty and overcooked, it would've been better to eat wood. You could not pay me enough to dine here again.

review_full: Taberna Origen has a great variety of dishes. The menu has been designed for sharing, more than the typical option of a starter and a second dish by person. It´s hard to define which are the starters and which ones are the main dishes, all options seem palatable. Also, each dish can be ordered in different portion´s size, which I consider an excellent idea that allow you to choose according the number of persons you are sharing. The restaurant is small but cozy, with high chairs and tables, which gives an informal look according to the kind of food they serve, but never forgetting the quality and quantity. The waitress was very helpful and nice, her recommendations were delicious and she indicated us the best size of the portion for three persons. The most surprising dishes for us were the poached tomatoes filled with Idiazabal´s cheese and the mini squid burgers, exotic mixture, but tasty. Also, the croquettes made with carabineros were soft inside and crunchy outside. Regarding the desserts they were correct, but we hoped more from them, due to quality and exotic of the other dishes. Without hesitating I would try to visit again Taberna Origen searching for a nice dinner full of small and yummy recipes. Furthermore, the price of the food is very reasonable attending the quality and quantity.

review_full: Lovely restaurant, modern décor & very welcome air conditioning. The staff were very helpful and recommended an excellent red wine - Martin Erdugo I think. We were not hungry enough for the tasting menu but it looked great. Nice amuse bouche and very good breads & butters served. We shared the foie starter which was great but were not fans of the very sweet guava it came with. However the suckling pig and the sweet & sour iberico pork (served pink) were both delicious. My only complaint is that the service became really slow as the place filled up, I would have loved to try the pineapple cannelloni for dessert but got bored waiting! Over all very good, good value for money, especially considering the quality and the location. Also it opens quite early in the evening which is great for us Brits adjusting to Spanish late eating times.

review_preview: This place is located less than five minutes from Plaza Mayor, but it's a lot better than anything you can find there. The dishes are very unique. As seafood lovers, my dad and I both got the shrimp on fire as a starter, and it...
review_full: This place is located less than five minutes from Plaza Mayor, but it's a lot better than anything you can find there. The dishes are very unique. As seafood lovers, my dad and I both got the shrimp on fire as a starter, and it did not disappoint. The fire was cool, but we care about food quality, and the dish excelled there as well. The garlic flavor was strong but not overpowering, and there was a good balance of shrimp and mushrooms. It was a good start, but it got even better with the introduction of the elusive butterfish, which we hadn't been able to find for three years. It is, quite simply, one of the most succulent fish in existence, and the addition of citrus-flavored ponzu sauce somehow made it even better. This was simply the best meal we had in Spain, and every dish we had in the country was exceptional. The butterfish was that good. The price was reasonable as well, and a delicious dessert, "Tribute to Chocolate," didn't hurt either. Bottom Line: if you like seafood, this place is worth it for the butterfish alone.

The scene is casual and friendly and indeed many customers are locals of a range of ages. The interior is small, warm, a little hip and charming. They have a nice selection of beers including craft Spanish beers (wine too. but I didn't pay attention to it) and the food is great. I had mussels, sardine on toast, ensaladilla, Oreja (grilled confit of pig ear - hey, you're in Spain, live a little) and Torrenzo (fried confit of pork belly). It was all great - food that is regional and prepared with skill and creativity. The mussels, Oreja and Torrenzo were exceptional. The price is very reasonable - about 30 euros and I was stuffed. A real gem.

title_review: Fantastic steak – a great taste of Argentina in Spain
review_preview: We had one of our best meals in Madrid on our first night here. Our concierge recommended La Cabana Argentina when we asked for a restaurant within walking distance (and told him that, after being in Spain for three weeks, we were tired of jamon);...
review_full: We had one of our best meals in Madrid on our first night here. Our concierge recommended La Cabana Argentina when we asked for a restaurant within walking distance (and told him that, after being in Spain for three weeks, we were tired of jamon); it is located on a charming, narrow street with several other restaurants. Golden light shines on the street through the big plate glass windows that display various cuts of steak, and the atmosphere is inviting: white-washed exposed brick featuring mirrors and old photos, charcoal grey leather banquets lining the walls, dangling lights, crisp white tablecloths. The service was excellent. Shortly after being seated, we were served bread and three kinds of olives. And the servers were attentive throughout the evening – moving efficiently through the very busy restaurant – but not cloying. And, the most important thing: the steaks were fantastic. A father and son own and operate the place, which has been around for more than 20 years, and import vacuum-packed Argentine loins and cuts twice a week. The quality is evident. We both ordered rib eyes and they were cooked a perfect medium rare and were tender and buttery. We share a massive salad with Roquefort cheese, walnuts, apples, tomatoes and a platter of golden, crispy fries. The wine list has a large selection of Argentinian Malbecs and Spanish reds, as well as a smaller but thoughtfully curated selection of other reds, blends, whites, sparkling (cava!) and dessert wines. Even though we were extremely full, we shared the dulce de leche ice cream – three large scoops of rich, creamy, caramel delight. We were very content as we walked back to our hotel – only wishing it was a bit further away so we could expend a few more of the many calories we had just joyously imbibed.

You can imagine how busy it is on a Saturday night, and yet we didn't feel ignored. I also didn't feel any issue with our lack of Spanish skills, they were so accommodating.  We finished the evening with the chocolate dessert with berries. It was a perfect end to our Spanish adventure. Do check these guys out as they are the real deal.

Opens right at 8pm and only holds 25-30 people so fills quickly. The service was quick and friendly and they have an English menu if needed. Their food is spectacular and features a mix of solid Spanish classics and new twists. The mussels in kimchi broth were divine so save some bread to use to sop the broth us with. I have no idea how they prepared the artichokes- entire small artichokes splayed out and cooked with jamon and such, just great. Also had the patatas bravas which were fried crisp and the sauce was just spicy enough. The chocolate ganache desert was very nice-a bit different but great! Overall, everything was well above our expectations and was the perfect finish to a trip to Madrid.

Started off with some bread and a little mix they had which was herbs, garlic and Oliver oil mixed together, on the bread it was awesome. Then into the plate of ham to share as a starter. Comes with plenty of ham (2 shared) and some toasted bread, again with the garlic it was lovely.  For mains we both ordered the rib eye (Angus) steak and it was perfect in every way. I love my steak houses and this again as in Romania is up with the very best. Served with a pepper sauce, fried with garlic and roasted red peppers it was such a lovely taste. Steak melted in your mouth, well worth the wait.  Cost:- well for all good, plenty of drinks it came to just €120 which I may add was a snip considering how lovely it was. Service:- very good, staff always keen to make sure you had everything and were very polite. Overall:- a lovely night for either couples or families with children too. Try it, I assure you will not be disappointed. Any questions, just ask ! Thank you

review_full: I walked by this place and glance at the menu after visiting the museum. I was looking for a spot with lighter fare options for a very late lunch and a few dishes on their menu caught my eye. So I decided to step in. First off, the staff here is wonderful. I was traveling solo (mid 40s female who only speaks about 20-30 words of Spanish), and from the beginning, despite my lack of Spanish language skills, everyone who works at this restaurant was very friendly and welcoming, and I did not feel at all awkward dining on my own or made to feel that I was holding up a table for a larger party. And judging by other people dining there, they serve a fairly diverse crowd. Service and hospitality was impeccable, efficient (without being overdone), and warm. Shout out to all of the friendly wait staff, and especially to Emilio, who offered a cinnamon-rice milk liquor to top off my salmon and avocado salad (which was also perfect). I also really liked the decor--it's warm, rustic, and very inviting. If you are looking for a change from regular tapas restaurants in the area (i.e. you are visiting the Reina Sofia or Prado Museum), I highly recommend this place. I would definitely go back again if I'm in the area and try some of their other dishes.

review_full: This trendy restaurant sits in a small side street by the Plaza Mayor in Madrid. We had made a reservation for 8pm but showed up at 720pm. The waiter/host Ibrahim was very kind to accommodate us near the bar in a table for two. He was quick to offer us a courtesy taste of the pineapple daiquiri, the wine list and menu. Two other couples were sitting nearby. He took our order (and those of our neighbors) and shortly thereafter started parading our feast. We had the house red wine which was adequate, followed by an appetizer of croquettes which were recommended by Ibrahim. The corquettes were indeed fantastic. We also had the escalibada vegetables, but the eggplant was a bit too tough and it needed some sherry vinegar to enhance the flavor. That was the only part of our meal which was not excellent. We had the steak tartare and the braised lamb and both were amazing. To top things off, the chocolate extravaganza dessert was world class. Nothing however beats the service and attitude displayed by Ibrahim. This is a good place with a well deserved reputation. At one point a large group showed up without reservations and the staff seemed to bend over backwards to accommodate them, rather than playing snob and making it hard for the guests. That is classy! The price for our meal was reasonable and that is appreciated.

title_review: A small gem near Madrid Airport
review_preview: It wasn’t really a surprise given the reviews but after my wife and I found this little gem we left with smiles on our faces. Our host was gracious and helpful in explaining the small but perfectly focused menu. The food was like watching an...
review_full: It wasn’t really a surprise given the reviews but after my wife and I found this little gem we left with smiles on our faces. Our host was gracious and helpful in explaining the small but perfectly focused menu. The food was like watching an excellent fireworks display with each dish exploding with new flavors and textures. This was easily one of the best meals we had during our two weeks in Spain. Highlights: Tomato Alinado: carpaccio like slices, in a lovely savory vinaigrette, with strategically employed salt crystals and topped with dollops of a berry cream emulsion. We used up most of our bread sopping up the marinade. Incredible!  Flores de Alcachofa: perfect flowers of artichoke, seasoned perfectly and topped with quail eggs and pancetta. Just fantastic.  Calimari: fried in a light batter and seasoned with just a touch of vinaigrette and hair thin strands of Chile pepper, Cilantro and Cucumber.  Oreja El callejon: perfectly cooked pork belly with an amazing crackling crust. Sinfully luscious! Purple salt added just the right punch.  We also enjoyed an amuse of patatas bravas which were spicy and incredible.  Our host was very helpful with selection from their small but well curated wine list.  All in all we cannot recommend this Taberna highly enough. We wish them success in the future. If you are flying through or just in Madrid for business / holiday.. this Taberna is well worth seeking out. Given their popularity I would recommend making reservations. We got lucky at 2:15. By 3pm the place was full.

It is small but quaint. In summary, we just got back from eating at this Taberna and we are totally satisfied with this place. First of all, the Bartender/Server Alex made the experience what it was. He speaks very good English. He took the time to explain each item on the menu then made some excellent recommendations. Every single tapa we ate was excellent, beyond our expectations. We had muscles cooked in a wok and served in a delicious broth. My wife is not a muscle eater. But she tried these and has become a convert. Artichokes that were grilled and topped with a quail egg were again excellent. The croquettes de bacalaou (cod fish) were delicate and creamy. I would not hesitate choosing this Taberna again.

review_full: We went here for a late dinner. Other restaurants ranked higher in the area were packed and needed reservations. Metro Bistro had space and were very welcoming. It is not your traditional tapas/spanish restaurant you find in La Latina or near Plaza Mayor. It had traditional ingredients but reminded my wife and I of a smaller fine dining restaurant you would find in North America.  The servers spoke english fairly well and were very attentive and courteous. The music they played was also very trendy as my wife had to ask who the artist they were playing was. Order the assorted cheese, platter to start. The cheese selection is fantastic and goes well with the assorted fruit and house bread.  We also ordered the treasures of the sea. Which were deep fried escargot or muscles with seaweed salad. That was also very good, but not as good as the cheese. For entree's we ordered the steak tartare and the scallop risotto. Both were very well presented and the taste was excellent. The portions were not too large as we were able to finish them after our appetizers and not be completely stuffed. For dessert we had the pineapple cannelloni and the dulce de leche cheesecake. My wife was in love with the pineapple dish and almost ordered a second. The cheesecake was also very good. I could not finish it on the count of the large amount of dulce de leche on top of the cake. The flavour was amazing, just a lot of caramel to eat.

Taking into consideration that it is an Italian cuisine, I would say it is the best value for money.  On the other hand, If I had to say something to be improved would be the space between tables, unfortunately it is being something as usual as uncomfortable. Holding more capacity not always imply more revenues. Anyway, Oven is highly recommended.

However, for the restaurant to rank #38 in Madrid gives the city a bad name. I could name 50 restaurants off the top of my head that are 100% better than this dump. The pumpkin cream soup was cold, the croquettes were cold and flavorless, the salad had no substantial greens or vegetables, the cheese pots consisted of two okay cheeses and 4 inedible ones. DO NOT BE FOOLED BY LOCATION!!!! THIS IS NOT GOOD SPANISH FOOD OR GOOD FOOD IN MADRID PERIOD! I will be contacting someone on trip advisor to ask how they can stand for such a terrible restaurant being in the top 100 restaurant in Madrid. This is an anomaly to trip advisor! We went to Takos Al Pastor right next to it after for $1 tacos and quesadillas and that meal was one of the better I have had in Madrid. Metro bistro is garbage. Do not give your business your money. Much better restaurants should be in that location.

review_full: After having a late "spanish style" lunch here a couple of days ago, we decided to go back on our last night in Madrid and try the 38 € tasting menu. We were so happy--everything was delicious, the portions were large for a tasting menu, and the bill was less than 100 € for 2 with a bottle of very good local wine that our waiter recommended (17 €!!!). The service was excellent. The waiters explained all the dishes in English, were efficient, but did not rush us. Metro Bistro is as good as some of the Michelin starred restaurants where I have dined.

title_review: Great food at a great price. A must.
review_preview: You have to try the 7 course tasting menu, which actually works out about 9 course with some little extras. Each course was amazing, interesting and very tasty. And at 38 EUR each its superb value. Service too was impeccable. Overall with wine and some...
review_full: You have to try the 7 course tasting menu, which actually works out about 9 course with some little extras. Each course was amazing, interesting and very tasty. And at 38 EUR each its superb value. Service too was impeccable. Overall with wine and some fizz it was 108 EUR for my wife and I. The only gripe I really have is the fact Metro Bistro offers fine dining but is still a bit of a bar type vibe - I had music from the entrance in one ear and nothing in the other, I think some cool chill out music played throughout would add to the experience. Also there was a group of lads on a stag do a few tables away and although they were fine (if not a little rowdy) it would have been a better experience if it was couples or maybe no more than groups of 5.  With these above areas of improvement I would have given it 5 stars, great service, superb food. A must for any visitor to Madrid.

review_full: Our group of 6 enjoyed a taste of Argentina at dinner at this venue. This restaurant has been established for some 20 years but was refurbished two years ago to great effect. The internal part rustic brickwork contrasts with smooth marble sections of the walls and gives a warm and comfortable feel. There is a relatively large seating capacity and it quickly filled with a mixture of groups and couples. The service, with some Argentinian personnel, was of a high standard. Paula's advice on the wine list was appreciated. Both the menu and wine list are comprehensive and easy to read. Of course the steak listing in the Menu is large with related meat sizes to show the extent of the meal. We were served olives, dip and bread to start. We did not require starters and went to the main courses which were either the beef tenderloin (300gram) or the rib eye steak.  The quality of the meats were excellent, and whilst nearly all of our party asked for the cooking to be "medium" the steaks were served more what we would class as "rare" in Australia. We were forewarned by Paula that the steaks would be cooked to a "pink" colour.  However all enjoyed the steaks very much and the accompanying sautéed vegetables, shared between two, were of good variety and servings. For our wines we chose an Argentinian Chardonnay and Malbec, both of which were reasonably priced and well suited our tastes. Overall a very enjoyable and memorable experience. A Booking is certainly recommended.

review_full: First of all, if you plan to eat here, you should definitely have a reservation. Otherwise it is almost impossible to find a seat. Like all restaurants in Spain, they are almost fully booked between 20:00-23:00, so either you have to visit earlier or book a table in advance. We have been to La Cabana to try steak and we did not regret it. We have been there around 19:00 without any reservation. They were fully booked for 20:00 afterwards and gave us a table on condition that we would leave latest at 20:30 which was ok for us since we had another plan later at night.  The staff was kind and friendly. But unfortunately not all of them could speak English. A waitress took our orders for drink and salad. When we asked a few things about the salad, an English speaking waitress had to come over to answer but it was ok. After our order was taken, a service plate with olive, a very good olive oil and some other oily spicy sauce was served to us. While we were trying the olive oil, a waiter came by and took our orders. We have tried two different steaks, one of which was recommended by the waiter and wanted half portion grilled vegetables. Though they were quite slow in serving and it took about half an hour for our dishes to be served, the steaks were really good. Surprisingly, the salad was above our expectations as well. Thus, we spent around 1.5 hours there enjoying our food and left the restaurant with smiling faces.

review_preview: It snowed in Madrid today, we were out walking and cold.  This place showed up on TA and we made our way to it.I don't know if it was just that we were cold and hungry, but we were, literally, blown away by our...
review_full: It snowed in Madrid today, we were out walking and cold. This place showed up on TA and we made our way to it. I don't know if it was just that we were cold and hungry, but we were, literally, blown away by our experience here. We were welcomed gracefully and warmly. Staff is unpretentious, kindly and efficient without being overweening. The food was excellent, from the bread box and butter cover, to the Cecina starter (which we shared), to my Perla Negra and My wife's Hamburguesa de Ternera, we just sat, ate and marvelled at the quality and the tastes.  The Cecina is thinly sliced cured veal with cream cheese and tomato. A fine blend of different flavours that lingered on the palate. And, there was lots for both of us.  My Perla was three scallops on a 'boat' of black rice in a shallow 'sea' of a curry sauce that was really quite indescribably good. I ate it all, savouring each bite and hoping it would go on and on.  My wife's hamburguesa was like no hamburger we have ever experienced. I have to admit that when I saw it on the menu, I began to have second thoughts about the kind of place we had come to. But, really, this is nothing like any other version of a hamburger we have ever seen. The meat perfectly seasoned, done just right. No bread, just finely shaped, amazingly crisp and tasty sliced of Yucca. (I know, who would ever have thought!) All put together beautifully artistically and very appealing. We had glasses of the house red together to start and I had a glass of house white and, really, if I had picked the most expensive bottles in the house, I could not have picked better myself. The décor is clean, elegant and comfortable and matches the food. What I cannot believe is that (apart from a group of six Spaniards who came in to share wine and olives while we were there), we were the only people in the place. At 13:45, I don't think we were unfashionably early for lunch. Perhaps it had more to do with this being a Thursday on an exceptionally cold - and snowing - day when few tourists or Madrilenos were venturing out when they did not absolutely have to do so. I try not to give out five stars unless a place is really exceptional in our experience. There is just too much review inflation andhyperbole out there what with all the 'Amazing's, 'Awesome's and 'Fantastic's one sees over and over again. Let me just say this place is excellent and to be highly recommended. You are unlikely to go wrong. On food, on wine, or on the cost of your meal.

review_full: Metro Bistro is located behind Plaza Mayor - almost hidden amongst other shops and restaurants vying for attention. Once inside, however, you are in the world of fine dining and delightful food prepared with due care. The service was attentive and enthusiastic. Everyone working in Metro Bistro really cares about ensuring you have a great dining experience and about presenting beautiful food. The experience of having many small courses over the evening is exquisite. The food is quite a picture of presentation and the taste is amazing as the flavours and colours and, yes, even the textures are thoughtfully and artfully combined. The black rice and squid is a firm favourite. However the chocolate plate is a triumph of mastery over the craft - too beautiful for words! - although we didn't take long to start to eat our way though the different gorgeous chocolate concoctions. Chef Matias Smith spends time with patrons during the course of the evening and is so keen to ensure that everyone is enjoying their food - a wonderful touch.

review_full: I title my review that way because this type of restaurants is not my first choice when I travel as I prefer in new place to get to know the local basic food. In that case, one of my colleagues who travel with me knew that chef and owner through a friend of his. The food in Metro Bistro is very creative and beautifully presented. I had for main course a hamburger which was actually 2 patties made of veal and bacon on bed of sweet little onions, camembert cheese and yucca. Across from me one of my companions had the steak tartare which was also very nicely presented. For desert, we shared the "TRIBUTE TO CHOCOLATE": Truffles “Bombón”, half cold with Sansho-Ko pepper, ganache Peta Z and cocoa mousse (copied from the restaurant website). The desert was good enough reason to go the Metro Bistro!!! The food was very good and the service was also excellent as expected and as noted in other reviews. I was also surprise to see the prices were also very reasonable. Overall, I highly recommend.  One word about our acquaintance with the chef/owner, that particular evening he wasn't there so I don't think that we got any special treatment because of that.

The burgers, I am told, were amongst the best they have had. The little pot of peppers which came with the steak are worth mentioning - they went really well with the meat and were something I hadn't had before with steak. So all in all we were very happy. As for the restaurant itself, a lovely atmosphere, not too big and not too small, very friendly staff and a house red which was delicious! I think if we were here longer we may well have gone back to Steakburger Atocha.

It is a bit more expensive than many restaurants in the City (300g steak was just over 19 euros without any accompanying dishes which had to be bought over and above) but it was well worth it from our point of view; the welcome, the service, the restaurant itself, and the food were of a standard I would expect when paying that bit more.  I definitely recommend this restaurant for an evening meal. I would advise booking; we got lucky turning up out of the blue I think, as it seems to be a relatively busy restaurant - which also tells you all you need to know about the quality of the food being served; if it wasn't good, no one would go there! Enjoy!

review_preview: We had a late dinner at Steakburger Atocha in June 2019. review_full: We had a late dinner at Steakburger Atocha in June 2019. The food that we got was tasty and plentiful, and the staff were friendly, but multiple logistical problems with the service made the experience somewhat disappointing. A high noise level (from other diners’ conversations, not music) also contributed negatively. To begin with, the server (who spoke fluent English) said he could provide tap water with ice, but then brought bottled water at 2 Euros each. Not a big deal, since most restaurants in Madrid will not serve tap water anyway, but we should have been given accurate information. For food, we ordered a goat cheese salad, a red mountain burger, a melting cheese burger, and the marinated grilled chicken. The melting cheese burger never arrived. The serving of grilled chicken was so large, however, that by the time we realized the melting cheese burger wasn’t just delayed but omitted, it was clear we had enough food without it. When we pointed out the omission to the server, he apologized, removed the missing burger from the bill, and also brought us a complimentary dessert (a large, oven-fresh cookie with ice cream).  We get that in Europe, diners tend to linger in restaurants, and one has to ask explicitly for the check, but in this case we had to ask three times for the check, with long time intervals between requests. Again, not a big deal, but it reinforced our impression that we weren’t a very high priority table. The restrooms were clean, but down a long flight of stairs and therefore inaccessible to those in wheelchairs or otherwise unable to manage the stairs. The temperature in the dining room was pleasantly cool on a rather warm evening.

review_full: We decided on this restaurant for a quick lunch in the city during a long layover in Barajas. The service was top-notch. Both were very tasty, although the tartare was far more conceptual and creative with its use of non-traditional ingredients such as foie-gras and caviar. We both had the creamy cheesecake for dessert, and it did not disappoint. All in all, it was an upscale experience that is recommended to anyone who enjoys creative and service-oriented dining.

After dinner, came a glass of sparkling white wine, and many candies (Turron and mazapan)! You should see every guest's face, everyone's beaming with joy! The service's great, love the hostess and the waiter.  By the way, we thought that it were hard to find a dinner place at Christmas Eve in Madrid, so we booked this place ahead of time, however, there were many restaurants opening in downtown.

review_full: We ate here on a wet Sunday evening and were the first diners at 7.30 pm. The restaurant is modernistic and chic and initial thoughts were 'oh no, not another pretentious eaterie'. However, having ordered the risotto (comprising Chinese black rice and scallops) and the veal and bacon burger, we were delighted with the meals delivered. Yes, the portions are very small and delicate and decoratively presented, but were extremely tasty, and with the fabulous variety of breads to accompany the meals, were sufficient to feed a hungry tourist. Desserts were delightful and sheer works of art - should have been at the Prado! So - not the place if you are looking for fast food and are starving, but if you have finer tastes, give them a try. you won't be disappointed.

review_preview: This was a rare find in the land of Iberian ham. One of our group walked past this restaurant during the day and said we should try it, not knowing how good it was going to be. A group of 6 arrived at 7.30pm with...
review_full: This was a rare find in the land of Iberian ham. One of our group walked past this restaurant during the day and said we should try it, not knowing how good it was going to be. A group of 6 arrived at 7.30pm with no reservation, I think we were the first diners there, but no problem, Paula our hostess arranged a setting for us. The restaurant at night, looking down the small lane did not stand out , but on arrival looking at the meat display in the window and the welcoming interior, one knew this was a restaurant operated by people that knew what it was about. This Argentinian Steak House had been operating for about 22 years and had been recently renovated to have an historical/modern theme which was very appealing and comfortable. All the right ingredients, Angus certified beef cuts, Argentinian Chardonnay and Malbec wines as will as Spanish offerings. The steaks were char grilled to European standards and very well too, but if you don't like really blue steaks then adjust your request from say medium rare to medium. Our group had rib eye steaks and tenderloins based on size of 300 grams and we added some share plates of sautéed vegetables which were fresh and delicious. Most had a dessert or cheese plate to finish and while we were waiting for our meals we had some bread, olive oil and olives. 3 bottles of wine, 3 beers, the meals and tip came to €270 - €90 a couple. I felt this was reasonable value given the service provided, the meal provided and the ambience of the restaurant. I would recommend this restaurant if you like a good steak but be sure to make a reservation so you are not disappointed.

review_full: Dined here a couple of nights ago and was really impressed with the quality of food as well as the top notch service, without forgetting the vast array of wine on offer on the wine list. The food on offer was exceptional. For starters we opted to share the cheese platter, the cured veal, the croquettes (filled with Mushrooms and Ham) and the sea treasures which consisted of deep fried anemones with deep fried seaweed and a seaweed tartar. The latter was the pick of the lot - although all the dishes were good. However the contrast of the hot and crunchy anemones with the cold seaweed was just too good. For mains I had the Steak Tartar which was out of this world. It came dressed with truffle, egg, foie-gras and vegetables - with the truffle being the pick of the lot. One of my colleagues also took this whilst another took the burger which does not come served in a bun however the taste of the meat is unlike any burger I have tasted before (yes - I did manage to steal a bite!) Service on the night was exceptional and I hope to return next time I will be in Madrid.

review_full: Being a foodie with a long history of gastronomique meals in France, where I live, and around the globe, this was my best meal experience in 5 days in Madrid. I was counting on Bodega de Los Secretos (which I booked in advance to celebrate my mother's birthday) for the special meal (see my review) but Metro Bistro totally exceeded my expectations. The name doesn't give it justice - it is basically a gourmet restaurant (both in the sense of inventive cuisine and top notch service) at a ridiculously cheap price (for this level of cuisine). We had a 7 course tasting menu for 38 euros. We were the first people in the restaurant as we came at 7PM - we didn't have lunch and wanted to eat early; so we got so much attention from the staff we felt like at the Ritz. The presentation, the attention to detail, the great, yet unexpected combinations of ingredients (anemones with seaweed tartar and lemongrass took time to identify)... It all started with complimentary tiny celery mojitos and then one course gave way to the next one and next one. When we thought we couldn't possible eat anything else, the dessert arrived: pineapple cannelloni with mango source. The chocolate selection that accompanied coffee after that was definitely over the top. If you come here for that tasting menu, make sure you don't eat for few days before. The staff was wonderful, friendly and very professional: they explained every course in details, offered great wine suggestions and even packed the little chocolates for us to take away.  Just off Plaza Major, this fantastic restaurant is not to be missed. I can't wait to be back!

review_preview: It was our first evening in Madrid and we were tired so we wanted to have dinner on the early side. Metro Bistro had just opened its doors and we walked in at 7:30.  We thought we would be dining alone at such an early...
review_full: It was our first evening in Madrid and we were tired so we wanted to have dinner on the early side. Metro Bistro had just opened its doors and we walked in at 7:30. We thought we would be dining alone at such an early hour, but much to our surprise several other people walked in. Everyhting we ordered was not only beautiful on the plate, but absolutely delicious. The crunchy anemones, the versatile salad, the black pearl risotto with scallops, the lamb and the pineapple cannelloni just wonderful. The waiter was charming and the service impeccable. What a lovely first dinner in Madrid. Recommend it and would go back in a minute!

review_full: My wife and I ate at the Metro Bistro on the last night of our weekend break. The food and service were superb. Next time we are in Madrid, we will be back to try the Tasting Menu, great value at 38 euros.

review_preview: My husband was on deck to find a restaurant on our final night in Madrid.  He read previous reviews on Tripadvisor and picked Metro Bistro.  Initially, we were disappointed that we were directed to sit at the bar (because we didn't have reservations); however, our...
review_full: My husband was on deck to find a restaurant on our final night in Madrid. He read previous reviews on Tripadvisor and picked Metro Bistro. Initially, we were disappointed that we were directed to sit at the bar (because we didn't have reservations); however, our excellent waiter made up for the lack of a seat at a table. Each and every course was amazing! We chose the scallops with black rice for our main entree. The waiter explained in detail what we were eating. For dessert, I had the pineapple filled with frozen yogurt, and my husband had a delightful assortment of chocolate desserts. All I can say is "Wow". The restaurant was filled with Americans, so Tripadvisor must be directing all of us overwhelmed tourists to decent restaurants. Thank you.

review_preview: We chose Metro Bistro  for our last dinner  in Madrid and we  couldn't have enjoyed it more. Situated just off wonderful Plaza Mayor, it is rather simple in appearance - not fancy but pleasant.  It appears that the staff - from chef Matias Smith to...

Everything we tasted was very good ( it would be difficult to mention the names in English,since I asked for the Spanish menu) but one dish stands out and shouldn't be missed: THE BEST dessert ever: the pineapple canneloni ! thin slices of pineapple wrapped around semi freddo yogurt and served with mango sauce : to die for!! review_full: We had a fabulous meal at Metro Bistro. And, being North Americans, we appreciated being able to make a dinner reservation for an earlier time than the typical Madrid dinner! The cuisine was very interesting, featuring creative combinations of food which were healthy and delicious. We shared a starter of their featured sea anemone with Asian greens, after reading about it on TA. It was quite a treat and probably something we'll never get again. For our first course, my husband had the pumpkin soup with cream and cheese and he loved it. I had a salad with figs and goat cheese which was also outstanding. For our main course, he had a slow cooked lamb with truffle sauce and I had scallops with black rice in a Ras El Hanout cream sauce. The flavors were all wonderful! Unfortunately, we didn't have room for dessert, but I'm sure it was terrific as well. The service was impeccable and for the quality of our meal, we thought it was reasonably priced. We recommended the restaurant to some friends who also said it was their best meal in Madrid.

review_full: I fancied a steak so did my usual and checked out Trip advisor from the hotel to see what was about. Some of the restaurants by the hotel looked nice but the reviews were not good then I spotted Steak Burger Atocha. The reviews were good and it was just round the corner. I didn't really fancy a burger but decided to give it a go anyway. First impression was good as we were taken to our table. Drinks order was taken straight away and we were given time to look at the menu. My fiancé chose the Nachos to start and I had the chicken wings. The nachos was easily enough for both of us and were some of the best I've had. Could have been a bit spicier but my fiancé saw to that with Tabasco. The chicken wings with the thick sweet sauce on the side were a star, sweet, crispy and cooked to perfection. For mains we both had steak. My fiancé had medium and mine was rare and they were cooked to perfection. I almost went for the burgers but I am not a great burger fan as I like my Steak but when I saw some of them coming out for other tables they looked fabulous. Meal was finished of with Carrot cake and a complementary milky sweet alcoholicy drink which was really nice. All in all if you are in the Atocha area and looking for good food, Reasonably priced and good service do yourself a favour and give Steak burger a try. I'll certainly be going back next time I'm in Madrid.

The waitress brought over some bread that was both crusty and soft in the right places, although a shame that they appear to charge for this (albeit less than two euros). The rib-eye was cooked medium-rare, as requested and was the best I have had in a long while... full of flavour and well seasoned. Alas the sizeable portion of fries was also well seasoned and eaten together there was too much salt going on. If I was eating here again I would opt for the baked potato, which is finished on the grill, and find someone to share the salad with.

The grilled peppers starter along with sausage was great but as usual I had too much fresh bread and didn't leave enough room for the whole meal. The staff were very friendly and attentive, service was smooth and accurate. The wine list had a good selection of Argentinian wine as well as Spanish. I would highly recommend for anyone to visit, a great experience.

No matter, the staff received us with open, friendly, arms.  Now, I have been a lover of traditional New York cheesecake for as long as I can remember, and I'm invariably disappointed when fancy restaurants try to turn it into something that it is not meant to be. With that said, I can say that the Cheesecake I had at Metro Bistro is the best cheesecake I have ever had, and it is by no means a traditional Cheesecake. First of all, it comes in what looks something like a large Martini glass. Right there I was thinking, ok, here we go again, why can't restaurants leave the cheesecake alone. But then I took my first bite, and was transported to cheesecake heaven. It had the traditional cheesecake flavor we all love, infused with dulce de leche. It was simply superb. If you love cheesecake, by all means try this one.

review_full: We have just returned from one one of the best meals we have had in 16 days throughout Spain. I wish we had found it before our last night in Madrid. While we have had some really good meals in Madrid, we would have substituted most of them for Metro Bistro Although we had read that it was hard to get into, because it was summer, not only did we get a reservation but there were plenty of seats all evening. First of all, the service was fantastic. Friendly, welcoming and seemed they were glad we were there. We had been a little concerned that most of the reviews talked more about the waiter Ibrahim and we thought maybe all the reviews were done by his family. Well, he was on vacation and the service was still great and we aren't members of his family pushing the restaurant. While not inexpensive, the portions are large and delicious. We were given a small cucumber mojito when we arrived. We split an appetizer of sliced veal that gives Iberico a run for it's money. We also split the slow roasted, low temperature lamb that was amazing. We finished with the chocolate dessert that was four different chocolate treats. They followed up with candy treats and limoncello. This is not your typical tapas restaurant so be prepared for a more leisurely meal with cloth napkins and tablecloths.  I don't understand why this restaurant is not higher on the list for TA but I would go back in a heartbeat. Just sad we can't do it this trip.

title_review: One of the best restaurants in Madrid.
review_preview: It is not surprising how highly this restaurant already ranks on tripadvisor but I believe it should be higher. My girlfriend and I visited this restaurant last night and we had such a fantastic experience I felt compelled to sign up to tripadvisor to share...
review_full: It is not surprising how highly this restaurant already ranks on tripadvisor but I believe it should be higher.  My girlfriend and I visited this restaurant last night and we had such a fantastic experience I felt compelled to sign up to tripadvisor to share it with everyone else.  I will separate the review into key areas: The Welcome: A warm and friendly greeting from the floor staff working that evening. We had no reservation which wasn't a problem and we were allowed to choose a table. The building is well decorated and modern providing a elegant atmosphere.  The Service: Exceptional care and time was given to us. Being the naive British tourists that we are, our Spanish is less than satisfactory. This was no problem for the staff who attempted to the best of their ability to translate and answer the many questions that we had. The food arrived promptly and we were given all kinds of complementary bits and pieces (explained in the food section). The Wine: The wine list is extraordinary! A few pages of whites and roses and an even bigger section of reds. These range from around Spain, France and the rest of the world. I chose an Argentinian Malbec for €21.50 which is an average price on the menu, this was lovely. The large variety also comes with prices ranging from €14 right up to €260. You will definitely find a wine that you like on this menu.  The Food: The best part of the evening. The menu boasts a selection of starters including four options for vegetarians. There are around 7 main course options which include a variety of meat and fish. There is also the option to enjoy a 7 course tasting menu for €38 per head. My girlfriend and I chose to order from the menu rather than try the tasting menu. Despite this we were given a stylish drink on arrival which we are still not sure what exactly it was but tasted amazing! Following this we were provided with a variety of breads consisting of normal white, spiced Peruvian and a subtle chocolate and orange version and all accompanied with olive and sage butters. Our starters of fois gras then arrived which was elegantly presented on a thin white plate with stylish and tasty decoration and was absolutely incredible. For our main course we chose the bacon and veal hamburger with fried yacca, caramelised onions and melted Camembert. If you have a big greasy burger pictured in your head then remove that image now! It was the best burger I've ever had. It consisted of two burgers of a veal and bacon blend. Between these was the fried yacca and the melted Camembert. They have chosen not to include a bun with the burger which is a fantastic idea and really adds to the flavour and presentation. For dessert I chose the caramelised pineapple filled with half frozen yoghurt and mango sorbet which was refreshing and light.  We were then provided with complementary sugar coated jellies one, amaretto and the other passion fruit.  The chef is nothing short of a genius with what they have done with the menu. The presentation and flavours were sublime, that can easily be compared to Michelin star standards. The price of all this luxury €78, and I walked out of there feeling like I had robbed them.  I couldn't urge you enough to visit Metro Bistro if you are ever in Madrid.  Thanks for a wonderful evening!

review_full: El mini bar is a cosy and vintage tapas restaurant right in the centre of Madrid. I would recommend booking a day or two in advance as the restaurant gets extremely busy after 8pm with a queue that goes right out of the door (especially on weekends).  Our hotel kindly booked a slot for us at 8:30pm however upon arrival the staff seemed to be a tad confused as the booking was under the hotels name and not ours. After a little back and forth of them telling us to come back at 11pm as we didn’t have a booking, eventually they found our reservation and we were seated... so the service at first impression wasn’t great.  We asked for a recommendation on how many tapas dishes to select and the waitress recommended 3-4 if we were very hungry, so that’s what we went with. We decided upon a mixture of the eggplant, chicken, boar and croquettes. All of which were amazing but especially the eggplant (the sauce that came with it was the best of the night). The dishes were also generous size portions and left us complete full! (They also provide all tables with complimentary bottled water and bread to go with the meals). To top off what was a great meal, the cocktails they provide are amazing. I had a few strawberry daiquiris and they are made quick and fresh straight to your table. If the restaurant/bar wasn’t so packed after our meal I would of definitely stayed just to have some more drinks. They worked out €7.50 each which is great considering back home they would be around £10 each.  I really wish I could rate this restaurant 5/5 however the service we received at the beginning was quite hostile and no dishes were brought to our table with a smile. Based purely off of service I have to rate El miniBAR 4/5 however the food and drinks quality overall was amazing and if you want good tapas, go here!

review_full: A friend and I stopped by Rosi La Loca for a drink and a bite to eat since we both had appointments in the city center. I knew the food was good, and my friend is a foodie. He loved it. Rosi La Loca puts a modern spin on traditional Spanish dishes.  For COVID measures, they took our temperatures and contact information (for contact tracing) at the door and gave us hand sanitizer. There was a plastic barrier between all of the tables, and staff brought cutlery in plastic packaging, which they removed from the table immediately. The plastic packaging feels wasteful, but I understand the goal is to protect customers.  Cristina and Ismail were extremely attentive. Ismail speaks perfect English, and all of the staff quickly scanned our table for empty glasses/plates every time they passed.  I recommend Rosi La Loca to anyone visiting Madrid. It’s fun and friendly, and the food is delicious.

title_review: Fun place with interesting ways to present food
review_preview: The restaurant is on an alleyway that is not so inviting, but inside you are in a colorful and interesting environment. There's an upstairs and downstairs so the restaurant is bigger than you would think. I would not recommend sitting outside, the alleyway is not...
review_full: The restaurant is on an alleyway that is not so inviting, but inside you are in a colorful and interesting environment. There's an upstairs and downstairs so the restaurant is bigger than you would think. I would not recommend sitting outside, the alleyway is not nice. The sangria was great, loaded with fruit. The food comes very quick so don't order everything in one go else you'll have a table loaded with food. There are limited options for a vegetarian but we still managed. We started with the eggplant chips (really delicious) and the burrata salad (also delicious). The next two dishes were not my favorite - we ordered the smoky octopus, it was the whole octopus (not just the legs) and although well cooked I was turned off by parts of it - a bit gooey and chewy. The tuna tartar was also not to my taste, it was quite spicy and the red sauce took away from the natural tuna flavor. The desert was probably our best part of the meal - the tiramisu served in a coffee pot. It was really delicious, quite rich so one to share was perfect. It was a fun experience but I would not go back.

review_full: My boyfriend and I went to Oven for lunch and the staff was really friendly. They were helping us with ordering in Spanish and overall our food came out fast, even though it was entirely full. However, two days after we went there for dinner. Our waitress was not having a good day it seemed, as she checked if we were done multiple times in 10 minutes time. And she did not even try to understand us in English. After we were finished, no one came to us to check if the food was good or to give the check (even though the place was almost empty at that time). Three stars, because of the difference in service. The food was really good both times though!

review_full: My daughter is studying in Madrid this year and my wife and I are here visiting. This was where we came for our first dinner and it was great. The servers were friendly and asked if we wanted menus in English. Everything was tasty from the bread to the pasta. We really enjoyed a grilled provolone dish that had tomatoes and peppers. The sangria was delicious as well. Side note for those from the USA. Service is different in Spain as they take a more leisurely approach to dinner and be prepared to flag someone down if you want something as you may not see them again until it’s time to order coffee. It’s not personal, it’s just how it is. We enjoyed our food and would go back again.

review_preview: We actually ate at this superb restaurant 2 times in a one week period.  The food is a fusion of "Spanish" dishes plus other foods and flavors, all very interesting but above all, appetizing and very delicious.  As you sit down, you are treated to...
review_full: We actually ate at this superb restaurant 2 times in a one week period. The food is a fusion of "Spanish" dishes plus other foods and flavors, all very interesting but above all, appetizing and very delicious. As you sit down, you are treated to a wonderful shot of celery drink, imagined by the great bartender. A combo of liquor and celery with a tiny little stalk in a shot glass, absolutely delicious! The entree selections are limited but all really delicious, with ample portions. The wait staff could not be nicer and more attentive! And for dessert, we first ordered the white chocolate cheesecake, which is more of a thick concoction with white chocolate strips. Have never tasted anything so delicious! Their flan is also wonderful! The prices were reasonable, considering the high overall quality of the selections, and their wine list is very nice. Highly recommend this wonderful restaurant, and, as mentioned, is right off the Plaza Mayor, where you can walk around in after a fabulous meal at this place.

One of our party chose the chicken dish which was on the front ‘specials’ page. He had virtually finished with just about a quarter of the chicken left when he found it was completely frozen. We were all flabbergasted as had never seen this before. The majority had appeared to be cooked ok but the last bit completely frozen. The staff were good and took the price of this dish off our bill and offered us a dessert but none of us could face eating anything else. So we paid and left and kept our fingers crossed that none of us went down with food poisoning. It was such a shame as it was supposed to be a special dinner to celebrate my birthday and it was completely ruined. Therefore I’m sorry but I can’t and daren’t recommend this restaurant.

title_review: Amazing food. The most rude server I’ve encountered to date.
review_preview: Minibar came highly recommended by a friend that has lived in Madrid for sometime. I was very excited and was told you couldn’t go wrong. The friend was right for the most part, the food was incredible. We ordered a variety to cater for vegetarians...
review_full: Minibar came highly recommended by a friend that has lived in Madrid for sometime. I was very excited and was told you couldn’t go wrong. The friend was right for the most part, the food was incredible. We ordered a variety to cater for vegetarians and meat eaters alike. As much as we loved the food, the service (one particular employee in particular) reallyyyy tainted our experience. We arrived and immediately notified the host that although just two of us had arrived, we would eventually have 5 in 15 minutes and were happy to wait at the bar or a smaller table in the meantime. Although most of the staff was fairly friendly, the man we told this to could not have been more unfriendly and grumpy. He rolled his eyes, told us there was only so much he can do (to which we replied it would be understandable if we had to wait a beat when they arrived). Meanwhile, a couple that was sitting at a five person table graciously offered to swap tables with our two person one. He managed to enthusiastically butter them up and refuse to allow the switch. It was so uncomfortable that another waiter went as far as to say not to listen to his colleague as he was rude and not helpful. To top it off, he ended up being our waiter upstairs. Although he actually was quite helpful with food recommendations and portions, he continued to be rude by being snarky and correcting our attempt to be polite by speaking in Spanish. He ridiculed the fact that we accidentally said copa instead of vaso and mocked our mistake by bringing us a wine glass. I’m so torn about coming back. This was by far the rudest server we have encountered during our two weeks, but the food was indeed quite good. Be warned- the upstairs feels like an overflow/party room and the atmosphere pales in comparison to below. I’m not one to write reviews but cannot help but give a heads up.

review_preview: I come very often to Madrid from Prague to piano training and pedagogy Suzuki training.  My husband is English and I am Puertorican. We both love good food. We found this gem after walking in the rain for hours. We had the boar roll (our...
review_full: I come very often to Madrid from Prague to piano training and pedagogy Suzuki training. My husband is English and I am Puertorican. We both love good food. We found this gem after walking in the rain for hours. We had the boar roll (our favorite), aubergines wrapped in bacon with tomato orange sauce, panko chicken strips, Manchego cheese cured with black truffles (absolutely delicious) with wine, beers and excellent service. I read review from an American saying that he had the aubergine with bacon and that it was delicious although it was not bacon. Well, certainly not streaky American bacon. If he travels and try all the world bacons, he would learn that American bacon is not the “only” bacon. Take for example the English bacon! Full of meat. Take the Eastern Europe bacon, extra thick and chunky, take the Italian pancetta. What I am trying to say is that North Americans aka USA people think their food products are the one and only ones in the world! So beware of reviews from some kind of people. The service here was absolutely out if the world. Many waiters looking after you! We travel a lot and know what is good food and good service. This place really deserves an excellent rate. Money worth food was excellent as well! We are definitely coming back!

review_full: Minibar is not a particularly enticing name for a restaurant, but the packed tables and line out the door told a different story. This was to be our first experience with tapas and we were truly spoiled right out of the gate. First off, don’t expect a small plate of olives, some cured meat and a little cheese, this place is full on creative genius. My favorite plate by far was roasted eggplant wrapped in bacon with tomato orange sauce. It wasn’t bacon, it was just the right amount of some kind of yummy specialty ham draped on the big chunks of succulent eggplant and the sauce on it was a-mazing! All the tapas were as interesting and yummy and you will be sorry you can’t eat more. Make a reservation, chances are pretty good you’ll need it. Service is friendly, helpful and responsive. We overdid it on ordering food, had several drinks before and during the meal and ended up with full bellies and a 50€ bill.

review_preview: Maybe we were there on an off night, but the atmosphere/ambiance of this restaurant is lacking. The food was tasty, no complaints, but we were in and out within an hour.  The place has a funky vibe that reminded me of a college hangout, not...
review_full: Maybe we were there on an off night, but the atmosphere/ambiance of this restaurant is lacking. The food was tasty, no complaints, but we were in and out within an hour. The place has a funky vibe that reminded me of a college hangout, not a good restaurant. The service, although indeed friendly, was overbearing. We were asked 3 times within the first 5 minutes if we were ready to order food yet. Every other patron appeared to be under the age of 35 (we are in our early 60's). A few tables had young children, and many appeared to be college students. At first I thought they were moving us along because we didn't fit the profile, but I noticed everyone received fast paced service. If you are looking for some decent food, a quick beverage, and to be on your way, choose this place. If you want a leisurely dinner, with a relaxed atmosphere, go elsewhere.

review_preview: Highly recommended. During our trip to Madrid, we visited this place twice since the combination of food- money- service- ambiance were just great ! Although we did not have any reservation ( it is better to book a table in advance), the extremely polite and...
review_full: Highly recommended. During our trip to Madrid, we visited this place twice since the combination of food- money- service- ambiance were just great ! Although we did not have any reservation ( it is better to book a table in advance), the extremely polite and very professional waiter - Lucas - was there for us to find a table and recommend us the best dishes of the restaurant. Actually ALL the dishes are great but the highlight for me are the ' Presa de cerdo Iberic ' , one of the best jamon iberico I have ever tried. Also, the potatoes ( from starters) with the 3 different sauces are extremely delicious. The hamburger -a surprise since it does not have the traditional bread but it consists of 2 beefs and potatoes - is one of the highlights of the Metro Bistro as well as the dish with the pork. We had also a great red wine, the 'Habla del Silencio '. Another surprise the bread- try the dark one with orange and chocolate ! In one word : you have to visit the place more than one time !  p.s. Lucas offered us in the beginning of our dinner, apple mojito . Our dinner just has started like this ...

review_full: A friend found this place online with great reviews so she wanted to give it a try. We were treated to two tasting samples of the house special mojito. While it was very good they also had several other cocktails which we ended up getting. They are good and definitely better than a typical empanada one would have, but I have certainly had better ones with more flavor and spice before. To consider it as one of the top ten places to eat in Madrid (as is shown on here) is a misrepresentation, in my opinion. If you are in a hurry and want a good, fast, and inexpensive meal, then I would definitely recommend to come here. One thing I'll say is that the service I received was excellent which is why I give it 4 stars instead of 3. Very pleasant and helpful young man.

review_full: We visited here after finding it through trip advisor. We wanted somewhere more authentic and not overly priced. We ordered 4 tapas dishes through the recommendations of the waitress (menu not English) and Sangria which cost us €32. Staff were really helpful in both helping us choose off the menu and when we enquired about general things to do in Madrid. It was busy but I felt we got as much service as we would have wanted without being hassled or feeling like we'd been forgotten. I don't know the name of the waitress but she provided this service and even told us about where to go out and get souvenirs.  4 tapas dishes were too much for us! The waitress did enquire thinking we didn't like the food but it was literally too much for us to eat. But i thought it was nice to ask as I've had experiences where I've left a plate of food because it wasn't nice and the waiters have not cared. I therefore thought service deserved a good rating as she was really attentive.  The restaurant is quite small (see photos) but this didn't bother us. This dining was better than the one we had in La Latina the previous evening which cost us double and it had a nice albeit busy atmosphere. Food was not 5* but we didn't want anything fancy. Would recommend if you are okay with small and cheerful but not if you want a fine dining experience.

So we sat down there.  The table was quickly cleared but when I asked for the children's menu (and yes I did speak in Spanish) all I was given was the adults 'menu del dia' and was told that there wasn't a separate children's menu. By this time our children were very hungry and didn't want to trapse upstairs and hunt for somewhere else to eat so we shared 2 menus between the 4 of us. The children ate the pasta starter which they said was nice. The Oxtail my husband had was fatty and cold (a lump of bone on the plate) and there were no potatoes (as stated it came with on the menu), My small piece beef was like a piece of gristle on the plate and was not nice either. No bread was brought out until I asked for it and the service was terrible....we waited a long time after the meal before the puddings were brought out. This was the best part of the meal! We had chocolate cake and profiteroles which were both delicious.  It was the worst meal we had in a week staying in Madrid and we would not recommend it or be returning to it again.
