Its located just off Plaza Mayor which is a prominent tourist destination so its quite easy to find!  We were treated to a welcoming cocktail type shot to begin with which I think was a mojitio style with celery. Very nice I must say!  We tried the 7 degustation menu and had cocktails to drink. We had been to a cocktail bar previously so decided to stick with them instead of wine.  The meal was excellent, course after course came at an even tempo while it was quick we never felt rushed! It was perfect! The service was excellent and we addressed in English by all the waiter which helped. Some had better English than others but I can't complain after all I am a visiter in their country.  Overall service and food was excellent and the highlight was the chocolate dessert medley, amazing!!! Price was reasonable too for a degustation menu, €38pp and cocktails for around €90. There are many place that do fine dining degustation menus to choose from in Madrid but this is a bargin in comparison!  I would thoroughly recommend going here if in Madrid.

review_full: Our first night in Madrid and we picked this restaurant, with help from trip advisor of course. We went to dinner a little earlier than expected, maybe 7pm, and had the place to ourselves.  The location is nice right along Gran Via. Inside, the restaurant has a great look to it and the staff was quick to have us seated and taken care of. English and Spanish menu options.  First of all, drinks are amazing. We sat near the bar so we got to watch our waiter make each one. Order sangria (comes in a little mason jar) and 2 mojitos- strawberry and mango (comes in flower pot). We could've drank 3 rounds of these.  The menu has a great selection, sticks true to its Italian/pizzeria feel. Our waiter was helpful to answer questions and give recommendations. We got a variety of pizza, mozzarella, and pastas. All spectacular. You could really tell they take time with each dish and use the stone oven!  We had to end the nice with dessert; cheesecake and oven baked cookie skillet. WOW. we may go back just for these, we were stuffed from the great meal but we definitely made room for this.  What really finished it perfectly was when our waiter brought us each a shot of an aperitif on the house (can't remember the name of it, but some kind of cinnamon-y milk-alcohol mixture). It was really a nice gesture that we would have never expected.  It's going to be hard to top this; if all else fails we could be back here in a few nights!  I recommend giving it a shot if you love some good Italian food and amazing service. Oh and did I mention the great prices?

Meanwhile a family of 4 were seated next to us. They ordered and received drinks, bread, a pizza for their children and a salad. Yes we could have yelled a the waitress to take our order while she waited in that family, but that isn’t how service works. We got up and left. Reality is their is a pizza place called Hot Now just a 5 minute walk away that will accommodate you with a smile. You get to sit alone or at a communal table, which is nice to interact with locals. This place was nearly full and they had no issue putting us at the communal table. The guacamole was excellent and the pizza was amazing for less money than this pretentious place. Don’t waste your time here wander 5 minutes into the side streets and get better food for your money. They got one star because I can’t give zero. But this is clearly zero star.

The place is starting to get packed around 9pm though (normal Spanish dining time) so better hurry or make a reservation! The price is also very reasonable, with hamburgers average around 10-12 euros for 250 gram beef (comes with fries and small salad). Definitely great burger for good price.

I stuck with it because of the good reviews and we were all very glad we did. We saw other people with blankets and so asked for some for us, and then the drinks arrived which were all generously served and helped to warm us up. When the food came, its quality and originality took us all by surprise. We had the tapas Breton, some chicken cigarillos and wild boar crepes which were all delicious and very different from your standard tourist tapas fare. We ordered some more drinks afterwards and were well on our way to a merry night by then. We were brought plenty of free nibbles and a farewell shooter each, which amused my parents. The measures are ridiculously generous and they seem to specialize in gin and tonic which really hit the spot.  A posh night out it ain't, El Mininbar is a little local spot with great and well-priced food and drinks that would suit an informal place to meet friends or start a night out. We'll be back, but I might leave my parents at the hotel next time.

review_preview: We went here on our first night in Spain and absolutely loved it. We had a G&T and it was delicious, poured at the table in a fun way too. We ordered the tapa Breton, a winner of the best tapas in Madrid 2013, and...
review_full: We went here on our first night in Spain and absolutely loved it. We had a G&T and it was delicious, poured at the table in a fun way too. We ordered the tapa Breton, a winner of the best tapas in Madrid 2013, and it was delicious! Definitely try it if you go there, it's grilled cheese, served with a tomato jam, coriander, balsamic and oil with bread on the side. It's very rich but a must! We also had the breaded calamarie which was also amazing. That was enough to fill the two of us but we couldn't resist the brownie desert. Also had a few wines which were really good. Cost around 40 euro in total. The waiters were really friendly too and it had a local feel about it. Absolutely loved it and would recommend you got here if you're in Madrid!

review_preview: What a fab surprise this restaurant was! Husband's first night in Spain and he wanted to taste his first patatas bravas but wasn't to be. He was disappointed - until the meal arrived! Recommendations on the Breton are correct. You have to taste the flavours...
review_full: What a fab surprise this restaurant was! Husband's first night in Spain and he wanted to taste his first patatas bravas but wasn't to be. He was disappointed - until the meal arrived! We'll be back for breakfast tomorrow - it was that good!

title_review: Great little place right opposite the Tryp Ambassador hotel
review_preview: We went to this place based on Trip Advisor recommendations and were glad that we did it was really very good (4.5 / 5). It is directly opposite the Tryp Ambassador hotel which is where we were staying. As others have said it doesn't look...
review_full: We went to this place based on Trip Advisor recommendations and were glad that we did it was really very good (4.5 / 5). It is directly opposite the Tryp Ambassador hotel which is where we were staying. As others have said it doesn't look a lot, in fact I hadn't noticed it while coming into and out the hotel. Once sat down, the staff were great - not much English spoken so we went with our limited Spanish and the English descriptions on the menu and it worked out fine. The Tapas we had was excellent - their award winning cheese special was great. We arrived early (7:30pm) and had to wait until 8:00pm (they looked closed on Sunday) for the food to start but had an excellent looking Gin & Tonic while we waited. The place was full when we left with a mixture of locals and visitors creating a lively atmosphere. Try this place if you want a great Tapas bar slightly off the main tourist routes.

review_full: I went with a girl to this lovely restaurant, we were walking in Sol and found this place in a narrow street. From Tripadvisor recommendations we decided to went in. The food was truly amazing!! the waiters were so nice and friendly all the time. The service was really fast. Something that I liked the most was they have the menu in 4 different languages (not common in that area). The paella was the best in Madrid, and we ordered "Medallones de solomillo" which I fell in love with. Everything in this place was so good that we are planning to coming back tonight again!! I recommend this place 100%.

title_review: Amazing atmosphere and food at great prices
review_preview: I'm not one to usually leave a review but this place needs a special mention. After a bad start for the holiday, this was our 1st dining experience in Madrid and what a lovely place to spend it. The atmosphere is modern and relaxed with...
review_full: I'm not one to usually leave a review but this place needs a special mention.  After a bad start for the holiday, this was our 1st dining experience in Madrid and what a lovely place to spend it.  The atmosphere is modern and relaxed with exceptionally tasty food at extremely reasonable prices  We opted for a paella, x2 bottles of Rioja which came to £35.  The house even have us x2 glasses of wine on the house (it was fair to say we had a good time)  If your a meat lover look out for there stake platter, and if there are more then x4 of you then I'd personally opt for both paella and steak, you won't leave hungry.  I hope the rest of out holiday eats live up to this place.  A real gem

review_preview: Just off Plaza Mayor a real gem. We went in and the place was empty so we were a little unsure but as soon as we were greeted and sat we knew we'd be ok. Actually we were better than ok - the food was...
review_full: Just off Plaza Mayor a real gem. We went in and the place was empty so we were a little unsure but as soon as we were greeted and sat we knew we'd be ok. Both my husband and I said that this was probably some of the nicest food we had ever had. We went to Bodin the following night and instead of staying for coffee and dessert we returned to Metro Bistro and they were more than happy to let us just have coffee and some of their gorgeous chocolates.  Would definitely recommend the chocolate selection for dessert - all homemade and to die for.  The bill was a lovely surprise too, very reasonable. Would definitely recommend Metro Bistro to anyone wanting to have a great meal, we will be back on our next visit to Madrid

review_preview: There was a big trade show in Madrid this year and I chose this restaurant for a business dinner, which was a big mistake.I went to this restaurant a few days earlier to make sure if this restaurant was suitable for the business dinner....
review_full: There was a big trade show in Madrid this year and I chose this restaurant for a business dinner, which was a big mistake. I went to this restaurant a few days earlier to make sure if this restaurant was suitable for the business dinner. A staff member confirmed my booking and told to reserve a big table nearby the window. On that dinner date, I was waiting at the reception to be served. However, a group of (stupid) people cut in the line and surprisingly took the window table! I spoke to the staff member whom I spoke to the other day but she said the table was occupied and they were preparing another table. The table was in the noisiest part of restaurant, we felt quite uncomfortable. The food was average at best, we had four more business dinners during the show, this was the worst in every way. When checking out, we were told that the credit card reader was not working and there was an ATM over there. I refused to fetch money (also cashing incurs an interest and a cashing fee), then the staff said "This is not working, OK you can stay here all the night!". What a rude person! This was not our fault at all, how dare could she behave like that? A couple of more customers were also told like this and got frustrated. I can see many positive reviews for this second or third class restaurant, but I do suggest there are many more better choices in Madrid.

title_review: You can't tell a book by its cover
review_preview: We found this place on Trip Advisor and decided to drop by one evening to see whether we would like to go there the next day.  It was not inviting looking at all.  It is quite small with only a couple of tables inside and...
review_full: We found this place on Trip Advisor and decided to drop by one evening to see whether we would like to go there the next day. It was not inviting looking at all. It is quite small with only a couple of tables inside and the outdoor seating was very messy looking. We had just about written it off, but I took another look at the reviews and thought we would give it a try. Wow! We went for a late lunch and sat outdoors in the shade and had a fantastic meal. For such a small place, the tapas they come up with are outstanding. They are quite complex and way above any of the other ones we had during our stay. We had their award-winning tapa Breton, a melted cheese dish; capresse, and minced meat with guacamole on toast. Everything was delicious.

review_preview: Never stopped at this little tapas restaurant across from our hotel because it was always full - now know why. This may be the best tapas restaurant in Spain! Yes, it is unassuming, and the tapas are fabulous. Tried the Rabas de Calamar - corn...
review_full: Never stopped at this little tapas restaurant across from our hotel because it was always full - now know why. This may be the best tapas restaurant in Spain! Yes, it is unassuming, and the tapas are fabulous. Tried the Rabas de Calamar - corn batter fried squid with arugula salad and aioli (yummy); Salmoreja (best in Spain, not too thick, great accompaniments); Tapa Breton (2013 best tapa winner in Spain, crusty, melted cheese with coriander and quince jelly-incredible); Tinto de Verano (sangria with mint); gin and tonic (so different!). Service was great, location is near Plaza Oriente and the Opera, value is good, can't believe we found this little gem on our last day in Spain! Don't miss this terrific little tapas restaurant.

title_review: Just awesome food! What else do you need.?
review_preview: This little place at the end of plaza Santo. Domingo looks just like the other thousand joint in Madrid, but don't be fooled, there's much more. The place says nothing from the outside and it doesn't get much better inside. We got an outdoor table...
review_full: This little place at the end of plaza Santo. Domingo looks just like the other thousand joint in Madrid, but don't be fooled, there's much more. The place says nothing from the outside and it doesn't get much better inside. We got an outdoor table on a wonderful night in June and just asked the owner what to order. We had tapa Breton and canutillos filled with boar. Just excellent, in every way. The tapa Breton was one of the best dishes I had in Spain. Complex in flavor and yet simple to enjoy. I'll be going back to try some more dishes this week. Staff is extremely accommodating and friendly, they really run a great place.

title_review: Degustation menu - excellent value for money
review_preview: We visited the Metro Bistro near Plaza Mayor on a Saturday evening (it was Halloween, so we had made a reservation a few weeks back already). We opted for the 7 course degustation menu (38€ per person). It included pumpkin soup, deep fried anemones, smoked...
review_full: We visited the Metro Bistro near Plaza Mayor on a Saturday evening (it was Halloween, so we had made a reservation a few weeks back already).  We opted for the 7 course degustation menu (38€ per person). It included pumpkin soup, deep fried anemones, smoked eel with vegetables, scallop with black rise, long cooked lamb, pineapple cannelloni with mango mousse as well as an assortment of chocolate desserts.  The food was amazing - really delicious, well prepared and the portions were good size. It was a bargain for this price. In addition we had a bottle of Priorat red wine, water, 2 coffees and 2 sweet wines with the desserts (do try the Spanish, sweet white wine with the cannelloni and Pedro Ximenes with the chocolates). The price for all this: 107€!!! Excellent value I would say (in Finland similar meal would cost at least two times the same)!

review_preview: From the outside the restaurant looks quite small, however it's large enough don't worry. First thing I was really happy about was that tables are not crammed together so you can talk without being overheard. Next thing was the starter and the dessert. For starter...
review_full: From the outside the restaurant looks quite small, however it's large enough don't worry. First thing I was really happy about was that tables are not crammed together so you can talk without being overheard. Next thing was the starter and the dessert. For starter we shared potatoes with three different dips (thank you for recommending TA reviewer). This was really really really good! For the dessert we had pineapple cannelloni and of course a tribute to chocolate (cannelloni is better imo if you are not dark chocolate lover through and through). The only thing I was a little bit disappointed about was that we would really prefer some potatoes, more vegetables or something with our meal (maybe this was our fault and we were supposed to order sides?) but that should not discourage you from going, especially if you are looking for something little bit fancier.

I had a tenderloin filet with potatoes gratin and she had scallops on a black rice cake with a soft curry sauce. Both were excellent. A trio of chocolates - sweet, bitter and mousse - was very nice pairing to finish the last of our rioja. Very nice place, would definitely return to sample more of their wonderfully flavorful and presented food.

From start to finish the food was delightfully imaginative, inventive & just delicious, even the bread & the butter at the start. The table next to us were having the 7 course taster menu which we would love to have had but it would have been too much. This is a chef at the top of his game, the presentation was a delight & the staff were nothing but helpful. This is a must visit restaurant.

title_review: Very good but short of excellent
review_preview: We were attracted to the Metro Bistro by the very strong pattern of reviews and perhaps a little by the fact that it is quite close to our hotel in the Calle Atocha.  But although it was an acceptable hour for early dining in Spain,...
review_full: We were attracted to the Metro Bistro by the very strong pattern of reviews and perhaps a little by the fact that it is quite close to our hotel in the Calle Atocha. But although it was an acceptable hour for early dining in Spain, we almost gave it a miss because it was so empty. However the reviews won the day and we decided to give it a try in the expectation that it would fill up a bit later.  The seven course Taster Menu looked to be good value and we chose that, although a bit surprised to find that it was, as we later read on their web site, “a tour of their kitchen” or more correctly a tour of their menu rather than the bespoke set of dishes that we have become used to elsewhere. Overall it was a pleasing tour with some stops being better than others. The scallop on a black rice bed was excellent but the escalivada was trying too hard; the sea anemones with seaweed was interesting and the finale tribute to chocolate was sublime. It may sound a strange complaint, but because the courses were dishes from the menu they were on the large size for seven courses. However the service was excellent and the waitress and kitchen responded well to our request to slow down the delivery a bit towards the end. We would not go so far as some other reviewers to say “the best in Madrid” but it was very good value and an enjoyable meal. Pity about the empty tables that did not fill up as anticipated.

review_full: After being in Spain for two weeks, and many of the food offerings in the Spanish restaurants were similar, it was really refreshing to experience this fantastic place. Everything from the service to the food, and the unique way everything was presented, was just out of this world. Every dish was really wonderful. On many recommendations, we tried the sea treasures (anemones), which you don't see often on menus. It's a must try. The steak tartare was perfectly prepared with incredible flavor combinations. We had a lot of croquettes on our vacation, and these were by far the best. If you're a chocolate fan like we are, the tribute to chocolate is outstanding, and the perfect way to wrap up the meal. Each item represented chocolate from a different area of the world, and was really interesting to experience the difference with every bite. Loved this place!

The food was very good, as was the house white wine. And the prices were very reasonable...€18 for two glasses of wine and dinner.  While Trip Advisor calls it Oven Gran Via, it's really just called Oven. This is a great restaurant and it would be very good to go there with friends. I would definitely visit again. I recommend it strongly and you won't be disappointed.

review_full: Came here upon recommendation of our Airbnb host - immediately greeted once we arrived and were quickly seated. Staff were very kind and provide fast service. The server gave us some suggestions for tapas - we tried a grilled eggplant wrapped in bacon with tomato sauce + feta cheese, wild boar (similar to pulled pork) inside a spring-roll like crust, calamari and a dish that had a sweet & sour sauce with melted cheese one top served with bread. Personally wasn't really a fan of that sweet & sour dish but it could be worth it to try if you're a foodie, apparently it was an award winning tapa! We got sangrias that were cheap (3.50e) and served in large fish-bowl like glasses, absolutely delicious! Price of tapas ranged from 6-8e which is decent.

review_full: Another recommendation from Alicia at the Dear Hotel front desk (she should be a restaurant critic!). Tucked away downstairs near Plaza Major, thiis tapas joint has a lot of energy, fun staff who look like they’ve stepped straight off the street and a really nice menu and wine offering. We had their speciality, a wild boar roll that was to die for, some good standard croquettes and a slightly strange dish of hot sweet grilled cheese swimming in jam (which we were told had won a “best tapas in Madrid” award. Now, on another night it might have worked for us, and it might work for you, but we couldn’t get into it. When we told our waiter, though, he was totally cool and refused to charge us for it, even when I insisted. That’s style! We didn’t stay long, we paid very little for a good experience. Definitely recommend it.

review_full: Service was excellent here and was what we enjoyed most at this place. When we arrived we were told to wait 15 minutes for our table. As soon as we were seated, the staff who spoke great English gave us food recommendations according to our preferences and they taught us about the different combinations and portions. We ordered the cod fish which was crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. The portion was just nice for 2 people. We also ordered the chicken tenders with 3 sauces: teriyaki, thai sweet chilli and tartar, which was average. Lastly we had the fried spring roll with boar meat which was highly recommended by the staff and indeed it did not let us down. Would definitely recommend.

review_full: I googled best tapas bars in Madrid and this one came up an was very close to where we were staying. The service was friendly and helpful, but I felt very rushed - in terms of choosing a drink; then it felt like hurry up what do you want to eat when we had literally had the menu for 30 seconds. The waitress offered to help us choose and when I politely declined one of the recommendations because I don't like coconut milk she argued with me. The food was delivered quick smart and before we had finished our first drink the food had been delivered, eaten and the plates and table items had been whisked away again which had made us feel they wanted to us to eat quickly and leave - which we did. The restaurant is obviously very popular and very busy because when we were leaving they were turning people away who did not have bookings. The food was ok but I would have probably done better if I had been given time to read through the menu options properly without being rushed through to choose. Would I come back? Probably not. I was expecting to spend a nice evening out and we were in and out in 30 minutes. They must be doing something right though because they are obviously very popular.

review_full: To celebrate my 60th birthday in early April /2016, I traveled with a best friend to Spain...While we were in Madrid, we discovered a great place to have an American-style burger...The restaurant is called "Steakburgers", and is centrally located and quite near the Reina Sophia museum. The burgers were great, and you can order them not only to the doneness you prefer, but also in the size you would like, measured in grams!! It makes McDonald's Quarterpounders seem skimpy by comparison!! You have a choice of hard or soft rolls, and you can order fabulous appetizers as well such as chicken tenders or onion rings and the wait staff was always very friendly and attentive...I must mention our waitress, Jimena, who made us feel so welcome and at home, and made sure we had a great meal and an enjoyable time. If you are feeling even the slightest bit homesick for a good old American style hamburger, this is definitely the place you want to eat!! Better yet, prices were extremely reasonable! We ended up eating there several times during our stay in Madrid...

review_full: We were looking for a cheap meal in Madrid and this was one of the most highly recommended low cost places on Tripadvisor. We were initially skeptical as the restaurant was in a very touristy lane near Plaza del Sol, but we were wrong to worry. We came initially on a night after having some underwhelming and overpriced tapas elsewhere. We enjoyed the gazpacho, pork, stuffed peppers, salad and, most of all, the Galician octopus. The food was great - simple, but well prepared - and we had fantastic, friendly service. We were offered a 10% discount card if we returned, so we duly came back the following night and tried some different dishes - the croquettes and pork were highlights. Our waitress (the same as the previous night) was kind enough to give us each a glass of wine on the house. We ended up coming back a third time on our last day in Madrid for lunch, where we had all our favourite dishes. Couldn't recommend this one highly enough!

We each had a glass of tinto at the bar with a complimentary tapa (bread topped with cheese and greens), then ordered a serving of croquetas and bocadillos (small sandwiches on delicious thick bread) to share. One bocadillo had pork loin, roasted eggplant, brie, and aioli; the other had tuna, tomato, and olives. Everything was excellent for a light, well-priced bite. Definitely worth the trip if you’re touring the city center!

We had to wait for around 15-20 minutes but afterwards everything went fine. A waiter recommended taking not tapas but so-called raciones to share and out of his top 6 we took 5. All were very tasty, we had fish with shrimps, some meat like beef or bacon and also cheese which rocked the meal. Definitely worth asking the waiter, they tend to know the menu the best! In general it wasn’t also very expensive, each one paid around 12€ (food and drinks included). For sure el miniBAR is a place to revisit!

review_full: I went on trip advisor (plug plug) to find the best steakhouse in Madrid and chose the Cabana based on reviews. It's a cracking little restaurant based in the very busy Principe area which is rammed with bars eateries and people- incredibly busy. The restaurant is not massive with I'd guess around twenty tables and has a great vibe. There are plenty of waiters/waitresses so you don't have to wait around if anything is required.  The steaks come with nothing else however the sides are huge, at least big enough for two. I had the tenderloin and it was one of the best steaks I've had, cooked to perfection (rare obviously!). Our waitress Geraldine spoke good English and recommended a great Malbec which wasn't too expensive. She was attentive and good fun and if going to the restaurant definitely ask for her to be your server. The maitre d' was unobtrusive, good, but there if needed and added to the great atmosphere, helped by a free glass of fizz in the front bar afterwards.  Bill for two including wine was €90 and worth every penny. Go there.

review_preview: This started off bad tonight and ended worse.I used the restaurants website to request a reservation. Their auto reply said they would contact us to confirm the reservation. They didn't.My daughter who speaks Spanish contacted the restaurant  and they did not have our...
review_full: This started off bad tonight and ended worse. I used the restaurants website to request a reservation. Their auto reply said they would contact us to confirm the reservation. They didn't. My daughter who speaks Spanish contacted the restaurant and they did not have our reservation so she made one.  One of the servers seemed annoyed we weren't ordering drinks. Oh well! My family of 4 ordered three Ribeyes, 2 of which were 500kg (1 lb) and a skirt steak which appeared to be about 500 kg, de la Casa salad (Lettuce, Apple, Roquefort cheese, celery and walnuts). The salad was being shared so we requested the Roquefort, which has a bold taste, on the side. They didn't prepare it that way and cheese was sprinkled over the entire salad. That aside, the salad was tasty. I requested my steak be prepared medium-well. This should provide me a light pink inside. The waitress said they would have to cut the meat to get it med-well. I'm assuming she meant butterflyed, but passed on it not wanting a well-done piece of dried out meat. All 3 pieces including the 300 kg (small cut) came out med-rare. We send back a 300 & 500 kg Ribeyes. The smaller cut came back perfect & the larger cut was about the same as originally prepared. The skirts steak is served on a skillet over a mini hibachi. I used the hibachi to cook my Ribeye the rest of the way. Overall, the steak was good, far from great. The only side ordered was a baked potato which was quite tasty. Note: it is typical that beef is prepared more toward rare so be prepared to send it back. Our table was cleared & the check was brought over. We felt rushed!  What about dessert ??? We ordered 3 desserts;  Lemon sorbet Mango sorbet, vodka, caramelized orange and vanilla ice cream  Crepe filled with argentinian artisan caramel cream  The first 2 are actually beverages. The lemon sorbet has rum (?) In it. Both were tasty. Unfortunately, I did not get the crepe I requested & pointed to on the menu. Instead,  I received the Apple crepe flambeé with rum. Before the waitress drenched the poor crepe in rum (nor did it flambeé) we tried telling her. Then she argued with us insisting it was what was ordered.  She returned with a new dessert, but again, the wrong one; 3 small scoops of vanilla ice cream drenched in cheap chocolate sauce. Argentine Beef may be "The tastiest meat in the world," but I would choose any of the Prime steak houses in New York & Boston that I've eaten at over the Argentine cut at  La Cabańa Argentina and their poor service. A bitter taste to end to an average meal--waitress with an attitude. If you're dying for a steak, there are other steak houses in Mtadrid where the outcome must be better than what my family experienced.

review_full: With literally hundreds of restaurants to choose from in Centro Madrid and other popular neighborhood, it's hard to go wrong (but possible) when it comes to paella. We found this popular spot online, and to be honest, it isn't full of locals. Quite the opposite. There were people from the U.S. (us and others) Japan, other areas of Europe, New Zealand, and Canada that we knew of. And the restaurant definitely has their act together to cater to tourists, but that didn't spoil the experience at all. The decor is cheery, and the restaurant appear to be quite small from the entry, maybe seating 30 people. But having to use the "facilities" downstairs had me discovering an even larger lower level with at least another 40 seats. While even the lower level was attractive, I wouldn't want to dine here, so be sure to specify when you make a reservation, and you will need one if you want to eat anytime close to when you arrive, that main floor seating is a priority. It's just that much nicer. As for the food, it was wonderful. Our paella was the best we had in Madrid, though we did enjoy one that was perhaps a whisker superior while in Sevilla. Our servers, Roxanne and Alex, were superb, and the pricing was reasonable. Not inexpensive, but not out of line with the experience. Nice wine selection, too, by the glass and bottle, also at affordable prices. We highly recommend!

review_full: We found this bar after initially seeking out Botin and finding it was all booked. I had put El miniBAR on our list after reading TA so as it was nearby we decided to seek it out. We were brought a generous free appetiser to eat while we looked at the menu. Every dish we ordered was superb, fresh fried chicken with 3 dips, crispy boar rolls, and the Duck confit with prunes and potatoes, wow! We finished off with two pieces of the lightest, creamiest, tastiest cheesecake. We enjoyed it so much we went back with our friends the following day. They said their pick was the best Goat's cheese dish they'd ever tasted! We had superb gazpacho and a fab aubergine dish this time. Drinks, wine, beer and coffee, were reasonably priced too. Lovely friendly service.

review_preview: I have been a regular visitor of Metro Bistro Debod for years, since before they changed to their fusion latin-mediterranean menu. Missing what I have had before, I called for a reservation for two at Metro Bistro Plaza Mayor and opted for the tasting menu....
review_full: I have been a regular visitor of Metro Bistro Debod for years, since before they changed to their fusion latin-mediterranean menu. Missing what I have had before, I called for a reservation for two at Metro Bistro Plaza Mayor and opted for the tasting menu.  To my disappointment, it didn't turn out as good as I had expected. Another friend of mine had warned me before hand that, in her opinion, the Debod branch was better.  The bread and butter were as same as those in Debod. I enjoyed the curry bread and orange-chocolate ones, although they were a bit too hard and too dry for my taste. Our first dish was the salmorejo with olive oil ice-cream. It was soooo good that blew me away. However the upcoming dishes came with mix feelings.  The sea treasure was fine but way too salty and you get tired of the taste after 2-3 bites. The baked vegetable salad was fine.The eel added a nice flavour to it, however they put too little eel in the salad to be enjoyed thoroughly.  Then we proceed to main dishes. The black pearl was the star. Perfectly cooked. Black rice risotto was relish and the curry added great flavour combo. We finished our menu with iberian pork. The pork was good but the side dish was something like a purple cabbage roll was a real miss! Way too sour for me.  The first dessert, pineapple cannelloni was way too sweet. I had nothing to complain for the tribute to chocolate, since it is always my favourite at Metro Bistro.  The service was great. The staffs speak pretty well english and are very attentive regardless the restaurant is busy. However, I think the tasting menu on that day didn't flow. (Not sure that they change seasonally or not). It was like high and low all the time.  I'd go back not for the menu but for the a la carte options or otherwise just directly to the Debod one. The price-quality relation was okay and the price for the menu was reasonable. The drinks were well-priced too.

review_preview: A tiny, quirky bar tucked away on a charming street corner, El Minibar has got some seriously delicious, innovative food! We will definitely be back to try more of their unique tapas. This is very reasonably priced and very creative cuisine! First of all, you...
review_full: A tiny, quirky bar tucked away on a charming street corner, El Minibar has got some seriously delicious, innovative food! We will definitely be back to try more of their unique tapas. This is very reasonably priced and very creative cuisine! First of all, you must try their "grilled cheese," which is basically a huge plank of white cheese, creamy and gooey in the middle and crispy and caramelized at the edges. This gorgeous goo is drowning in a pool of heavenly tomato jam and topped with an earthy dose of pesto and a drizzle of balsamic. Served with crusty baguette, it's probably the most sinful and tasty tapa we've experience in our 11 days in Spain. Also phenomenal are the crispy boar rolls with portabella mushroom sauce: WOW. We split these two items and we were perfectly full. Add in a sangria, bottled water, and two beers and our bill was only 30€... So don't leave Madrid without eating here at least once (or twice:))! If you're looking for something with a little more international flair (and don't mind a slightly skanky bathroom overflowing with beer cases, which I thought only added to El Minibar's eccentric charm), this place is for you. Our only "complaint" was our free tapa (which is kinda hard to complain about, since it's FREE): deli-quality ham and cheese on a bit of bread that looked and tasted like it had been sitting out a bit too long. But I'm not going to end on a negative note; this place is seriously amazing! Glad we found it!

review_full: Yes, it is an Argentinean restaurant, and yes it is Angus beef but ultra tender meat, and yes it is rated #2 so far, and yes you should try it even if it's in the centre of Madrid, Spain. It is located in a deserted alley near the Congress Hall. There are some Indian and Peruvian restaurants nearby.  Spanish restaurants generally open late but this steakhouse runs from 1:30pm till wee hours without breaks so you can avoid the crowd and have an early dinner like us n many other foreigners. Locals come in after 8pm in general. The Angus steaks are so tender unlike what we had experienced in uk and other countries. No extra sauces given and not needed either anyway. There is a dish of herbal olive oil on the table that goes well with the meat but even better with the fries. We asked for a second dish. The many choices of Homemade desserts are recommended too. We had custard with sweet caramel sauce that was just the right thing for a strong cup of coffee.  Nice ambience but some waitress have limited English ability. There are English menus so worry not.

title_review: A shame - could have been much better!
review_preview: First off, the decor was beautiful - but that was it. From the moment we went in, the service was iffy: we were sat right by the door where people were coming and going throughout the meal. I assumed the restaurant was full, except I...
review_full: First off, the decor was beautiful - but that was it. From the moment we went in, the service was iffy: we were sat right by the door where people were coming and going throughout the meal. I assumed the restaurant was full, except I later discovered plenty of available seating downstairs! After taking our orders, the waiters forgot our drinks (we had to remind them about 30 minutes later). Then, I went to use the toilet but it wasn't clear where the toilets were, so I tried to ask a waiter for directions: I received a snarky reply, and whilst I was trying to listen, another waiter barged straight into me with a couple of menus - ouch! I rubbed my head and looked at him, waiting for an apology...silence.  Enter the main meals: I can't speak for all the meals, but the pork dish with sweet potato was quite small considering the 7 euro price and I left the restaurant feeling hungry! At one point I wanted to try my friend's food, but needed to ask the waiter a question first: when I tried to ask, he snatched the dish away before I could finish the question and my friend waited another 25 minutes for a new meal.  To top it all off, once the waiters had collected our plates they came back immediately with a receipt: I've never experienced anything like that - it felt like they wanted us out as soon as possible. We left pretty soon after that! So overall, a pretty exterior but poor - borderline rude - service and portion sizes that don't justify the price at all. Won't be back again!

review_full: 9/29/2018 Was looking for a great tapas bar while on vacation in Madrid and stumbled upon El Mini Bar and so happy I did! It ended up being my favorite place to eat there! The customer service, food, and drinks were all on point. This place has a comfortable hipster/laid back family vibe that made me feel welcomed and relaxed. The dining tables were also spaced out enough to allow for a bit of privacy for conversations which was very nice! I only tried two drinks which included the tinto de verano (sangria) for 3 Euro and the mojito for 7 Euro. Best mojito I've had so far!  I ended up going two nights in a row so I can try a variety of things on the menu. I was with my boyfriend and between the two nights we enjoyed the Crispy boar rolls, Cod + shrimp, and the Iberian sirloin with veggies and then the sirloin again but with grilled potatoes, green peppers and tomatoes. We wanted to go a back for a third time but also wanted to try other tapas bars around Madrid. Well, we ultimately regret that choice!  The tapas and raciones were honestly the best I've had in Madrid and I was blown away by the quality. The price point was good for the quality of both the food and service provided. If I ever get a chance to visit Madrid again I will definitely be visiting.

title_review: A true hidden gem off the beaten track
review_preview: The good: Looking for a quick bite before going to the movies can be at times difficult in Madrid as dinner time usually doesn't start till 9.00 pm. Looking for a good dinner in the center of Madrid can be also quite difficult seeing the...
review_full: The good: Looking for a quick bite before going to the movies can be at times difficult in Madrid as dinner time usually doesn't start till 9.00 pm. Looking for a good dinner in the center of Madrid can be also quite difficult seeing the quantity of restaurants and tapas bars. But Rosi La Loca delivered on both. I called ahead to make a reservation (which is advisable for later dinner times as the place is tiny and draws quite a crowd during dinner time), the restaurant called back an hour before our arrival to confirm the reservation (even some of the big and famous restaurants don't do that) and we have been received with a warm and personal welcome once we stepped into the simple yet nicely decorated restaurant. We decided to share a couple of the dishes from the menu, which has a good selection of tapas for everyone yet isn't overloaded with items. The food was well prepared and very tasty. For drinks try their Mojitos (especially the one with strawberry!). The service overall was very friendly, welcoming and fast.  The bad: There is nothing really to point out that was negative - yes, the hanging garden at the entrance was missing a couple of plants but the staff told me that they are updating the decor of the restaurant bit by bit. They are also working together with tourist groups so don't be surprised when now and then a large group guided by someone with an umbrella storms the restaurant to have a couple of tapas and drinks before they all leave as quickly as they entered the restaurant. The conclusion: For a small restaurant / tapas bar in the dead center of Madrid this place is definitely worth stopping by and try some of their cocktails and delicious tapas. It is a bit off from the big main street Gran Via so it is perfect if you want to take a break from the hustle and bustle of the big city, your sightseeing or shopping. The food is delicious, the drinks are strong and the staff is very friendly, welcoming and helpful. Thumbs up!

review_full: Are you hungry and craving some pizza?  We were walking back to our hotel and we decided to stop by Oven Mozzarella Bar in Gran Via. It looked pretty cool and elegant from outside. We noticed that it was really hard to get a table, it looked that there was quite a long wait.  We were lucky: weird enough, some tables were cleaned in a matter of 5 minutes and we were comfortably seated. Our table was very close to the kitchen so it was fun to watch the pizza men doing their lovely job....it was like a beautiful show. We ordered pizza margherita, chicken pizza, spicy prawn linguine, and salmon in hollandaise sauce with baked potatoes. The pizza were crunchy and good, but they...forgot to add tomato sauce. What kind of Margherita pizza was that, without red tomatoes sauce? For dessert we had apple crumble cake and affogato di caffe' (an Italian coffee-based dessert which takes the form of a scoop of vanilla gelato "drowned" with a shot of hot espresso). Everything was pretty tasty. We had a problem with the waiter: in taking our orders, he forgot to write down "the timing" of what we wanted. The result was that the pizzas and main courses came to our table all together...and we had to send back the pasta and the salmon for later. For that reason, when the spiced linguine returned, they were cold and over-cooked. Certainly the place is beautiful, elegant, spacious, clean with a lovey and stylish  décor. It was a nice surprice to find out at second floor a gigantic portrait of a smiling Rita Hayworth on the brick wall and, next to the restrooms, three charming Greek-style amphorae as washbasins, with a bright-red neon sign 'bacio' (kiss). Reasonable prices. Service must be tutored. Recommended

review_preview: This was a matter of being in the right place at the right time. My wife and I were hungry, it was about 1:30 pm, and we didn’t know where to go to get a good lunch in Madrid. But, there it was! Steakburger.We...

But, there it was! Steakburger. We were seated immediately and we ordered cheeseburgers and drinks. The service was efficient, but not very friendly. But, it was efficient.  The beer was cold and tasted great. And then came our burgers. They were both absolutely delicious! Cooked perfectly, they consisted of high quality beef and were accompanied by very tasty perfectly crisped french fries. Our lunches were delicious! I think this could be a top-notch lunch restaurant with just a little more friendliness shown by the wait staff. I would definitely recommend!

review_preview: I visited here three times to eat during my stay in Madrid. Out of all the tapas bars I visted. (And there were a lot) This was by far the best. You are greeted very warmly by the staff behind the bar and a very...
review_full: I visited here three times to eat during my stay in Madrid. Out of all the tapas bars I visted. (And there were a lot) This was by far the best.  You are greeted very warmly by the staff behind the bar and a very lively atmosphere as you walk down the steps into the place.  The serving staff are very helpful if you are not sure on what to order, you also get a complementary snack when you order drinks too. As for the food, I highly recommed the goats cheese, it was full of flavour.  The cod with shrimp I had on my last visit is also worth mentioning, the cod was cooked to perfection and you get a slight kick of heat right at the end. The only downside to this bar is the size, it only has ten tables.  Because of it's high ratings (and deservedly so) it does get very busy during peak periods, not just tourists like myself but locals too.  I would recommend making a reservation or expect to have to wait at the bar for at least 15-20 minutes, 30 at most.  Also it's not really a place if you are a vegetarian, from memory I think it only has two dishes that don't contain meat. Even though Tripadvisor says it's vegetarian friendly (you have been warned)  All in all a very pleasant experience and well worth a visit for every traveller to Madrid.

review_full: I have to disagree with the generally positive reviews. I found this restaurant very generic and the service indifferent. review_full: After walking around Madrid for a while looking for a good Tapas experience, we stumbled into this place. It has great style and even better food. We walked in about 11pm on a Sunday looking for a tapas restaurant that didn’t specialize in Jamon and cheeses (because we just had that for lunch). The place was packed, which was a good sign. Anytime sooner would’ve required a reservation. Our waiters Jorge and Mauricio did a terrific job helping us order and spoke English very well. The menu was in dual language which helped too. When visiting a restaurant for the first time, we like to cut to the chase and get to the highlights and they helped us do just that. We got the tuna, the eggplant chips and the pork tenderloin with Sangrias. Then we got the hot chocolate dish for dessert. All were excellent! The dishes were unique and incredibly flavorful. Very fulfilling experience!

review_full: Visited with my husband and two children on a Friday night at 7.15pm and the outside was already busy. We sat inside (my daughter hates the smoke) and the food was delicious and the service was friendly and excellent. Expect to pay €8-€11 for a racion (per plate of food) we went for the cheese special (rich and super tasty) the Iberian meat in a Chinese style sauce (the most tender cut of meat ever) my son chose the chicken cigarillos (tastes like super thin spring rolls) and my young daughter chose the caramelised chicken roll. We also went on to order the squid strips but couldn't manage to finish them. We were served bread with our meal and crisps and nuts with our drinks before we ordered. The drinkers outside were being given tapas with their drinks. Would come here again in a heartbeat. So rare to find a high rating place on Trip advisor where the service is still exceptional. Remember that food is never served all at once but one/two at a time to share.

review_preview: Okay, I spent 4 and a half week in Madrid and I visited this restaurant 5 or 6 times during my stay. So I think I can write an honest and fair review. The reason I was in Madrid this long was for a study...
review_full: Okay, I spent 4 and a half week in Madrid and I visited this restaurant 5 or 6 times during my stay. So I think I can write an honest and fair review. The reason I was in Madrid this long was for a study course and the reason to visit a burger bar, was to be able to eat "normal food" in stead of all the tapas that Madrid is filled with. Don't get me wrong, I don't think there is something wrong with tapas, but I don't like to eat the same thing all the time. Anyways, the first time I visited the Steakburger Bar Atocha, was also in my first week in Madrid. I was looking for a place where I could eat, but also where I could take out my study books and study in peace. I found this quite little corner in the restaurant and made my seat comfy with all the cushions they have. I sat there at about 17:00h. (a little early for Madrid, but normal for the place where I live) so the place was nearly empty. During the evening it got more busy, until it was completely full and every table was occupied. Even though I was holding a table all alone, sitting there, studying (I had a burger in between and some coffee), the waiters did not beg me to leave at all. I left the place after 23:00. The day after I scored a 9 out of 10 on my exam, so from that day on, Steakburger Bar Atocha was my lucky study place :P  And indeed, every time I had an exam at school, I went to the Steakburger Bar to eat and study, at the same table in the same corner, keeping the table all by myself even during rush hours and never got I any annoying look, or remark from the waiters. Instead, they started to recognize me and showed interest in the study I was doing, which was a Cocktail Bartender study. One of the waiters told me he liked to shake cocktails as well and we got a good click together. I even invited him to my table when his shift was over, so we could talk about cocktails and other stuff. He gave me a very nice recipe for a passion fruit version of a Maitai. In the end, I scored big time on all my exams, so I really believe eating at this Steakburger Bar brings you good luck. For the rest, I can assure you will love the burgers they serve. They use good meat and you can choose between Beef or Ox burger. You can also choose what size burger you like, from small to XXL. The money you pay for it, is fair. Not too expensive, also not cheap, but I think it is right. Anyway, let me sum up the good things about this Steakburger Bar. + Good Luck Bar + Good music (they play lots of madonna, 70ties, pop, music that gays love and that is always good music) + Good burgers, well proportioned, nice meat + You can choose between beef and ox + Fair prices + They serve cocktails as well + Friendly service + Comfy cushions to adjust your seat + Relaxed atmosphere  + Mixed public (single ppl, couples, families, tourists, Madrileens) + Gay friendly  + You can pay by credit card + There is an outside terras  + It is next to Atocha Trainstation + It is next to Reina Sofia Museum + It is at walking distance to the districts of Lavapies, Salamanca and Retiro I promise, you will love this Steakburger Bar. I sure will visit it again next time when I will travel to Madrid. I don't know when that will be, but I sure hope this restaurant will still be there. Sincerely Tommy

He had not eaten half of either steaks that were cooked, in both cases he had barely touched them. I tried both the first steak and potatoes and they were as he described. The steak was changed but no effort was made to change the potatoes and when he raised this, we waited 10 minutes and gave up when nothing came. Yes we were offered a reduction of the bill but in both cases that steaks were brought to my friend, they were barely touched. In addition, the staff gave us shots of liquor at the end as a token. We did not touch these, paid our bill and left. I was reasonably happy with my meal, I wasn't happy that I could not eat with my friend as his meal was not the same. My friend and I were not rude to either the staff or other diners, but my friend was obviously unhappy with his meal and informed staff accordingly.   I am also saddened and annoyed at the lies and inaccuracies in your response to his review. We come to Madrid regularly but will not eat with you again.

title_review: One of the Most Memorable Dining Experiences of a Lifetime!
review_preview: Our reservation was to be cancelled because of a technical difficulty (there was some painting that had been done in the bar) -- but we didn't check our email.  And I am so glad we didn't!  They allowed us to dine and all I can...
review_full: Our reservation was to be cancelled because of a technical difficulty (there was some painting that had been done in the bar) -- but we didn't check our email. And I am so glad we didn't! They allowed us to dine and all I can say is that it was a once in a lifetime experience... The service was elegant, and enhanced our evening. The food was fabulous -- so unique, and truly memorable! Loved the croquettes and tempura vegetable appetizers. The 'Iberian Prey' (pork) with goat cheese and apples was truly enjoyed by my husband. And my oxtail was something that I doubt I will ever experience again, except maybe in heaven. Now I'm sorry I didn't meet the chef... We didn't have room for dessert, but received a wonderful complimentary liquor made from the symbolic strawberry tree of the Madrid coat of arms (not so much a liqueur but more similar to a Canadian icewine). I doubt that the restaurants at The Hotel Ritz or The Westin Palace could do this well at this value! And make you feel so welcome. Please do not miss the opportunity to have dinner here. Our whole experience will be savoured for years to come.

review_full: El mini bar Our last day in Madrid and we found this little gem on TripAdvisor as it was very close to our hotel. It was raining so we could only have sit inside and it was busy, but as this is usually a good sign we decided to wait at the bar for a table. The staff were great, they gave some snacks to eat with our drinks and pretty soon we had a table. We asked for a recommendation on what to have for our lunch and it sounded great so we went with it. We weren't disappointed! We ordered the Cheese which was a hot skillet of melted cheese with a sticky tomato relish, pesto and olive oil in different areas, kind of like a four seasons pizza made entirely out of cheese. Served with some fresh bread. The soft rind was left on in parts and melted to an amazing chewy texture. It was incredible!  The second dish was the Wild Boar, essentially pulled pork wrapped in thin pastry and fried, like a large spring roll made entirely out of meat. The Boar has a distinctive flavour, quite different from normal pork and it was also really nice. Very rich so I couldn't have eaten much more. Maybe not the healthiest food but who cares, we're on holiday! Service and staff were excellent, food was amazing, prices were reasonable. Loved this place.

This time I went for the fixed price lunchtime menu. Within a few hours I felt unwell and my delayed flight home was sheer hell as I clearly had classic food poisoning symptoms (...as a qualified Microbiologist I think I know this). I hadn't eaten anywhere else, so unfortunately the rave review I was going to give Rosi la Loca has rapidly evaporated. The staff were extremely friendly and were working very hard. Perhaps I could have eaten here a hundred times and not had a problem, but I can only speak from the experience I had which left me off work for a day and lamenting our decision to return for the second lunchtime visit which ruined my memories of a weekend in Madrid.  For that reason I cannot recommend. Pays your money, takes your chance I guess....

Although like most traditional tabernas this place is quite small by UK standards it doesn't let you down with the quality of the food. We had a mixture of tapas and paella (which was worth the wait in cooking time). Every dish we tried was well presented and hot. The fish mousse was very tasty and the octopus was quite a large portion. The ham croquettes were hot and tasty and the mixed paella (seafood, chicken and veg) was enough 2 people and a reasonable price also (20 euro's). I think the only thing we could pick at was the fact that for us the coffees let us down, unless you're a fan of small strong nesspresso coffees. Miss this and miss out!

review_preview: I stopped by Oven on a lark after a long day of errands. The prices were very reasonable but It definitely showed in the quality. I ordered a simple pasta dish with tomato, eggplant, and mozzarella. The tomato sauce was tasty enough but the eggplant...
review_full: I stopped by Oven on a lark after a long day of errands. The prices were very reasonable but It definitely showed in the quality.  I ordered a simple pasta dish with tomato, eggplant, and mozzarella. The tomato sauce was tasty enough but the eggplant pieces were small and hard to find. And the biggest disappointment was the mozzarella. Considering this is a “mozzarella bar” I was expecting some nice chunks of mozzarella, but I couldn’t see any cheese at all. I even asked the waiter if it was the correct dish and if there was mozzarella in it. He assured me there was but I never found any evidence of it. I tried to compensate by adding parmesan, but the stuff they had on the table was a kind of cheap, fake, sawdust parmesan, it wasn’t real cheese.  Service was friendly enough though I had to ask several times for the bill. All in all, it was a pretty disappointing experience. The food seemed to be an experiment by the ownwers in how to wring the most money out of their customers while offering the least acceptable food. I have an apartment nearby but won’t be back. I think they must survive off the tourist trade due to their location on Gran Via.

title_review: The Best Tapas, our best meal in Madrid
review_preview: We deliberately came here for lunch (with the high recommendation from Trip Advisor). Food: We ordered a Torreta De Huevos (Torreta Egg with sliced roasted potatoes), Bacalao (salt cods with prawns), 1/2 rabas (squid rings), a strawberries mojito, a toffee cheesecake and a bottle of...
review_full: We deliberately came here for lunch (with the high recommendation from Trip Advisor).  Food: We ordered a Torreta De Huevos (Torreta Egg with sliced roasted potatoes), Bacalao (salt cods with prawns), 1/2 rabas (squid rings), a strawberries mojito, a toffee cheesecake and a bottle of water.  The Torreta egg potatoes was the star of the day. It came in a pot with large portion. The egg yolks were still runny and lovely. The roasted potatoes were hot and crispy. The aubergine and parma ham added a bit of extra taste to the texture and it was a perfect dish. The Salt cods with prawns came in 4 pieces each and they were fantastic too. The butter coated cod were crispy outside and the fishes were very moist inside, they melt in my mouth and were not oily at all. The prawns were also fresh and delicious when dipped into the olive oil. The squid rings was supposed to be a tapas as it cost only 5 Euro, but the portion was surprisingly big. The squids were hot, meaty and crispy and it married so well with the freshness of the salad dressing. The strawberries mojito was another amazing cocktail as I never had mojito with strawberries before. Everything was outstanding and tasty. (I forgot to add that it came with sliced of breads and cheese canapé (on the house))  Service: The staffs were very friendly and helpful. The female staff explained to me patiently about each dish from the menu and she gave us good recommendations. She also warned me that I ordered too much initially. The rest of the staffs were also very kind and kept checking whether we were happy during our meal. The food were served fast to the table. The service was 5 stars.  Restaurant: El Mini Bar is a very low key restaurant which located at the basement. From the exterior, it's hard to tell that it is a restaurant. However, the interior design is lovely and cosy. It is a bit dark as it looks like a bar (which it is) rather than a restaurant, but I love it. I also like the portraits of celebrities and presidents on the wall. The seats and tables are comfortable too. I felt very relax and cheerful dinning there. Price: Bacalao (13), Torreta (9), Rabas (5), Mojito (7), Water (1.5), toffee cheesecake (4.5). A full belly lunch for two people cost less than 40 Euro (+ tips, which I gave a lot (10 euro) because I was extremely satisfied). It's been the cheapest meal we had in Madrid but its food quality and quantity were the best. In summary, the food quality here was great, it's cheap, and the service was flawless. The only slight downside was the restaurant at the basement, as some people would prefer to sit under the sunshine or outdoor. It's my best restaurant in Madrid and it was also the best Spanish meal I had in my life. It deserves a 10 stars rating if Trip Advisor allows me. 100% recommended! Wish I will return one day. It's perfect!

review_preview: Positives:Our server Sandra was so accommodating, friendly and attentive. The bread was good and plentiful. My husband loved the Cosmo. At the end of the meal they provided cookies and lilac flavored candy.Now the food Review: It wasn't good. We ordered the stew...
review_full: Positives: Our server Sandra was so accommodating, friendly and attentive. The bread was good and plentiful. My husband loved the Cosmo. At the end of the meal they provided cookies and lilac flavored candy. Now the food Review:  It wasn't good. We ordered the stew available on Weds and Fri evening which was billed as the specialty of the house and a tradition carried over from the founder of the restaurant. It came out as very dry meat (and body parts from various animals) on top of garbanzo beans with a boiled carrot and potato thrown in. I don't know which was grossest: the chunk of blood sausage, the chunk of completely well done dried out beef or the giant pig ear in the middle of the plate.  As I am writing this review, I am finding it hard to believe that A) I actually ate some of it and B) how utterly gross it was.  The other problem is the very limited menu selection. There were only 4 or 5 main entree choices and unfortunately I the chose the house specialty for the evening. Perhaps the other menu selections are better but I can only share my experience.

review_preview: As it was close to our hotel we went there for dinner- based on the very positive reviews on Tripadvisor. I have to say I would be amazed if there are not many more than 10 restaurants which are better than this in Madrid. The...
review_full: As it was close to our hotel we went there for dinner- based on the very positive reviews on Tripadvisor. I have to say I would be amazed if there are not many more than 10 restaurants which are better than this in Madrid. The waiting staff were generally keen but seemed vague and unsure what to do-and when to do it. They didn't speak English well (or at all) and took a very long time to take our drinks order- then ages to bring the drinks. The bread arrived with- out butter and we had to ask twice for it. The food (when it finally arrived) was average to good - but not great. No wine list ever appeared - apart from about half a dozen wines mentioned at the end of the food menu. With some difficulty I ordered a piccolo bottle of cava- that then disappeared never to be seen again -although there was still about 40% of the contents left. So, although we enjoyed our meal - this was hardly an A grade restaurant to appear in the same company as those with Michelin stars. If this is what you want suggest you go elsewhere.

My advice is to stick to the more traditional Spanish restaurants and don't bother with this place.

review_full: We read about the place in TripAdvisor but were not committed to trying it. However, we ended up just around the corner and decided to pop in. We were so glad we did. All the food we saw looked delicious. The dishes we ordered were spectacular. We had the squid strips. The cornmeal crust was crispy and crunchy and not greasy. The squid was incredibly tender. It squid cane on a bed of salad with a light aioli sauce on it. A nice contrast of tender and crunchy, hot and cold. We moved onto the pankitos. They were like chicken tenders served in a paper cone and with three sauces. Like the squid they were juicy and hot encased in a crisp crunchy deep fried coating. The three sauces were lovely. We saved the grilled goat cheese for last as recommended by two young lads from Manchester. They were so right. The cheese was very smooth and melty. We could not get enough of the tomato jam. I am glad we reserved some of our table bread to soak up the yumminess. Manners prevented me from licking the plate clean. Although truth be told, if my family wasn't with me I would have.  We also ordered a bocadilla. Warm crusty bread cradling the fragrant and fatty Serrano ham. By itself it would have been satisfying. But suffering from comparison to the other dishes, it was merely delicious.  Oh and the mural of Freddie Mercury on the wall of the men's room was an added surprise. Thanks fellow reviewers. It was a good call.

review_preview: We were in Madrid for a long weekend and chose this restaurant to celebrate my birthday. We chose very well.It is a smart restaurant, spacious and nicely decorated.We were presented with an amuse bouche of chicken pate served with crispy toast. For a...
review_full: We were in Madrid for a long weekend and chose this restaurant to celebrate my birthday. We chose very well. It is a smart restaurant, spacious and nicely decorated. We were presented with an amuse bouche of chicken pate served with crispy toast.  For a starter my wife and I shared the tuna tartare. This was more than enough for two and really lovely.  For mains my wife had the cod and I had the sea bass on a skewer. This was presented and filleted by the waitress at the table. Both our mains were lovely, generous and beautifully presented. For dessert we shared the chocolate bomb. Lovely.  We both had coffees and were presented with a complimentary liqueur.  You are charged €2,50 for bead and €4 for a bottle of water, which I know niggles some people. I would say that a bottle of wine at this restaurant starts at just €10 which is amazing for a restaurant of this quality. We had a very nice dry white for just €14. Throughout the service was very, very good. For three courses, a bottle of wine and coffees we paid €103 which is extremely goid value for the setting, service and excellent quality of food. I would recommend this restaurant or a special occasion but equally you could have an excellent two course meal here any night for a very reasonable price.

Highly recommend and really good value.

review_full: Been to oven many times and never been thrilled by the staff but usually just came back as good enough food. How times have changed. My experience at oven last night was like no other. Staff being slow, rude and inconsiderate of customers. Not only was the service unbelievable slow but when staff eventually came to take order or deliver drinks/ food they just come down drop everything and run away. Since it was first time for my partner to experience oven we decided to get a starter, when still eating starter the mains arrived. When these arrived the female waiter attempted to remove the unfinished starter, when I said we were still eating she let out a big sigh, basically dropping plate on table and storming off. This was not the first time in this experience my partner and I have felt that the staff did not want any customers to be their and them not to be working. Even the staffs attitude to tasks, for example when I asked for a spoon with pasta I waited over 15 mins till I eventually got up and asked another waiter.  The food was average but nothing to call home about. It was over priced and we left feeling v v disappointed. A few months ago I recommended oven to everyone but lots of great restaurants in Madrid no point wasting money at one that isn’t good anymore.

They carefully explained every dish and even had some interesting stories to tell about them. The place itself is also very well set-up. You might not like how it is set-up, I personally liked it very much but I recognize that the style could be seen as outdated for some. To me it added to the idea that this is a restaurant about Madrid.  The food was excellent. Portion sizes were just right, the dishes were all very well presented, and you could tell that there was abundant love and quality in all of them. All in all, don't think twice about it, this is perhaps the best restaurant in many aspects in Madrid, and definitely the one that gives you most bang for your buck.   Thank you to the restaurant and its staff for what they do!

review_full: Found this place by pure luck, passing by after shopping and in need of a quick bite. When we entered, the place got my attention right away with its ultra trendy design, buzz and nice smell of food from the kitchen located at the side of the ground floor. We were greeted right away and shown to the table, explained all and got an english version of the menu. We chose the Burrata Iberica with a bit of bread, bottle of Tempranillo from Ribera del Duero, Prosciutto pizza and Burrata y Jamón Iberico pizza. Starter arrived quite fast and was already a great sign of a good choice. Full of flavour in great combination of cheese and jamon, bread still warm as brought fresh from the oven. We managed the starter in no time and moved onto the pizzas. As 38 years old pizza lover I have quite a few pizzas under my belt;))) and still this was something I would call the best pizza of my life (talking about the Burrata y Jamon iberico). Melted burrata together with warm jamon, melting on its top, together with couple of fresh basil leaves.. absolute treat.. After finishing the pizza, we ordered couple of desserts. Tiramisu and Biscotti al Forno. The later was the winner there, again full of flavours and an absolute delight, accompanying the well tasting coffee too. The place is very neatly made, nice decor, great lights, kitchen on display, toilets in a great design with nice idea of the deep sinks, plus very nice view at grand via. Service wise, fully staffed and easy to get attention of anyone when needed, needless to say that everyone was very friendly and polite with genuine smiles. I guess working in a place where you’re proud of what you’re serving makes a huge difference for both sides, the customer and staff. To summarise it, the bill was a great surprise as well as with water, bottle of wine, starter, 2 pizzas, 2 coffees, 2 desserts and bread came to €68.. With the quality of ingredients the value is definitely great and worth of visiting and coming back again and again!;) Thank you!!

review_full: Having saved el minibar as one of my must try places to try tapas in madrid, I quickly checked into my hotel and headed straight here to satisfy the travel hunger. On arrival we recieved a lovely greeting and once I quickly used up my total Spanish vocabulary in around 1 minute which we all had a laugh at we got a table near the bar. There is some lovely art around the place and the general vibe in the place is relaxed and enjoyable. We ordered some sangria each which was delicious and is up there with the best ive tried of the mini tour of Spain I am currently on. We were also given some aperitifs while we browsed the menu which were very tasty. Toastado with salmon. Our waiter gave us an english menu (gracias!) and proceeded to make some recommendations of their popular dishes. We had the wild boar which comes wrapped in a thin pastry and topped with a creamy mushroom sauce over about half of it which was perfect as the pastry stayed crisp and was not too rich. We also had the calamari, steak slices and a main course of what I think was battered cod sliced into 4 with a large prawn on each piece of cod lying in a bed of garlic sauce. We were brought some bread which was perfect for mopping up the plates and washed it all down with another glass of the delicious sangria. I think the bill (without tip) came to around 42euros. Good value for delicious tapas. Will return here when next in Madrid.

If you find yourself in Madrid, and enjoy food based on the culture where you are, please please go see the staff at GastroVia61, you will not be disappointed. title_review: One of the worst restaurant experiences I’ve ever had
review_preview: We went last year with some friends to celebrate my birthday, from a recommendation from a friend who said that it was “looking to get a Michelin Star”. It was literally the worst restaurant experience I’ve ever had. I don’t think it’s fair to only...
review_full: We went last year with some friends to celebrate my birthday, from a recommendation from a friend who said that it was “looking to get a Michelin Star”. It was literally the worst restaurant experience I’ve ever had.  I don’t think it’s fair to only bag places for the stuff they do wrong so I’ll start with the positives- the presentation of the food was very creative, like “master chef” and presented in a Michelin Star way (ie explaining each dish, the ideas behind it and how to eat it etx). The restaurant was clean.  Now for the rest. We were a party of four people and on the menu we were offered two options. The long menu and the short menu. The same food in both and one with a couple of extra dishes. Turns out one of the people with us doesn’t eat seafood. And quite a few dishes in the menu contained seafood. The staff refused to change any of the dishes or offer any alternative. It was explained that she wasn’t “obliged” to eat anything but the menu was offered to a full table, ie she could have not ordered anything otherwise. So the only three options available were: all of us leave without eating (this option meant paying a large amount anyway, as a “depósit”), for the three of us to eat and for her to watch and maybe eat something later, or for all of us to order the full menu and for her to just leave the dishes without eating them. So we ended up ordering menus for everyone.  The first “dish” was a “caldo” that was very good. It had an Asian type flavour and was well presented and elaborated.  The rest of the dishes were very well presented (as I’ve mentioned above) and mostly were inedible. We tried different dishes (like tendons) which were very creative and not pleasant to eat at all. I’m not a fussy eater at all (I’ve eaten insects, live prawns, etc) and many of the dishes we couldn’t finish, despite being hungry. Our friend who didn’t eat seafood could only eat certain dishes anyway and even those weren’t edible. So of the whole menu, there were dishes that were unedible and those which were edible and not good. For the whole meal we were trying to look for positive things to say about the food (i support and respect creative cuisine) and couldn’t. The waitress asked us for our opinion of each different dish and it was obvious (by us not finishing the food) that we weren’t impressed by the dishes. She seemed surprised and insinuated that we were in the wrong because their dishes were amazing (according to her). At the end of the meal we set to pay (the restaurant is very expensive, especially considering our experience) and we expressed our deception between our expectations of how the experience would be and how it was. We were then insulted by the chef, the waitress and told basically that we were wrong and didn’t appreciate their food and that we had the option to leave at any time (after paying the “deposit” for the reservation anyway).  The end of the experience was that We paid a large bill for really bad food and obnoxious service. With so many amazing restaurants in Madrid I would suggest that people spend their money in other restaurants.  Literally the worst dining experience I’ve ever had
