review_preview: So they are famous and you have to stand in a line outside the place waiting for your turn to arrive. When you get to the bouncer, he tries to be funny while waiting, and asks questions... to entertain you? Really, I don´t want to...
review_full: So they are famous and you have to stand in a line outside the place waiting for your turn to arrive. When you get to the bouncer, he tries to be funny while waiting, and asks questions... to entertain you? Really, I don´t want to be asked where I am from or why I am in Madrid.  The magic moment arrives that you are allowed to get into the place - and get rid of the bouncer and his questions. Ok, drinks are excellent, presentation is beautiful, water is also served with snacks that are often refilled.  In the beginning, there is A LOT of noise; music is loud and people have to scream to each other to be heard. Suddenly they turn up the music volume and from that moment on, it becomes impossible to have a conversation with the people you are with. So you end up looking at what is going on around or your cellphone. There is not a fixed style of music, so it goes from the typical music you hear at street festivals to some old songs.  I expected much more of this " famous " place. At least, I expected to have the possibility to talk with the ones I was with without being bombarded with tasteless music at full blast. All is all, for what I got, it was very expensive.

review_full: Have eaten Spanish food in Asia and in Europe, this is the best place to eat this type of cuisine.  Ate dinner here twice as the food quality is good. review_full: A bartender in Madrid had mentioned that Salmon Guru was a great bar and that on my next trip to Madrid I should try to go there. As it happens, David, who embodies what a bartender should be by anticipating what a client wants, now works there. I waited in line to go in for about 15 minutes (Madrid is very respectful and strict about complying with fire codes and the maximum persons allowed inside a restaurant or bar) and it was worth it! The service is exceptional (thank you, David, you are the best!!!), the bartenders work hard (I can attest to how hard David and Filippo, another bartender, worked), and the drinks were creative, beautiful works of art and simply delicious! The support staff, like Estefanía, who brought the bill, and another David, who was attentive about providing water and good potato chips to customers, couldn’t have been nicer. And, last but not least, I was truly surprised at the prices. Such drinks would cost a lot more in New York, Washington, D.C. and San Francisco. And they wouldn’t have been as beautiful!

title_review: Amazing cocktails. A must do In Madrid.
review_preview: My mum and I were staying at the Catalonia des Cortes Hotel and I was looking for a cocktail bar nearby. Luckily this place was less than 100m from the door and was the best find of the holiday. This bar is very near to...
review_full: My mum and I were staying at the Catalonia des Cortes Hotel and I was looking for a cocktail bar nearby. Luckily this place was less than 100m from the door and was the best find of the holiday. This bar is very near to the Plaza Santa Ana and we visited on a Sunday evening around 19.00. The bar isn't huge and luckily we were able to get a seat. An unassuming exterior does not prepare you for inside; quirky decor, cool music and very strong drinks. The menu was all in Spanish but we did a fairly good job of deciphering what was what. The staff were amazing; a constant stream of crisps to snack on and topping up our water glasses from a duck shaped jug. The drinks are fantastic; one of mine was called the flamingo and came in an appropriately shaped mug and was delicious. Loving the atmosphere so much we stayed for 2 drinks each- be warned, they are using the real deal spirits here and the drinks are strong. We could only manage a salad for dinner after our liquid pre- dinner drinks. We were the only tourists here and seemingly the only people who didn't know all the staff on first name terms but they were so welcoming and attentive. We were devastated that we found this place on a Sunday and could only have one visit- they are closed on Mondays. Drinks cost around €10, so about the same price you'd pay in an English city for a cocktail. You can get cheaper drinks in Madrid but I would go back to Madrid just to go here again.

review_preview: We had an amazing experience at Burnout! We were initially standing outside the restaurant to look at the menu for the following day and we were invited in to the restaurant just to experience the atmosphere and enjoy their delicious potato chips. Little did we...
review_full: We had an amazing experience at Burnout! We were initially standing outside the restaurant to look at the menu for the following day and we were invited in to the restaurant just to experience the atmosphere and enjoy their delicious potato chips. Little did we know we were greeted by their amazing chef, Aldo! When we shared that my fiance was vegetarian he invited us to come back the following day and although a vegetarian burger is not on the menu, he said he would make one for us! We came back and had an even better experience. He created a black bean burger for my fiance from scratch that was filling and so delicious. I had a burger from the menu and it was also cooked to perfection, with great fries, and some of the best guacamole I've ever had. Everything on their menu is made fresh, and that was evident with the first bite into my burger and guacamole. We also had nachos and the chili was also delicious. In addition to the great food, the staff was just wonderful, they were friendly, and SO accommodating. We asked if they had sangria, they didn't have any but they made a fresh glass for us! The restaurant overall has a cool and chill vibe. They have some great art on the walls and good music. I would absolutely recommend this place!  This restaurant is a perfect example of Ask and you shall receive!

review_preview: My partner and I were standing in front of Burnout deciding whether we wanted to enter when Chef Aldo welcomed us in and offered us water and chips at no cost. We started chatting with him and when I told him I couldn't eat there...

We started chatting with him and when I told him I couldn't eat there because I'm a vegetarian, he promised to make me a veggie burger if we returned the following day. We returned the following day and as promised, he purchased ingredients to make me a veggie burger and they made us sangria (although it's not on the menu). The food was so fresh and delicious. My partner loved her burger and fries. We also had carrot cake and it was the best carrot cake I've ever had! Chef Aldo and his colleagues made us feel loved and welcomed. Although it was a burger and fries at a burger joint, the service was comparable to the service I received at top steakhouses in NYC. If we return to Madrid, we're definitely going to Burnout at Calle Valverde 6! Thanks Aldo!!!

Burnout has just recently reopened after under going a refurbishment. It has a really nice ambience.  The burgers were cooked to perfection. You will not be disappointed Aldo will Make sure of that! The Oreo milkshake was better than the English versions. The vinto tinto and beer were refreshingly good.  Make sure you leave room for the delicious dessert. We had Aldo's own freshly baked carrot cake, chocolate brownie cake and ice cream. The adults finished off with a very strong Apértif We rolled out of there about 11pm.  My son said that was the best service he had ever had.  That was a truly memorable meal for the last night of our Madrid holiday. Thank you Aldo and team from Michael, Jay, Claire and Junior.. "My wife and kids"

We sat downstairs which is perhaps less appealing but this is not high end dining, its good everyday food. We started with Mozarella injected with pesto. Very tasty - but beware quite filling, then we had the pork fillet with blue cheese and apple sauce, and the ubiquitous Heuvos Rotos. The pork was the star - very tender and a surprising mix and balance of flavours. Most people that visit go for the paella which I am told is very nice (but also quite expensive). My advice is to take the advice of the staff - Alex did a great job of guiding us through, wish we had settled on all his recommendation as the two we had were great. Hes a nice guy too. Checkout the sister restaurant inClan if you have time - a previous trip for us, nice too, but this place gets my vote as the best.

review_full: Enjoyed a fantastic evening at Salmon Guru. Arrived before 9pm, there were a few tables of people already filled. We were warmly greeted and offered a table. The seating is lounge style with a long bench/booth along the wall and individual seats and tables, there is also bar seating.  We ordered two of their house cocktails and the hummus, then another round of cocktails and a selection of plates. Everything was fantastic. The drinks were mixed with fresh ingredients and served with beautiful garnish, the food was delicious and exceeded our expectations. Also important all the staff were attentive and friendly the whole evening.  Recommend everyone visit now, they are just a year old and I anticipate this will grow to a very popular hard to get a reservation establishment as the word gets out.

title_review: A great first meal in Madrid
review_preview: We had dinner at Cacao Restobar on our first day in Madrid in June 2019.  Our experience there was wonderful in every way: excellent food and drink, friendly service, relaxing atmosphere, and reasonable prices.  We highly recommend Cacao Restobar for hungry, travel-weary tourists.We had...
review_full: We had dinner at Cacao Restobar on our first day in Madrid in June 2019. Our experience there was wonderful in every way: excellent food and drink, friendly service, relaxing atmosphere, and reasonable prices. We highly recommend Cacao Restobar for hungry, travel-weary tourists. We had a 20-minute wait for a table, which is not bad considering we arrived without a reservation on a Friday night. Next time, we’ll make a reservation; it’s easy enough to do online. The staff very nicely accommodated for our limited grasp of Spanish. For an appetizer, we shared an arepas sampler. It consisted of two full sized arepas rather than the four small ones in the description; no matter; they were delicious. An arepa is a corn bread round split and filled with a savory mixture of chicken, seafood, or other ingredients. The corn bread used is thicker than a tortilla, but not as cake-like as American “corn bread.” For entrees we had the sliced pork tenderloin with caramelized onions and goat cheese, the cuttlefish with roasted potatoes and salad, and the pabellon criolo (a traditional Venezuelan plate of pulled beef with rice, beans, plantains and a fried egg). The cuttlefish was described as “spicy,” but at our request they scaled back the heat to a mild level. The pork tenderloin was served over scalloped potatoes. The plantains with the pabellon criolo were savory rather than sweet, which combined very well with the other flavors on the plate. For beverages we shared a pitcher (jara) of sangria, and also a non-alcoholic pina colada and a non-alcoholic mango colada. All were quite sweet and served with a sprig of fresh spearmint (note there are plenty of non-sweet beverages available for those who prefer them). For dessert we shared a piece of the tres leches cake that others have recommended. It lived up to our high expectations; very sweet and almost custard-like in texture. Our server (manager? owner?) also brought us small servings of a creamy, coffee-flavored liquor “on the house.” A note about the background music, since it was mentioned by another reviewer: It does indeed consist of covers of Latin American pop standards; we could see the controlling computer monitor from our table, and the mix was clearly titled “Latino Acoustica.” Some songs are repeated in the mix, performed by different artists. It is understandable that the simple arrangements and repetition could be annoying to some; on the other hand, the setting is a restaurant, not a concert, and others might find it interesting to hear different artists’ acoustical takes on well-known tunes. Most important to us was the fact that the volume level was just right: loud enough to hear clearly if one wanted to listen, but not so loud as to hinder conversation. The restrooms are located up a short flight of stairs, and therefore not wheelchair accessible. The restaurant itself also had a few stairs at the main entrance. It is possible there is a second entrance without stairs, but we did not inquire about this.

review_preview: This place is small, with a friendly staff who knows their menu.  Definitely try this place any time of the day.Food: My wife and I came here twice, and in total ordered the patatas bravas, arepas, and croquettes.  All were very well seasoned, and...
review_full: This place is small, with a friendly staff who knows their menu. Definitely try this place any time of the day. Food: My wife and I came here twice, and in total ordered the patatas bravas, arepas, and croquettes. All were very well seasoned, and tasted great. Potatoes are covered in a sweet chili aioli, arepas are freshly made with a variety of options to fill it with. Chicken and beef were fantastic filling choices. Croquettes were as expected, but good. Drinks: Had beer and sangria. Sangria is a must if you enjoy good sangria. They make theirs fresh with brandy and fresh cinnamon, and it really shows in the flavor. Bartenders are A+. They know how to make all kinds of drinks, and are skilled at doing so. I asked for a carrajillo, and they delivered on point! Atmosphere: Small place with a few tables in the front and more in the back. Has a gastropub feel, except they will come to your table to take your order like a restaurant. review_full: First impressions: the outside of this tiny restaurant is so discreet as to be almost non-descript, so you could easily walk past without realising it's there. But that would be a big mistake. Huge (to quote a certain person) The chef here is doing amazing, bizarre, but incredible things with flavours and textures.  After a warm greeting from one of the waitstaff, you sit down, and notice what looks like a weird autumnal floral decoration, in a jug, on your table.  But that turns out of be one of your starters! A "double infusion" of mushrooms, garlic, lemongrass and a whole host of other ingredients (each dish was explained as it was presented, but without either recording it, or asking them to repeat it several times, there is no way I would remember everything), served as a wonderful consommé, the rich flavours of which set the scene for the rest of the evening! I could probably write a review of each course, but given there were 4 starters, bread, fish, 2 meat courses and 2 desserts, I'd be here all night Standouts (although it's like trying to pick your favourite children!) were the Cod, the Duck, the "Lamb Sandwich" and the Mushroom dish with Meringue pieces (not joking) After the Sticky Toffee Pudding with Salted Caramel Ice-cream and curry powder (still not joking), the waitress brought out 2 leaves on a plate, explaining that they were to cleanse the palate before the last course, and that we should not think so much about the flavour as the feeling (?) So, to the wife's comment of "It looks like privet" we chewed away, only to experience the plant equivalent of Space Dust, leaving our mouths tingling - we just burst out laughing at the sheer playfulness of it. All of this is done for €48 for the short menu or €63 for the long - about a quarter of the price you'd pay at somewhere like DiverXO (and without the 6 month waiting list) I can't believe that this place isn't higher up the rankings, or that we were lucky enough to find it, after some random trawling of TA. Do yourself a favour and try it next time you're in Madrid - you won't be disappointed

I was lucky enought to get a table, the place looks nice, the look is modern and rich, without exageration, everything seems to be just right. The waiter arrived and informed me that he would have gone for reduced portions as I was eating by myself and their normal portions are very abundant, which sounded to me like good news and a right start. The starter arrived after a few minutes, croguettes flowers, covered in a delicious Spanish wine sauce, and filled with a tasty and creamy local cheese. title_review: The BEST restaurant in Madrid. Simply phenomenal
review_preview: I speak for both Alcaravea and the sister restaurant Alcaravea Gaztambide in this review, having visited both on numerous occasions during my 6 months in Madrid. I only have great things to say about this place... not ONE negative comment to makeI stumbled upon...
review_full: I speak for both Alcaravea and the sister restaurant Alcaravea Gaztambide in this review, having visited both on numerous occasions during my 6 months in Madrid. I only have great things to say about this place... not ONE negative comment to make I stumbled upon this restaurant thanks to TripAdvisor as it happens. At the time it was in the top three places to eat in Madrid - it still should be! - and as I lived in the center it wasn't difficult to get to.  While the first time we went was on a weekday early evening, so we were able to walk right in, friday to sunday dinners I would suggest booking in advance. Even during subsequent visits, when there were only two of us and we hadn't booked, the warm and welcoming staff were happy to make space even if it meant shifting a few tables.  The first thing I noticed about this place when walking in was the mouthwatering aroma of beautifully cooked Spanish food lingering in the air. In both restaurants the owner would personally seat us, keep conversation flowing throughout the dining experience and always be available for advice and recommendations. The staff all spoke perfect English, and even the owner of the Gaztambide branch who wasn't quite as fluent, would make jokes in Spanglish and recognize me everytime I came back.  Not only is this place perfectly romantic for couples, I went twice with family (just 2-3 of us) and another few times with a massive group of friends, which didn't make the service and food any less personable and punctual. I insisted some of my Spanish friends should book it for their birthdays, and they all raved about it and congratulated me on the fantastic find, all wishing that they had discovered the place years ago in their own hometown. Even my foodie friend whose parents own a restaurant took her family here and they were just bowled over. Which seems to be the general reaction. As for the food, be it recommendations from the staff, or the complimentary 'amuse-bouche' that came with every meal (from many types of warm fresh bread and cheeses, to tangy shots of gazpacho) or the array of amazing desserts (and I learnt that Spain weren't the best at cakes and desserts, perhaps it's their flour.... but this place changed that perception in seconds) It was all absolutely breathtaking. If I didnt have favourites that I would continually choose, I would have loved to get through the entire menu. ahhh the favourites (see pictures)... MUST ORDER:  -Kilo of Kobe Beef Now i'm not a steak/beef/burger fan whatsoever. It's always been too chewy for me, or lacking flavour. So when (only thanks to a recommendation by the staff) we ordered a kilo of Kobe beef, rare and still moo-ing on the plate (at a ridiculously cheap price of £30) which came with potatoes and green peppers, i was a little apprehensive. It was the most succulent, melt-in-the-mouth, delicious meat I had ever tasted. And the portion was so huge, but too delectable to waste. This dish alone is a reason for anyone to come here. -Croquettas (especially the goats cheese and honey) Delicate, perfectly crispy on the outside and silky smooth on the inside. Possibly the best croquettas I've tasted... and I've had a fair few in my day -Calamari Commonly overcooked, chewy and bland. Not this time! Perfection -Desserts Because you couldn't possibly choose as everyone of the desserts are heavenly. But the Tiramisu inside a toblerone is a stroke of genius!!! Even though we were bursting at the seams from all the food, we HAD to have some of this. We ended up waddling home, our bellies pregnant with the tastiest meal I'd eaten in a very long time. But the real icing on the cake was the bill at the end. For such attentive, creative fine-dining the price was extremely reasonable, making Alcaravea free from that 'fine-dining' pretentious nature.  Honest, humble food made with heart and passion. No wonder Spain has been a contender for the best restaurants in the world this past decade. I implore you.... don't miss out.

review_full: We would definitely recommend going to this restaurant for some lovely South American tapas. The food was lovely and fresh and the gentleman serving us was super friendly. But then the nachos came out with cheese on. The waiter was more than happy to take them back and get me a fresh plate without cheese. Then my main didn't come out at all (vegetable strudel). We thought it was because the atmosphere was very relaxed and food came out as it was prepared but by the time my husband and friend had finished their main, we didn't bother to mention it to the waiter nor did we get billed for the item. These are very two minor problems but I didn't think it was fair to give them a perfect score.

review_full: Planned a visit to Madrid from London with my wife and checked out best restaurants on tripadvisor. We got there and been told to wait 10-15 mins so they can sort something out for us. The place was packed. After 10 mins we were seated to a small 2 pers table, but asked before if that is ok with us.  They were opened to a chat in english, but i tried to do it in spanish and i was complimented for it.  Starters come out. Really good. Nothing mind blowing but really good. And then mains. Wow. Had the grilled octopus. Best ever.  Prices are very good but the most important thing is these guys attention to customers. You are number 1 in their eyes, as it should be. They make everybody feel welcome and homely.  All in all i take great pleasure in reviewing this place and giving it top marks.  Well done guys !!! Keep it up!!!

review_full: We had planned to go here on our honeymoon because of the rave reviews on Trip Adviser, but they still aren't enough to speak to the wonders of this place!! The staff were incredible, working through our meager Spanish and making the whole experience fun. The food was out of this world -- we had the nachos, bravas, plantains, and Spanish cheese sticks from the tapas menu. All were fantastic. Then the sangria. The white sangria was the best I've ever had and very seasonal with cinnamon. The manager of the restaurant chatted with us a few times and offered us their homemade liqueur with our check. Also an amazing concoction.  Do not miss Cacao Restobar when you go to Madrid.

We had a bottle of wine to go with it. The portions didn't look big, but they are well measured - you won't be hungry, but not so big as to be off putting. Overall a very pleasant evening - muchas gracias to all the staff!

review_full: We were eating early by Madrid standards due to an early flight the next morning and sat in the bar area. Great ambiance with a fun, inviting interior. Excellent service, too. Some dishes were a hit, others not so much. I highly recommend the Patacones -- flat fried plantains with toppings of avocado cream, pulled pork, and pico de gallo. The arepas were also very good -- basically muffin-sized cornbread circle sandwiches with a variety of fillings. The sauteed mushrooms and garlic were a bit boring and the pulpo a la gallega had been cooked a smidge too long, and I felt was also a bit bland. The octopus sits on a slice of potato with very little seasoning. Although our dishes were not all hits, I do recommend this restaurant. The dishes we liked were truly delicious.

My husband had the fajitas which he said were tasty and I had the prawn risotto which was a little bit light on taste but when the waiter noticed I hadn't eaten it all he said I was only going to pay half because I'd only eaten half - a lovely touch but I felt so bad, he really cared. We had room for dessert - thank goodness, they were amazing, passion fruit pie and a cheesecake - both superb! All in all this is a lively, casual place with good food. review_preview: Delicious food, attentive service, and colorful atmosphere. Our main server, Andres, was polite, attentive, helpful, and spoke perfect English. review_full: Delicious food, attentive service, and colorful atmosphere. Our main server, Andres, was polite, attentive, helpful, and spoke perfect English. We didn’t catch the names of the other staff who were also very helpful, and working very hard to provide excellent service. The smoked octopus was delicious and entertainingly served with a smoky flair. The eggplant fritters were interesting, and the ham croquettes were delicious. Our servers apologized about our paella taking long to arrive, though we really didn’t notice. The staff made multiple efforts to make up for our paella wait time. However, from our seat near the kitchen, we saw how efficiently everyone was working and did not feel at all inconvenienced as we enjoyed our tapas and wine, entertained by the whirlwind in the kitchen. It’s Spain. If the food is taking long, enjoy the atmosphere and drink more wine. We’ve had long waits for paella not worth our time and this was NOT the case here. Their seafood paella is among one of the better ones we’ve had in Spain. House wine was nice, the sangria was tasty though a bit sweet for our taste. Good value and an interesting restaurant worth checking out.

review_full: Myself and my boyfriend went here enticed by the vibrant colours and photos of the food on the online menu. However when we ordered two “super tapas” dishes - a spicy aioli potato dish and the tacos, we were presented with a minuscule bowl containing all of one single potato chopped up into squares. The two tacos were equally tiny, each one smaller than the size of a hand. After seeing the same dish served to the spanish people next to us which was easily double the size, we complained about our bill, to which the waitress immediately and without question amended our bill for the potatoes to the price for the smaller size (not at all for the tacos, despite them being nothing like the picture). Her being totally unsurprised just approved our suspicions that they regularly attempt to scam young tourists like ourselves. If you go here, be sure to check your bill twice or three times and have a good look at what they serve to the Spanish customers compared to yourselves. review_preview: We love local food served in small family restaurants. But we didn't love this. Ultimately we left quite disappointed. (In fairness, we might not have been disappointed had the reviews on Tripadvisors not ranked this so highly. Mind you, we wouldn't have gone at all....
review_full: We love local food served in small family restaurants. But we didn't love this. Ultimately we left quite disappointed. (In fairness, we might not have been disappointed had the reviews on Tripadvisors not ranked this so highly. Mind you, we wouldn't have gone at all. I'm shocked at the Tripadvisor ranking!) We were charged 40 Euro for not much: two coffees, three hot chocolates and five bland sandwiches (small white buns with a bit of ham and crushed tomatoes). The hot chocolate was actually a cup of milk with a packet of nearly flavourless powder to mix in ourselves. The tomatoes tasted and looked tinned. Certainly not fresh local produce. A friendly owner/employee chattered away and handed over cheap trinkets that we would never want to purchase (repeatedly saying "my treat"). We were shocked at the bill (we never received a menu and just acceited the recommended meal, and so we didn't know what the price would be) But we smiled and paid and handed over the usual European tip: the small change. The employee/owner took the tray with the change and with a big smile asked "tip?". But when he saw the small change he was suddenly not so friendly anymore. The smile vanished and he walked away without a word. (Perhaps more generous tips are oftentimes given - and have come to be expected- from non-Europeans.) There were regulars stopping in for coffee so obviously the locals are happy here (we didn't see anyone else dining). There is a large terrace with a shrub surround and a lot of umbrellas, but the street has through traffic.

title_review: I went there with some friends
review_preview: I went there with some friends and unfortunately two of them said the next day they had vomited their dinner. I am not surprised since some of the things we ordered were very far from what I would call authentic Mexican food, unfortunately. I asked...
review_full: I went there with some friends and unfortunately two of them said the next day they had vomited their dinner. I am not surprised since some of the things we ordered were very far from what I would call authentic Mexican food, unfortunately. I asked for enchiladas verdes and was given some tortillas swimming in a sort of cheese or bechamel sauce. A friend of ours ordered some Cochinita pibil tacos and he ate half of one and gave the rest away. I tried one and it wasn’t what it should have been. Pork covered in lard is not cochinita pibil. And I don’t write lard to be funny, the meat was soaked in grease.  The service was nice, or not, depending on the waiter waiting on you. The Spanish waiter was very friendly and nice, whereas his Mexican colleague I guess was having a bad day. Lastly, we waited around 40 minutes between our first course (basically ceviche and guacamole for three) and the main course. When we asked the waiter about our food he left and came back saying it would be coming up shortly, but we still had to wait for it to arrive about 5 more minutes. I don’t think understand why a restaurant of all places would think its ok to leave such a long gap in between courses. As a parting thought, the place really needs to revamp the toilets. The massive spiderweb wasn’t very nice to look, among other things. I wont be going there again or recommended this place to any of my friends. I was very disappointed at the whole experience, to say nothing of my friends vomiting their dinner.

review_preview: What an absolute treat...what a great meal...what a great evening!  Even from the street the upstairs wine shop is elegant and tasteful.  Although we had a feeling Las Carboneras de Lu might be very very nice, we and our friends were in for a stunning...
review_full: What an absolute treat...what a great meal...what a great evening! Even from the street the upstairs wine shop is elegant and tasteful. Although we had a feeling Las Carboneras de Lu might be very very nice, we and our friends were in for a stunning gastronomic and visual treat. The downstairs restaurant could not be more beautiful, refined and romantic. From the bottles enclosed in the staircase to brick wine cellar motif to the soft lighting, we instantly sat down and said around the table, "This place is incredible!" And that's before the service started. And when the service did start, we instantly saw that no detail was left to chance. The staff was extremely well trained and politely attentive without being distracting. We were immediately served a salted edamame, followed by an excellent amuse bouche. We each shared a bottle of Pinot Noir Rose Cava, which was excellent. Lourdes, the co-owner recommended an excellent Madrid-area Ganache. And then the courses started to arrive. My wife shared the stuffed pasta (a thousand apologies to Lourdes and her husband that I don't know the exact name of each dish), while I shared the pate and foie gras plate. Both looked beautiful and were fantastic. Our friends ordered the boneless beef steak, which they couldn't stop raving about. I had the beef cheeks with root vegetables and it was amazing. My wife was served the suckling pig, which was cooked for a loving 9 hours. When she shared a bite, It was one of the best single bites of food I've ever had. My first thought was, "I'd fly back to Madrid just to have this single dish." It really was that good. Ending with dessert, my friend and I had the lemon pie, which was simply exquisite. So good, I forget what my wife had- my friend had ordered a lemon pie as well and we just couldn't stop talking about it. Throughout the evening, the staff could not have been more polite nor more professional. The ladies' dishes were simultaneously removed first, followed by the mens'. Every detail was attended to promptly and politely. We learned that Lourdes and her husband have been open a mere 5 months. They have done an absolutely amazing job with the restaurant and the wine shop. They are absolutely lovely people. If you are in Madrid and you appreciate fine dining, you have to treat yourself to their lovely restaurant. I hope this restaurant and the lovely founders have all the success in the world. You can tell they've poured themselves into Las Carboneras de Lu! Incredible.

review_preview: I stumbled onto Decadente with a few friends on accident —it happened to be right next to the hotel we were staying at. Often times trying out a random restaurant can lead to disappointing results, but that was not the experience this time. It was...
review_full: I stumbled onto Decadente with a few friends on accident —it happened to be right next to the hotel we were staying at. Often times trying out a random restaurant can lead to disappointing results, but that was not the experience this time. It was a fantastic choice . The host, Diego, easily found us a table in the packed dining room. He put us at ease with his charm and attentiveness. It was obvious that the whole staff strives to make their guests’ dining experience the best possible. The dining room is decorated with distressed wood, metals, interesting architectural features, and pleasantly low lighting. It was at the same time romantic and great for a group of friends.  Among other things we ordered croquetas de carabinero (fantastic!), torrenzo con su Corteza, and gambones crujientes (crunchy prawns). The chef clearly knew what he was doing with seasoning and ingredients representative of the region, and all of the plating was beautiful.  Definitely check out the downstairs ultra cool cocktail bar, which slightly resembles an old New York underground bar. It was cozy and intimate, and yet the whole restaurant is lively and fun.  Go here! You won’t regret it. I’ll definitelt be back next time I am in Madrid.

Wine selection was also fantastic. Highly recommend this restaurant. The Spicy Shrimp truly are what dreams are made of!

title_review: Owners make this an unforgettable dinner - best classy gem of a restaurant in Madrid
review_preview: Recently, I had the privilege to take a group of professionals to this restaurant for dinner – we were about 24 persons in total. Well, it’s difficult to explain our overall surprise and pleasure at this establishment, however, I’ll try.  Right from the entry, there’s...
review_full: Recently, I had the privilege to take a group of professionals to this restaurant for dinner – we were about 24 persons in total.  Well, it’s difficult to explain our overall surprise and pleasure at this establishment, however, I’ll try. Right from the entry, there’s a glass rectangle in the floor over which you must step to enter. As you look down, you have a bird’s eye view of a private dining room in the restaurant below. This glass area showcases the place where coal, (for heating the building), was delivered in ages past. Yes, this restaurant has an interesting history. Then you proceed through a small but charming wine store to the staircase which takes you one floor below to the restaurant. Mostly done in brick to resemble a beautiful wine cellar, the restaurant is extraordinarily lovely, with elegant touches everywhere – from wall color to decorations to paintings to stiffly starched table cloths & napkins, to striking table settings. Incredibly pleasing and stylishly furnished. The restaurant consists of several gorgeous interconnecting dining rooms The food was absolutely the best part. Executive chef Lourdes Poveda is a culinary genius, she, along with seven other expert & talented chefs prepare your delicious meals. They spare no detail - everything is freshly prepared, elegantly plated (on striking dinner ware ) and lavishly served. Make sure you observe the chic dinner plates, as a different style is used for each course. We selected a tasting menu of 5 courses + dessert and each one was better than the next. At the end, we couldn’t tell which course we liked best…..they were all delightfully delicious. What an amazing treat! Dessert was good too, the best lemon concoction I’ve ever had - one more pleasing surprise at the end! We will remember this place for a long time to come and find every opportunity to visit each time we are in Madrid. By the way, Executive Chef Lourdes owns the restaurant along with her charming husband who is the extremely knowledgeable and attentive sommelier. He hand selects your wine once he knows your preference, and if you don’t know what you want – all the better because are in for a good surprise. He does know his stuff! During the course of your dinner Executive Chef Lourdes visits your table to ensure your satisfaction. She comments on any given course and encourages your questions. She is just as delightful ad the food she prepares. Service was remarkably impeccable – a couple of times, I dropped my napkin on the floor by my feet. Each time it was noticed, retrieved and a fresh one was returned to me on a platter, beautifully folded and served to me with tongs – no human hands touching it! Price is remarkably moderate for this one of a kind gem in Madrid. If you love superb food and outstanding service, you owe it to yourself to visit.

The idea, to place a restaurant in the cave of a wine merchant is intriguing. The wine cellar itself is just a small room, with about 200 different wines, mainly from Spain and France. We startet with a nice glass of Champagne and they talked us into a wine from the Madrid area to accompany our dinner.  Then they walked us down to the restaurant, it was nearly empty (at 9pm), but during the evening, all tables (about 10 tables) were taken. The chef greeted us and we asked her to suggest something. We started with a small amuse bouche, followed with an excellent zucchini flowers in tempura, filled with bacelao, then Bacelao Negro, quail, tournedos with foie gras and as dessert, lemon pie and torrija de panettone. Our wine “Initio” by Las Moradas de San Martin was excellent and for the sweets we had two glasses of Pedro Ximenez and Moscatel plus two coffees and mineral water. We have been to very good restaurants all around the world, but the “LU experience” was one we will never forget: Outstanding cuisine in a cozy atmosphere, excellent wines, very good service for a very fair price (EURO 172 for two persons). Thank you Lourdes for this experience; we will come back for sure!

review_preview: In Madrid for my cousin’s birthday I wanted somewhere that would be the culinary accompaniment to a morning at the Thyssen. Having chosen Las Carbs on the basis of Trip Advisor reviews we were delighted with our choice. You enter through an upscale wine shop...
review_full: In Madrid for my cousin’s birthday I wanted somewhere that would be the culinary accompaniment to a morning at the Thyssen. Having chosen Las Carbs on the basis of Trip Advisor reviews we were delighted with our choice. You enter through an upscale wine shop and descend into a surprisingly light and airy former coal cellar. Like all good restaurants they do the little things really well - three types of lovely bread, great butter, an amuse bouche of warm edamame peas. The cooking is technically excellent and highly skilful - apparently it takes 20 minutes to debone a quail - roughly twice as long as it takes to eat one. The service was delightful, with the lady chef coming out to explain each dish (there were only around twenty covers on a midweek lunchtime, I doubt she can manage this at the weekends). We trusted wine selection the sommelier and were very pleased. We were trying to refuse pudding when the chef said she had a cheesecake with truffle honey. It isn’t on the menu but should be as it is sweet savoury heaven. Prices are where you would expect them to be for cooking at around about the one Michelin star threshold, which is exactly what you get. Will be back when next in Madrid.

The place is very uptight, in a good sense though. The service is impeccable and on top of you which is not necessarily what we were looking for on that day. The place itself is elegant and exuding good taste everywhere even though is set in an old coal storage place (hence the name). The food is good, nothing that wowed us though and that really was what we went for. Certainly more on the tasting side of things given the size of portions and the level of prices. This is the kind of place you will go with some business partners to drink some amazing wine (the place claim to have one the best bodegas in Madrid) and eat something good. The star of the place are the wines which you are immediately made aware of as soon as you enter the place. The fact of the matter is that we were not there for the alcohol. So given all this we can only review this place given our expectations and experience which undeniably has always a subjective component.

title_review: Such high hopes....dashed by the attitude of the owner!
review_preview: On arrival into this warm and eclectic restaurant, we were warmly greeted into the ‘wine shop’ upon which the sommelier encouraged us to try some local wines so we could pick a bottle to take to dinner.  Once we chose a delicious and recommended tempranillo,...
review_full: On arrival into this warm and eclectic restaurant, we were warmly greeted into the ‘wine shop’ upon which the sommelier encouraged us to try some local wines so we could pick a bottle to take to dinner. Once we chose a delicious and recommended tempranillo, we were taken downstairs to our table. The staff were great with the actual restaurant and dining room lovely; however, the owner had one almighty attitude problem. We started with a shared cheese platter and was then promptly (and I mean literally not more than 5 minutes) followed with zucchini flowers. Both these dishes were delicious! My partner had the sucking pig for his mains which he thought was fabulous and I had the cod. I double checked with our waitress when ordering that it was a fillet with NO bones and she assured me it was.  My first mouthful I found a large bone so called over our waitress (who unbeknown to us was the owner), who said that it would be impossible for the chef to find all the bones without destroying the fish - so clearly, you’ll get some bones and then walked away. My third mouthful had another bone so I called her over again and asked her to remove my plate as I didn’t want it. There was no apology, no offer for another meal, just an argument in front of the other guests justifying the dish before turning and walking away again!  Once my partner finished eating I asked for the manager but was ignored. As we were getting ready to leave, I again asked for the manager and was told our waitress was the owner. She refused to come over to speak with us, so we left. It was such a shame as the rest of the staff were fantastic but her attitude really ruined our night. I’ve worked in fine dining establishments and would never have spoken to or treated my customers like that. It was embarrassing and I ultimately left hungry. Maybe if we had been a group of 20+ people we would have received the fabulous service that others appear to have had although, having said that, the owner doesn't even bother with the reviews or opinions of diners. Hopefully she'll receive enough negative ones to change her attitude!

review_preview: Visited Purnima Thursday night and felt compelled to write a review as the food was outstanding!Decor - Modern and chic. Very tastefully decorated.Food - To start we ordered onion bhaji’s and were given complimentary mini poppadoms and chutneys. On hearing that my wife...
review_full: Visited Purnima Thursday night and felt compelled to write a review as the food was outstanding! Decor - Modern and chic. Very tastefully decorated. Food - To start we ordered onion bhaji’s and were given complimentary mini poppadoms and chutneys. On hearing that my wife loves spice, the waiter brought over a separate curry paste for her which she thoroughly enjoyed. For mains, we asked for advice and the waiter was very happy to learn about what we like, our spice levels etc. We opted for a chicken tikka masala and a chicken vindaloo. We also ordered boiled rice and roti’s.  When the food arrived, the waiter checked that it was to our satisfaction and I commented that both lovely but one dish could be hotter in the spice department. I want to note that the food was delicious and we were happy but the waiter took the dish away as he said the chef will get it to our likening. On return, the dish was perfect, and we were blown away with how much the waiter really cared and went to the effort he did.  The portion sizes were great also, we were offered our leftovers to take away but as we were moving on to bars, we declined but nice touch. We were also given a complimentary mango drink and jelly sweets, again nice touch. Service - Amazing! Wish we had taken note of the waiters name but he was excellent. Very polite and friendly, even understood our Scottish accents! Overall - When we come back to Madrid we will definitely return, that’s if we don’t go back before we head home! You need to visit as this is one of the better Indian restaurants in Madrid.

title_review: Worth a visit. Nice curries-request ´English curry/customer´ if you want something a bit more spicy, great staff.
review_preview: We were a party of 2 having lunch. Overall food is good. Place is really clean. Staff nice and cheery and helpful. Downside, we ordered a bottle of wine which was corked , tasted and smelt dreadful and had to be sent back. I was...
review_full: We were a party of 2 having lunch. Overall food is good. Place is really clean. Staff nice and cheery and helpful. Downside, we ordered a bottle of wine which was corked , tasted and smelt dreadful and had to be sent back. I was told i would have to pay for a replacement but i refused. There was no manager to consult and staff seemed worried about having an unpaid bottle of wine in the system. As none of them drank i couldn´t prove the bad taste to them but i made them smell it and compared it with a same brand but different bottle being used to serve wine by the glass from the bar. It smelt so bad that they eventually gave me another bottle which was fine. I offered them my mobie number if their missing manager wanted to discuss this further.  Apart from that everything was good and i would go back. I´d like to say Hakim was very helpful throughout and speaks really good English as do a few other members of staff.  More detailed info if you need it... There are 3 ´menus´ ( at 11.90, 25 and 35 euros) plus the a la carte. Starters are between 5.50 and 11 euros. Mains between 11.50 ( chicken) to 15 euros ( king prawns dishes). Lamb is around 13 euros. I didn´t have room for dessert so can´t comment on that.  Personally i wasn´t too impressed with the choice on offer in opening price point menu which served bhaji, chicken soup, salad, ( forgot 4th option) and mains such as Dhal, Dhamsak , none of the common more favourable dishes available here but the 25 euros menu showed a lot of promise with bhajis, samosas etc...to choose from and mains such as CTM and madras among others. You also get a veg side dish in this menu along with nan or rice. A dessert or coffee at the end. None of the menus include a drink.  Rice portions are really good. ( 4 euros for plain 5 euros for pilau) Recently we have had to order a 2nd portion of rice - many restaurants are cutting back on portion size - but this time we just ordered 2 straight away as we were really hungry so we were quite surprised when 2 deep pots of rice were delivered to our table so much so we had to bring nearly a whole portion home with us. Nan bread was lovely. Soft , fluffy, freshly cooked. We got 3 medium sized bjajis which were a lovely starter with a choice of 3 sauces, not amazing but ok. We ordered lamb balti and chicken bhuna. Chicken dishes seem to be bigger coming in a wide rounded curry dish where as lamb dishes come in a bucket style pot which has a false base half way up so it seems you get a smaller portion if you order lamb...costs i guess. Anyway both curries were nice, the lamb being the better option but no spice/heat at all even though we asked for ´medium´. As mentioned before the staff were great and took our curries away to make them spicier. Upon returning the smiling waiter said ( inEnglish) please tell the waiter next time that you are English so he can make a note for the chefs who will make you a ´medium´spiced english curry.  More suited for couples, friends and business. Dont think you can get around too easily with a pram and 2 flights of stairs to the loos.

review_full: We went in simply because we were tired, hungry and we loved the window filled with bottle caps. It was a snap decision but we didn't regret it. We immediately loved this place as soon as we set foot in it: it looked cozy, welcoming and absolutely beautiful. It was a pretty small place but that just made it feel intimate, with the retro-looking bar monopolising the entire space and setting a romantic, slightly nostalgic tone. We sat at the table closest to the door and ordered our drinks, which came with the tapas and chips typical of most Spanish restaurants. Next I had the paella with black rice and my boyfriend had the BBQ ribs. My paella was really good but my boyfriend's BBQ ribs were out of this world. I had a few bites out of curiosity and I feel like that taste will never leave my memory. I recommend the heck out of them. The price was decent and the waitress was reasonably nice to us - even though she didn't find much amusement in my short bit of trivia, namely that their WiFi password featured my birth year. I mean, I myself found that pretty amusing, but to each their own I suppose. :D

review_full: Almost a year later, I went back to Purnima again, since the place is right next to my friend's place. They have an awesome lunch special for 13.5 Euros, which includes a drink, first plate, second plate and dessert. We sat outside at the terrace, which was lovely and decorated with plants. The owner and the staff have done a wonderful job on that. I actually met the owner Delawar and the guy was funny and super friendly. He gave us some free shots and additional drinks while we were there. The service was great too. They have these disciplined Indian workers who come by all the time. They speak multiple languages so if you only know English, that won't be a problem. They will be able to service you.  The food was absolutely delicious. I love eating the creamy curry there. I have also tried the Keema Curry before and that was delicious too. After that curry taste, you can finish off with one of their wonderful ice cream dishes. I like the pistachio ice cream. Yummy! The place gets really busy after 2pm, so if you want some peaceful moment, go a bit earlier and you will definitely find seats.  a must try when you are in Goya! pinchetravels.com for more info on my blog.

Except the lady that served us, we didn't feel welcome at all by anyone in the staff including the person who looked like the manager. Here I must say that their behaviour towards non Indians was completely opposite. I could see it from my table how their mannerism changed when they were talking to others. They were more friendly and cordial. With us, they were just loud, rude and curt. To top it all, the food was bad and extremely spicy. I don't remember eating anything which was remotely good. I regret taking my family to this place. Good thing is that we finished in less than 1 hour and went somewhere else to bring in New Years Eve. Pls avoid.

review_full: Stumbled upon this place one tuesday evening when wifey wanted to reward me with a burger. Ended up being the only place we ate twice during our stay in Madrid. The food is excellent, american style. Like others have mentioned, medium might be what you consider rare. Even so I went with rare on our second visit and loved it. It's only as cooked as needs to be, you get what you ask for. The staff is great as well. Even though they're visibly busy (place was packed both times), they're still in a good mood, smiling and laughing. Javier is the only name I got, but he and his co-workers are all very serviceminded and it truly shows. They have options other than burgers too. If you're looking for Something meaty, american style, check this place out.

review_full: I booked this restaurant using the Fork through trip adviser. This was a very simple system and worked well.  The restaurant was amazing. It is one of the best Indians I have ever had. The staff were very helpful when ordering and recommended just one starter to share. We went for onion bhajis which were delicious and just the right amount for 2 of us.  For mains I went for chicken jalfrezi which was delicious. The waitress asked what spice I would like and recommended mild and it was just right. The curries are usually slightly hotter than what we would get in England. My partner went for chicken tikka masala and really enjoyed it. We only went for one rice and one naan to share between us as this was recommended and this turned out to be a perfect sized portion. The rice was huge and we didn’t eat it all between us.  One member of staff turned out to be from our home town so it was nice to talk to him.  Overall this is a lovely restaurant with great food and great staff.  It is just around the corner from the Wizink Center.

review_preview: Steakburger makes a good burger, but they seem to have a different understanding of how much to cook the meat than Americans have. We ordered our two "shy/timido" 1/3 lb burgers medium, but they came out somewhere between medium-rare to rare. There was meat inside...
review_full: Steakburger makes a good burger, but they seem to have a different understanding of how much to cook the meat than Americans have. We ordered our two "shy/timido" 1/3 lb burgers medium, but they came out somewhere between medium-rare to rare. There was meat inside which was barely warmed, with no sign of cooking. Other than that, service was good and the French fries were very good. Ketchup, brown mustard, and mayo were on the table. Coke Zero was served from a glass bottle into glasses with lemon and ice. The interior could almost have been transplanted from the USA, in terms of table size, spacing, and decor. The downstairs seating area had an unpleasant smell which seemed to come from the restrooms; I would have left if that was the only available seating. Overall, a good place to eat American food if you order well.

We ordered the nachos to share for starters which were very good and each ordered a burger with fries for mains. Being British we don’t like uncooked burgers so opted to have them well done. But unfortunately they were very well done and a bit dry, so medium to well would have been much better. They were still tasty, we ordered the tikka masala burger, the Philadelphia burger and the British burger with the fried egg. The children shared the chocolate brownie, which they enjoyed. Less than €90 for 1 starter, 4 mains, 1 dessert, bottle of House red and 4 soft drinks was very reasonable for Madrid.

review_full: Machiavelli would love their sneaky pricing. They put a signboard outside advertising a set menu brunch for 14 euros. You order and eat then comes a bill for 17 euros. review_full: Delighted to find this excellent restaurant so close to our airport hotel, serving simple food cooked to perfection. There is a menu in English if you need it. We sampled 4 dishes from the tapas menu - all made from fresh ingredients - all delicious. Especially liked the black sausage and the pork in tomato sauce. The best though was the fish - simply pan fried with home made chips. This very much a family affair and Pepe head of the clan educated us on the ways of Spanish food and drink. He gave us typed instructions on how to make Sangria and a breakdown of the origin & components of all the dishes we chose. All this delivered in a very entertaining "Pepe style". Before we left we were treated to a nightcap of the house - a kinda Baileys with whipped cream and then he gave us a range of presents from cap to key ring. But the best surprise was the final bill. Given what we had had, it all came at a very reasonable low price. Highly recommended.

review_full: We stopped in for lunch during our trip to Madrid, Spain. Despite the wonderful cuisine that Spain offers, we wanted something that felt closer to home. We had the BBQ (Beef) Burger while my brother in-law the BBQ (Ox) Burger. Yes, they make burgers out of Ox as well. My wife had the BBQ Ribs which were excellent.  All of this food for a very reasonable price. However, the best part of the meal was the wonderful service given to us by Marcos. Marcos appears to be running the show at this well-run establishment. Great food, great prices, great service and most of great management from Marcos.  It was so good that we decided to go back the same night for dinner. Problem was the restaurant was closing at 12:00 midnight and we arrived at 11:55pm. No problem for Marcos who not only made sure we got some food, he made sure it was very fresh as well. This time we all got the Ribs but Marcos also threw in some dessert (Apple Crumble Pie).  When you’re staying in Madrid and looking for a place with great food, great prices and great service, then go to Steakburger (Preciados) and ask for Marcos.

review_full: I'm staying at a nearby hotel and wanted a cold beer and some food. I knew I was in the right place because the outdoor seating area was full of locals. This is a modest, non touristy area. Las Campanillas felt very homey.  I ordered a half serving of calamares. Pepe explained that "the women were eating" and there would be a half hour delay. I took that to mean that the cooks were having their meal break. Fine. I relaxed with a nice Mahou and the olives Pepe brought. A few minutes later he brought a tapa of chorizo on the house. Delicious. The calamares arrived as promised. They didn't have the crunchy coating that we get in the US, but there was a much fresher squid flavor. Just a little lemon juice was all they needed.  This was probably the friendliest place I've been during my ten days in Spain. Pepe was very welcoming, asked where I was from, etc. A very nice vibe all around.

review_preview: Thank you everyone for sharing!What people write is really true. First I must say that I just love tapas and places like this. Where people have their heart with it. I ended up staying night next to airport between my two flights and of...
review_full: Thank you everyone for sharing! What people write is really true. First I must say that I just love tapas and places like this. Where people have their heart with it. I ended up staying night next to airport between my two flights and of course seeked (from tripadvisor) what to eat. Found Campanillas! Yes, it's true, you miss it if you do not know it. And even you would know you still think other places "look nicer" or have better entrances or lights in window etc. No. Try it. Do favor to yourself! If you want white table cloth or hate friendly, home made tapas then you might catch some fancy italian or McD somewhere. Otherwise if you are around go there and you find lovely family run tapas bar with attentive service. Owner Pepe has stories to tell. In any language. And if you do not speak spanish (like I don't) it doesn't matter. You will learn, someone will help. Or you just smile and enjoy.  So what did I do there? I stepped in and asked to get dinner - got menu. But turned away from it and told Pepe that he probably knows better what I need. And he did. Served many different things, I think I ate 4 plates (few small, few very big - meatballs was so to say main course, ah so lovely!) and was really full. During all this we were speaking a lot of football, travelling, Pepes history and stuff. People all over have sent photos, post cards ... everything, bar is decorated with memories. He has some fans. Now one more, me. I have a reason to return to Madrid. Don't even have to go far from airport next time!

review_full: I found Real Talent Cafe on TripAdvisor, lured by the positive reviews of the proprietor, the ambiance and setting, and the paella. It took me a subway ride to get here and a meandering walk down some side streets but eventually, I made it. And I'm glad I made the trek. review_preview: I had booked a table for a large group for 9pm on a Saturday, and in the afternoon, called and asked if we could move it to 9.30pm. The manager said it was not possible as he had another table coming at 10.30pm. I was...
review_full: I had booked a table for a large group for 9pm on a Saturday, and in the afternoon, called and asked if we could move it to 9.30pm. The manager said it was not possible as he had another table coming at 10.30pm. I was surprised we would only be allotted 1.5 hours but he said this was how things were done when you booked online. As we were taking the train in from Toledo, we had to rush to the restaurant and arrived by 9.15pm. The main server seems to be the owner. He was pleasant enough but has a major chip on his shoulder. While he was serving someone at the table a cocktail, a little bit fell into my companion's wine. He said sorry and took away the glass, we assumed he would replace it, but nothing happened. When he saw us talking about this, he brought back the glass saying "oh well if you still want it, here you go." Through the night, he seemed kind of cocky and not helpful when ordering.  Funnily enough, during my trip to Spain, I had at least one waiter drop a drink on the table or on me or on someone at the table each day. Overall, servers aren't very bothered by this so I guess it's something we had to get used to. The food here is quite good, apart from the overuse of nachos in a few dishes, you will be very happy with the quality and portions of the dishes. The flavours are authentic and the sauces they serve on the side, are delicious! The cocktails sound lovely but are all very watered down so apart from the margarita's, stick to the wine (and protect it with your life).  If it weren't for the owner/server's attitude, I would have given this a four-star review. Also, we left the restaurant at 11.30pm and there was no other table waiting, hence we could have easily arrived a little later, more comfortably.

review_full: After reading the reviews of this restaurant we were looking forward to meeting Pepe and we were not disappointed. Forget the food, forget the wine, forget the surroundings, just enjoy the experience. We were fortunate in that we had a friend with us who spoke fluent Spanish so we left the ordering to him though in fact what we were served was decided by Pepe who has some English albeit limited. This is not a high-end restaurant but excels in what our friend described as typical Madrid-style home cooking. Some dishes we loved, one or two not to our taste. The wine was again chosen by Pepe who insisted we try several. Constant visits to our table to chat about rugby, soccer, food, wine, sharing jokes added to the pleasure of the evening. Something very different from the usual restaurant visit. Campanillas is a place where ordinary Spaniards go for home-cooked food, watch football on TV and share a glass of wine or two with friends. It should be approached on that basis. Hopefully you'll be pleasantly surprised. You'll certainly be satisfied with the very modest bill you'll receive at the end of the evening.

We were craving some delicious Spanish food, and we found it here. We sat outside and ordered a pitcher of sangria and the suggested seafood plate and sausage plate. The seafood plate included delicious fried calamari, fish, and anchovies. The sausage was also very flavorful. (Probably too much food for just two people though - I didn't realize the portions would be so generous!) During the meal, they brought us several samples. When we left, Pepe came over and said he had two gifts for us if we visited him behind the bar before leaving. He gave us a Madrid baseball cap and a large Madrid magnet! Very friendly service and great food make this the perfect spot for a relaxing dinner for exhausted travelers!

review_full: We were staying across the street and the hotel shuttle driver clued us in to this little pub where the locals eat. Ask for Pepe! He has a lot of personality and we just let him bring us food (all of it excellent) until we'd had enough. He did ask if there were any dietary restrictions, which for us was not an issue, but it is good to know he was thinking of the possibility. Come early (Spanish early = 9) as the place fills up with locals. We had a small pitcher of sangria (made fresh at our table) and a few combo platters of traditional pub food: calamari, croquetas, fries (with garlic aioli and 'spicy' sauce), tortilla de patata, meatballs, mussels, jamon, oh and for dessert a few lovely little homemade truffles of chocolate heaven.  Enjoy the ambiance and the chance to be Spanish for an evening- don't rush it! The food is worth every minute! If you happen to have a cap or tchotchke from your city to donate to their wall, they may even display it. Sadly our city was not yet represented, but we'll be sure to bring something next time we come!!

review_full: Visiting the Campanillas was an absolutely right choice. We only had the evening in Madrid between flights and didn't want to waste it. We found this place on Trip Advisor and realized it was 600 meters from our hotel near the airport. Too tired to go across town we gave it a shot and walked down the street. At first we weren't sure it was even open but we had just come so early - our body clocks were out of synch with local time and we were hungry by 6:15pm. Met Pepe as we entered and sat at a very nice little home-spun dining room with red checked table cloths. My were were we in for a treat. I'm not sure which we liked more, the great food or the wonderful conversation and delightful time with Pepe, his wife and daughter. He kept bringing out samples and extras that just made the experience a perfect evening. We talked about the spices he uses, the places they come from, how it's made. And basically I loved the fact that he told us what we should order. He suggested - and we agreed - to each get something and share the flavor with the other. The anchovy on potato chips was superb. My wife loved the black pudding appetizer. The salmon was great and the entrecote steak so flavorful. Dessert was amazing - flan and rice pudding and he kept showing is unique features and spices to put on it. We loved it when Pepe sat and told us the story about how he started the place 43 years ago and how he's been married 30 years - happy and thriving. It was a perfect evening. Although he may not be able to spend as much time with everyone if the place is full at 9pm, I am sure he loves to meet each person who walks through the door. The value was amazing. His hand-written menu on a piece of spiral paper torn out of a notebook was written especially for English speakers who can't navigate the Spanish. The set price of 12 Euros included everything and it was well worth the bill. The quality and taste was great. But the experience made it a truly unforgettable experience. Not a superficial, glitzy bar. But a true Spanish community place that you'll remember. It's a great place to add to your list of things in Madrid.

review_full: You won't want to go way WAY out of your ordinary travel path. But my wife & I stayed at the nearby (five minutes walk away) Hotel Täch, before a next day departure for San Francisco. We spotted this place (thanks in part to Trip Advisor), and went there for an early dinner ... 8:30-ish instead of 10-ish, since we had to be up the next morning early. And it was just great. Pepe and wife Carmen run a fine place, with excellent food (some of the best croquetas we had in Spain), and the owners were excellent company, until around 9 pm, when the neighborhood began to occupy all the tables outside. There are great stories to be told about this place; Pepe doesn't speak a lot of English, but he's trying, and the photograph above the bar is of his father, who raised mules & used them to deliver farm produce in the 1910s to the main market in Madrid (Barajas was then a suburb of slowly developing Madrid). They've been in this spot since the late 1960s: the food, the stories, the warmth and friendliness of the proprietors and the neighborhood -- all huge pluses. Give it a try; you won't regret it.

We were lucky enough to find this place as it's a bit tucked away and requires some searching, but it is an absolute gem of a restaurant.  To start, the decor is chic without being pretentious and blends the comfortable culture of Madrid with the practicality and edginess of Asian island cultures. The bar tender whips up a mean Pisco Sour that shouldn't be missed and is a great way to start what is about to be an incredible journey of the tastebuds. We went all out and ordered several dishes. We started with the Chipirones de Anzuelo, which come in a perfectly battered panko crust. We then had what was our absolute favourite dish of the evening - the Bao de Panceta (or Pan Bao). They suggest you eat it shortly after ordering as the bread is fresh from the oven and the insanely tender pork absolutely melts in your mouth. Honestly, you could go here to order this dish at least three times. The palm sugar based sauce is also part of the magic to this dish. We followed with the Carrillera de Turner and the Presa de Ibérico. Both full of incredibly unique flavours that mix the best of Thai and Spanish cuisines. For dessert we ordered the Chef's "mess", which included a beautiful assortment of fresh berries, citrus, sorbet, and ice cream. Though it does end up looking like a huge mess of tasty treats when all is said and done, when delivered to your table it's almost too beautiful to eat. Almost being the key word, of course. You simply can't miss this place on your visit to Madrid. The chef is a genius and the flavours are some of the most incredible. we've tasted to date. From top to bottom this restaurant is one of the best we've ever had the pleasure of visiting. Make sure to go out of your way to do the same!

title_review: BEST Food, BEST Value, and BEST People!   Amazing Dinner in Madrid!
review_preview: We are New Yorkers and have been on vacation for a week in Europe.  We have eaten some terrific meals, but for overall experience our evening tonight at Rosi La Loca Taberna was absolutely the best eating experience of our vacation.   The combination of terrific...
review_full: We are New Yorkers and have been on vacation for a week in Europe. We have eaten some terrific meals, but for overall experience our evening tonight at Rosi La Loca Taberna was absolutely the best eating experience of our vacation. The combination of terrific food at an incredibly reasonable price and the “over the top” warmth and friendliness of the restaurant staff, who truly could not do enough for us, made the dinner more than a meal, it felt like a family experience. From our servers Gloria and Adam, to the manager Alejandro (who spent many years living in New Jersey), to our hostess Eva (who literally went the extra mile to assist us in getting a reservation at a sister restaurant for tomorrow), to Richard (already a Trip Advisor Legend in reviews we had seen prior to booking) - everyone treated us like 10 year regulars instead of like the tourists we were. Their warmth and genuine interest in us, in addition to their excellent service, made the experience memorable.  While being well treated was wonderful, the quality of the food for the price took the experience to another level of enjoyment. We started with burrata infused with a hypodermic filled with olive oil and pesto, in a tomato based immersion. We then had tenderloin of pork with sweet potato chips and applesauce that was perfectly tender and delicious. My wife is not a pork lover, and she found herself wanting more of this delicate dish. The next appetizer was tuna tataki, which was served in a gondola “floating” in dry ice. The tuna was rare and perfectly marinated in soy sauce and Japanese spices, and topped with an aoli cream sauce and sitting on a bed of seaweed. I am a huge tuna lover and I order it in restaurants frequently. This was among the best tuna dishes I have ever eaten. Its excellence required a second order - which was consumed even more quickly than the first.  We then had the chicken and seafood paella, which was served in the Spanish style for 3 - and was plentiful. The rice was done perfectly - neither too “al dente” nor mushy. The sauce was delicious. The seafood and chicken cooked perfectly. It was a treat. All the while, Alejandro, Adam and Gloria were checking in frequently to assure our satisfaction - mostly they heard as “oohing” and “aahing”over the quality of the food. They were accessible without hovering.  Finally, after eating a tremendous amount of excellent food, and very good (and not expensive) wine, it was time for dessert - sadly, we only had room to split one. The brownie with ice cream was like lava cake and disappeared almost upon Gloria placing it on the table. As we went upstairs to pay the check by credit card, we encountered Richard, who also asked about our meal. Feeling like family by now, we told him of the pleasurable evening we were having, and he insisted on providing, on the house, one additional treat. He reached into the fridge and removed limoncello shots in test tube like containers, which we shook and downed.  Having finished an incredible evening, Alejandro told us they had a sister restaurant around the corner, named InClan, and we eagerly agreed to dine there tomorrow. Eva then worked some magic to get us a reservation, again treating us like family. We can;t wait to try InClan tomorrow - if it’s half as good as our overall experience tonight, we’ll be satisfied. I realize in reading such a rave review you might wonder if we were somehow connected to the restaurant. I assure you we are tourists from New York (I have many other reviews on line in TripAdvisor) and have never seen this place or the people who were so incredible before tonight. We thank Gloria, Alejandro, Adam, Richard and the enchanting Eva for making us so very happy not because of the great food, but because we were treated like family. We highly recommend this place - a trip to Madrid won’t be complete without a visit.

It was a kind gesture by the bartender / waiter but because we only had churros for lunch we were pretty hungry after walking around the city the whole day so we went ahead.  The fried cheese appetizer was delightful. We ordered steak and pork fillets for mains however was served pork ribs and pork fillets so was quite disappointing. However initially I wanted to ordered the ribs as well so was half ok with the mistake. The pork fillet was tender and delicious but the ribs weren't great and dry. Both servings was huge and could see why our order was queried initially.  1 appetizer + 2 mains + 2 beers came to less than 30 Euros.  *Also the menu del dia that many has mentioned previously is only available for lunch.

title_review: Vinos, Tapas y Amigos..  De Divino Tinto al Cielo!
review_preview: We discovered Divino Tinto on our last visit to Madrid and this year it was at the top of our !MUST! return to restaurants in the city.We were delighted that David remembered us as he so warmly welcomed us like friends upon arrival.It...
review_full: We discovered Divino Tinto on our last visit to Madrid and this year it was at the top of our !MUST! return to restaurants in the city. We were delighted that David remembered us as he so warmly welcomed us like friends upon arrival. It felt as if we were visiting old friends, but friends that not only make the best Tapas in Madrid but also have the most wonderful selection of small producer wines as well. All the selections on the menu are generous and designed to share, and all made to order. David expertly describes every dish and its preparation, including the local sourcing of the ingredients.. even down to which town and farm! As before, we left the wine pairing to David as he is a master at choosing the perfect wine to accompany each dish and even remembered our preferences from our last visit. After all, we were among friends and not just dining out! We started our adventure with the best Scallop Ceviche we have ever tasted, the sweetness of the scallop perfectly balanced by the tart sauce. Crisp in texture and tasting of the ocean, truly magic upon the tongue!  We followed the a very tender and fresh veal carpaccio dressed with the signature house olive oil, made by a friend from single variety grapes and produced in one farm only. So good we were tempted to have it by the glass. Next we enjoyed our absolute favorite from last year, the Baby Habitas with Grilled Chipis. Truly a dish to enjoy again and again with the habitas meltingly soft and a perfect counterpoint to the sweet and crunchy grilled calamari.  We could not finish our Tapas feast without trying the Lingote de Cochinillo, a wonderful slow cooked pulled pork creation served with the in season boletus mushrooms and a confit of figs cooked in port.. ESTUPENDO!!! Torrijas con Helado, a chupito of Pedro Ximénez and expressos revived us for our ride back to Malasana. Make sure to reserve a table if you are having dinner as there are only a few and it is always full with the local crowd.
