review_preview: We were walking thru the park and it was getting late for lunch (3pm) and none of the ‘cafeteria’ style restaurants in the park were capturing our attention so looked on Tripadvisor for something nearby and this grabbed the attention of both of us.  Although...
review_full: We were walking thru the park and it was getting late for lunch (3pm) and none of the ‘cafeteria’ style restaurants in the park were capturing our attention so looked on Tripadvisor for something nearby and this grabbed the attention of both of us. Although in the wrong direction for where we were going next, it looked worth a go. So glad we did. It was tiny but full of locals and no other tourists (always the best to my mind) and I could see why once they managed to squeeze us in despite no reservation. It remained packed and people constantly trying to get in throughout our time there.  Our waiter was a lovely, warm and engaging guy. He recommended a few things to us which looked and sounded great but sadly we were only there for a light lunch so didn’t go for them but if we came back, we would. We went with a couple of very simple things - patatas bravas and manchego cheese which were both perfect. We also tried a new dish (for us) which was mushrooms and crispy spinach cooked with raisins and Pedro Ximenez - outstanding and one of the best tapas dishes we have ever had.  Couple of small beers and a glass of wonderful Ribera Del Duero (always blows my mind that I get a glass like this for less than €3 vs what I get in London!) made this the perfect lunch! If we come back to Madrid, we will defo come back here - could not recommend it enough. So much buzz abut the place coupled with wonderful service and that food/drink!

review_preview: I was in Madrid for a long weekend, mainly because two German friends were visiting there for the first time and I was "tour guide". As it was a few years since I was last there, many of the restaurants that I liked in the...
review_full: I was in Madrid for a long weekend, mainly because two German friends were visiting there for the first time and I was "tour guide". As it was a few years since I was last there, many of the restaurants that I liked in the Cheuca area have closed, so went to Esplore as a result of good reviews on here. Went alone on a Thursday night and had: starter - the morcilla (Spanish black pudding which I love) on toast with goats' cheese - for me, a wonderful combination of flavours and textures; for main course I had the rice with prawns and asparagus - was expecting the usual of, in Spanish restaurants, white asparagus but was fresh green asparagus which was a wonderful compliment to the prawns and the tomato based sauce of the rice; and a glass of a great Albarinho wine. Only "criticism" is that the portions were too big for me, but I have come to expect that in most spanish restaurants. Food is modern Spanish, so "with a twist" on traditional foodstuffs and dishes I booked a table for me and my friends for the Saturday night and they too loved the food and great service. We had the rice dish between us and they too enjoyed it as much as I had done.

review_full: We enjoyed a delightful evening at Divino Tinto! The wine list is superb and very reasonably priced. The tapas and platillos were outstanding, all beautifully presented and the preparation faultless, truly worthy of the finest restaurant entrees.. and all in this small and extremely local wine bar near the Legazpi metro just a short ride from Madrid's centro. This is a very small and intimate venue and we were warmly greeted by David upon arrival who made us feel welcome and 'como en su casa' as he escorted us to our table. Make sure to book ahead as there only a few tables for dining and this wine bar is truly a local hangout and very busy at night, but not noisy. David tends bar, takes orders and serves the tapas all with amazing cheer and charm. We enjoyed our tapas with vermouth's to start and four wines, plus a dessert wine as suggested by David. All from small Spanish bodegas, all luscious and satisfying! We would have sampled more but we had an early train from Atocha the next morning. The tapas, the wines, the service, oh my! this was truly one of the best meals we have ever enjoyed in Madrid and we can't wait to return. Thank you so much David for such a delightful evening!!!

The atmosphere was buzzing, mainly with couples and groups of ladies. It is very small and this helps the atmosphere. Each plate was better than the rest. There were three desserts and we had one each. All were sublime. Booking is essential as many people were turned away while we were eating. This is one place not to be missed.

review_full: When we found this place, there was only one table available. Good sign right? Totally true! The food was A-MA-ZING! Starter olives were nice and fresh as well as the house wine. review_preview: We ate here as we stayed at the H10 hotel around the corner. The reviews prompted us to seek the venue and its flavours. It was busy and I would suggest making a reservation. We got a table on a Sunday after a 5 minute...

Try the crocodile croquette - it’s far superior to the regular. The duck on noodles for main and their signature dish was also delightful. Thank you for a great good bye meal. What an experience. title_review: Probably the best (larger) tapas dishes ever!
review_preview: Needed a place close to Retiro Park for a meal, so located this on TripAdvisor - and so glad we did. We had to wait for a table, but judged this to be worth doing looking at the food passing. Do yourself a favour -...
review_full: Needed a place close to Retiro Park for a meal, so located this on TripAdvisor - and so glad we did. We had to wait for a table, but judged this to be worth doing looking at the food passing. Do yourself a favour - order the tartare tomate - a stack of tomatoes, soft cheese and crispy ham - one of the best dishes I’ve ever had. The croquettes and huevos rotos (fried egg, ham and potatoes) were also first class - we couldn’t fault it. This is obviously a place in the know with locals, for a really good reason. Try it - you won’t be sorry. Staff were really friendly and helpful in squeezing us in without a reservation and in describing the food.

review_preview: My wife and I visited this establishment during a recent trip to Madrid. The food at Esplore is very good, and the staff very friendly and attentive. We started off with a couple of tapas (potato frittata) at the bar. We then ordered the pumpkin...
review_full: My wife and I visited this establishment during a recent trip to Madrid. The food at Esplore is very good, and the staff very friendly and attentive. We started off with a couple of tapas (potato frittata) at the bar. We then ordered the pumpkin soup, eggplant chips with honey, and the migas. Food, plus 3 drinks each (wine, beer, cider) came to 45 euros. The following day we returned for lunch. I had the pork burger. My wife had the pork surprise (pork and caramelized onions on toast). Again, it was excellent. The total tab with drinks was about 25 euros. WRT the pic of the migas, I had already chopped the fried egg into pieces before thanking the pic.

review_preview: I reserved a table at the last moment, following the positive reviews about this restaurant. Everything was great. The place is nice and make you feel comfortable. The staff is friendly and efficient. The food is great. We had a "degustacione" a taste of everything....
review_full: I reserved a table at the last moment, following the positive reviews about this restaurant. Everything was great. The place is nice and make you feel comfortable. The staff is friendly and efficient. The food is great. We had a "degustacione" a taste of everything. Not really a simple taste but every course was pretty big. Simple genuine and flavoured food! Try it!

review_preview: The 26 euro tasting menu was very interesting and tasty.   It was good value and the service was great.   The wine was good and reasonably priced.     The menu is generally pork based.    All in all a lovely dining experience.
review_full: The 26 euro tasting menu was very interesting and tasty.   It was good value and the service was great.   The wine was good and reasonably priced.     The menu is generally pork based.    All in all a lovely dining experience.

review_preview: I was suspicious right from the start, for some reason. Intuitive? The croquettes I think were from the freezer and popped into the deep fryer. The paella was so over cooked that the mussels and clams were dried out. Not just tough but dry. The...
review_full: I was suspicious right from the start, for some reason. Intuitive? The croquettes I think were from the freezer and popped into the deep fryer. The paella was so over cooked that the mussels and clams were dried out. Not just tough but dry. The mussel shells crumbled trying to open them. Another sign of overcooked. The rice in the paella did not have one filament of saffron. When I gave the feedback, the server came back with some jumbled excuses around that is how it comes in. Was it just reheated? The compensation for the bad paella was a dessert. The dessert was brownie bits purchased from some factory - terrible. Given all of the choices of great food in Madrid this rates at the very bottom. Oh, and I was surprised there were so many English speaking tourists eating here. Perhaps a social media phenom. Do not waste your money eating here.

review_preview: My wife and I ate here in September, having enjoyed dining here 2 years ago when in Madrid.  Even though the restaurant has new owners and been remodeled, the food was as good as before.  We had the Black Ink Risotto and Iberian Prey [pork...
review_full: My wife and I ate here in September, having enjoyed dining here 2 years ago when in Madrid. Even though the restaurant has new owners and been remodeled, the food was as good as before. We had the Black Ink Risotto and Iberian Prey [pork shoulder] mains and both were excellent. The staff was also just as friendly as before. Highly recommend. Hint: Reservations are usually necessary.

review_preview: This restaurant came as a recommendation. Walking into the restaurant we had high hopes because the decor and lighting made for a good first impression. I can’t say I felt the same way upon leaving this restaurant. Overall, the server was friendly and attentive, but...
review_full: This restaurant came as a recommendation. Walking into the restaurant we had high hopes because the decor and lighting made for a good first impression. I can’t say I felt the same way upon leaving this restaurant. Overall, the server was friendly and attentive, but the food was quite underwhelming. We decided to try the Paella to get a sense of a staple Spain dish, but this dish completely missed the mark. The Paella was not very flavorful and was too crunchy to actually savor (i.e., burnt). Maybe if we had purchased a more expensive dish the the quality would have been better, but for a dish as simple and staple as Paella, I expected a lot more. While I’ve seen a lot of positive reviews of this restaurant, nothing really stood out to us enough to recommend to someone. However, if you do decide to eat here, go with something besides the Paella.

review_full: had a wonderful two course breakfast for only €19. started off with the mimosa, which was made with fresh orange juice, and a beautifully creamy cappuccino. then they brought us fresh, soft, buttery breads which came with great jam and some other condiments, and a delicious yogurt with fresh fruit. for our main courses i chose the eggs benedict with avocado, which came with a salad with a nice balsamic vinaigrette. it was a LOT of food so definitely worth the price!! couldnt finish my main, but i wish i could because it was so delicious. the waitress was nice and very helpful and the restaurant is decorated really cute! definitely will be returning.

title_review: Small and welcoming with excellent food
review_preview: We visited this restaurant on the strength of the previous reviews, having eaten at similarly sized Mama Gus (small and unpretentious) the previous evening, which we had really enjoyed. Taberna Gastromaquia turned out to be another excellent choice. One of the staff, possibly the owner,...
review_full: We visited this restaurant on the strength of the previous reviews, having eaten at similarly sized Mama Gus (small and unpretentious) the previous evening, which we had really enjoyed. Taberna Gastromaquia turned out to be another excellent choice. One of the staff, possibly the owner, spoke excellent English and explained the menu (there is no English menu) and gave us recommendations. All the food was very good, particularly the goats cheese and the octopus, which was a real revelation. We got there early on a Thursday night but it soon filled with people, many of whom seemed to be regulars. Don't be put off by the size and appearance of the restaurant from the outside. I would rather eat well and receive good good service than apy over the top for fancy furnishings. The only negative I could see was the charge made for bread, as mentioned in the previous reviews. Though this did not spoil a very enjoyable meal.

title_review: Refined dining in casual, intimate setting
review_preview: We were pleased with this small restaurant because of its original dishes, down to earth and attentive service and solid cost to quality ratio. review_full: We were pleased with this small restaurant because of its original dishes, down to earth and attentive service and solid cost to quality ratio.  Goat's cheese with honey and basil vinagrette was excellent. Codillo stuffed with tetilla cheese was another highlight.  One downer: they charge you for the bread. It was about the only thing that felt non-gourmet but they charged as if it were. We visited for lunch on a Saturday and were one of three parties present. Very small place, clean and comfortable.

review_preview: I selected this restaurant as it was close to my hotel and I read the good reviews on Tripadvisor. I found it average, with some good dishes (entre of Guacamole with banana chips or Baked goat cheese) and some others really disappointing (Octopus in a...
review_full: I selected this restaurant as it was close to my hotel and I read the good reviews on Tripadvisor. I found it average, with some good dishes (entre of Guacamole with banana chips or Baked goat cheese) and some others really disappointing (Octopus in a creamy sauce and, I think was called Enchiladas). Desserts are good. If you're looking for more traditional Spanish cuisine don't go there, it's ok if you're just for a snack. friendly staff, but rather poor service. For what we have eaten (30 EUR each) it was also rather expensive.

review_preview: This is one of the gems you're looking for in Madrid. Look beyond the entrance and grab one the tables beyond the bar. The service is warm & friendly and gives you the feeling that they want you to have a good experience. The food...
review_full: This is one of the gems you're looking for in Madrid. Look beyond the entrance and grab one the tables beyond the bar. PS: The place is fairly small so it may be wise to phone ahead.  C/Pelayo 8, Chueca

All of the food was flavorful, the meat was juicy, and the simple clean ambiance made for a delicious experience.

review_preview: I had a great meal in this restaurant. I started with the tuna loin accompanied by a salad that perfectly combined the sweetness of mango with a bit of heat, if anything the portion was a bit too big for one person but it was...
review_full: I had a great meal in this restaurant. I then had the pan fried fish of the day with saffron risotto, this day it was a piece of brilliantly cooked salmon, still moist in the centre, with crispy skin. I didn't have any drinks with my meal so I was expecting the bill to be reasonable, but I was still shocked by how small the bill was. The restaurant is fairly simple, the service is pleasant and efficient, all round a really nice place.

The clientele was mainly composed by couples and international tourists, the service is efficient and friendly.  Definitely a place I would recommend visiting.

review_preview: The small restaurant is divided into smaller areas.  A pleasing mixture of surfaces ( wood, brick, plain wall) and different types of lighting created a soothing, modern but not industrial feel.  I came basically for the squid ink risotto, which was creamy and delicious,  The...
review_full: The small restaurant is divided into smaller areas. A pleasing mixture of surfaces ( wood, brick, plain wall) and different types of lighting created a soothing, modern but not industrial feel. I came basically for the squid ink risotto, which was creamy and delicious, The addition of broiled squid rings , tomatoes and a bit of a Spanish pico de gallo was genial; it lightened the risotto. Alas, the other choice, octopus in a potato foam was the opposite-- too thick and heavy for an already substantial mollusk Sometimes traditional styles (a la Gallega), grilled with garlic) work better. My servers were pleasant and professional. There is a lot of imagination in this menu--I would definitely go back for more hits...

review_full: This is a lovely place to eat in. The ambience is shabby chique which is delightful and unusual. It is not “typical Spanish” but looses nothing as such for it is very much itself! Book a table preferably in the back room to add to a memorable experience. Those not so close to their late teenage and early twenties might be uplifted by the other patrons!

review_full: My wife and I visited this restaurant whilst in Madrid and were blown away. Some of the food was up there with the best we’ve ever had. When the bill came, we thought we’d been undercharged. We hadn’t, it was just great value. If you are staying in Madrid, take a short walk out of the city centre, avoid the tourist trap restaurants and visit Gastromaquia

review_preview: Honestly, looking at the other reviews I feel bad for giving a 3/5. It could be a one-off experience, but not everyone can be satisfied. To put it briefly, the food was nice but the dishes we had were not particularly special. The best dish...
review_full: Honestly, looking at the other reviews I feel bad for giving a 3/5. It could be a one-off experience, but not everyone can be satisfied. To put it briefly, the food was nice but the dishes we had were not particularly special. The best dish was a starter, the goat cheese with pesto. The other dishes were ok, but not great. For example, the bbq ribs portion was massive, slattered in bbq sauce, and accompanied by plain fried potato balls with mayo. The dish would have benefitted from some variation. Another dish, the duck, suffered from the fact that the puree was tastier than the duck, which was slightly underdone in some parts. Finally, we ended up giving a tip (10%), but instead of being thanked the response was "ok". I'm sure this is just a one-off experience, but it did not fit the other reviews we had read. Overall the food was descent and the service was good, but the other reviews make it feel like we missed out.

review_full: My wife and I visited Gastromaquia for lunch and tried the Bluefin Tuna, Grilled Goat Cheese, and Fried Eggs. The tuna was fresh and tender and topped with sweet mango, tomatoes, pomegranates, onions, airy rice noodles, and sriracha mayo. The goat cheese was creamy and topped with honey and a basil pesto sauce. The salty and yolky fried eggs sat on a bed of savory potatoes and were topped with diced bacon and scallions. Overall, Gastromaquia is a solid spot for lunch.

review_preview: We visited Gastromaquia for a light supper recently. We had the octopus with potato foam, "crunchy aubergines", and slow cooked ribs. Each dish was very well executed. We love octopus and this was the best we had on our stay in Madrid - perfectly seasoned...
review_full: We visited Gastromaquia for a light supper recently. We had the octopus with potato foam, "crunchy aubergines", and slow cooked ribs. Each dish was very well executed. We love octopus and this was the best we had on our stay in Madrid - perfectly seasoned and the potato foam was a nice upgrade on the traditional potato base. The ribs were meltingly tender and flavoursome, and the aubergines were delicious too. We had 2 glasses of Protos Roble (about €5 a glass, very cheap), and the lovely waiter left the bottle with us. Service throughout was very friendly, quick but not overly so. I would definitely return to Gastromaquia.

review_full: We went here during our stay in Madrid. A pleasant surprise was that the lady spoke good English so a noob in Spanish could actually say something meaningful. We had a shared tuna tataki, which was a really beautiful dish, and also inventive and tasty. This dish could have been served in an even fancier restaurant. Highly recommend you to try it. For our main dish we went with a safe option, the entrecot. The meat was great in medium, quite red but also very tasty. Also recommended. Everything went so smooth we ended up going here twice on the same trip. On our second visit we tried other dishes, they were good but not excellent. Hence the four stars for food, if we had only gone the once it would be 5* on food.

review_preview: Gastromaquia is aptly named. With early 8:30 reservations, for awhile we were the only customers in the restaurant. By 10:00 it was completely full, so make reservations as the Spanish eat late.All the tapas we ate were excellent. Highlights included Octopus with Potato Foam...
review_full: Gastromaquia is aptly named. With early 8:30 reservations, for awhile we were the only customers in the restaurant. By 10:00 it was completely full, so make reservations as the Spanish eat late. All the tapas we ate were excellent. Highlights included Octopus with Potato Foam and the Tikki Masala Mussels in an Indian-flavored broth. Our favorite was the caramelized Grilled Goat Cheese with honey vinaigrette and basil pesto. Dinner entrees were excellent. Find out what the fish of the day is being served. The food execution was nicely paced, wine constantly flowed, and our server was the best. A great Spanish foodie finale for our trip! Gastromaquia is my #1 choice when I return to Madrid. Chueca barrio has come a long way!

review_full: I have to join in with most people who have reviewed Gastromaquia and write that this is an excellent place to eat in Madrid. We ate there, I believe, Easter Saturday night 2012. We found the place through Tripadvisor The restaurant is small, so I would reserve. Plates on the shortish menu are to share. What was most striking about the food were the unusual preperations of wonderful things that we all have been eating for years but here they are done differently AND deliciously. We had tiny boiled potatoes that were bathed in wonderful red sauce from the Canary Islands. Then the most delcious curried mussels. The mussels wonderfully fresh, the curry gravey divine. We also had grilled asparagus with a light cheese topping of some sort that was perfect and great desserts. Along with a bottle of wine, the bill for two was about 63 euros. My companion couldn't believe the bill and said "Wow! Our best meal, but the cheapest price!" The restaurant was crowded and there was a small bar in the front. Everyone was talking, laughing and enjoying themselves greatly. Serrvers were knowledgeable and friendly. Make sure you try this place.

review_preview: Here is the thing. Madrid is a wonderful, exciting, incredible city but the food can get very repetitive. Fast. How many times can you eat oily mediocre ham and heavy croquetas with lukewarm tortilla? I love Madrid, and have lived here but I understand that...
review_full: Here is the thing. Madrid is a wonderful, exciting, incredible city but the food can get very repetitive. Fast. How many times can you eat oily mediocre ham and heavy croquetas with lukewarm tortilla? I love Madrid, and have lived here but I understand that sometimes that craving for something different, something a little fresher is too hard to ignore. So. La Taberna is very good. But to me, it was my personal standard of good. Yes, the ingredients were fresh, a little different and a little lighter than what I had been eating all week. The Guacamole was....guac. What can I say? It was as good as any. And the pork skewar was very tender and nice, but the same as you could get for a dollar from a vendor in a street cart in New York. The rabbit was wonderfully tender but very salty and overpowered the braising liquid. I know I sound pretentious, its just that I really enjoy great food which shouldn´t be that hard to find and this was just that. Good simple food, just not knock your socks off gourmet extravaganza.

(dopey mistake to take a cab when it was a 10 minute walk plus the guy gave us the 10 Euro tour getting there, but I suppose we deserved it.) Food involves modern takes on Spanish classics. Wine was splendid and the only slight disappointment was a big dish of octopus in cheese sauce which was almost inedibly rich. Hugo (who's the chef and a terrific host as you can tell by the reviews)conferred with us about everything, and was a delight. He was sad that we didn't care that much for the octopus but everything else was lovely. Dessert was a sorbet which was some of the best I have ever had, and my friend had a frappe of some sort that we both fought over to scrape the last bite. Just a totally fun evening in a place that's doing well because of Trip Advisor, but not taking any of it for granted. Excellent (perfect) English spoken here too by the way.

Usually this gives me a nervous feeling that perhaps it's empty for a reason. Nope, it was only empty because of the time of day. The paella we ordered we devoured. It was mostly gone before either one of us thought to take a photo. Our waitress was very kind, checked in on us regularly, and let us know when the food was getting close as they prepare it only upon order and not in advance, as good paella must be done. This was great comfort food, in a cool and quiet setting, with excellent service and not unreasonably expensive. Check, check, check, and check! What more can you ask for? We left full and wishing we had found this restaurant on our first day instead of our last.

title_review: Dining at Esplore: The Good, The Bad, & The Bizarre
review_preview: Let’s start with the good. I made the dinner reservation in a hurry and didn’t realize that it was for a degustation menu. However, I can say that I was happy that I inadvertently did. For this menu, you get two starters (zucchini salad and...
review_full: Let’s start with the good. I made the dinner reservation in a hurry and didn’t realize that it was for a degustation menu. However, I can say that I was happy that I inadvertently did. For this menu, you get two starters (zucchini salad and smoked salmon), two main dishes (ravioli and Iberian pork), two desserts (dark chocolate cake and torrija), paired with a wine or liqueur for each course. I have to say that the food was well prepared and portioned, and the wines of good quality. Definitely a good dining experience and well worth the EUR25 price. I will be recommending this place to my Madrileno friends to try out. Now, the bad. Compared to other smallish degustation menus that I have tried before, this menu is a set, and I mean a SET so there are no other options to choose from. If you have any dietary constraints (e.g., pork, nuts, alcohol), this menu may not be for you. And finally, the bizarre. Just before the dessert, I inquired about the ravioli, and was told it was the third dish I was served. I had to rack my brain to remember what the third dish was, and what I remembered was slices of meat on a bed of vegetable puree. However, the manager insisted that I was served ravioli so I asked to see what their ravioli looked like (just in case ravioli means something else in Spain). From what I was shown, I can categorically say that the third dish was not ravioli. I don’t eat a lot of pasta, but I would like to think I know a ravioli when I see one. Bizarre indeed!

review_full: You wouldn't know it from the outside, but this place offers up some excellent food. Our server was welcoming, and spoke excellent English. He even humored us as we tried to order some in Spanish. The food is served in stages, which the three of us shared. We started with guacamole and banana chips, followed by goat's cheese with basil and honey. We then moved on to seafood, with mussels in a tikka masala sauce and octopus. We ended with pork on skewers. Each dish was better than the last, and I think you'd be hard-pressed to find a bad thing on this menu. The meals weren't, strictly speaking, traditional Spanish dishes, but rather unique takes on classics. We ended with three different, delicious desserts: cheesecake, blackberries and white chocolate cream, and strawberries with vanilla sorbet and coca cola extract. They were all great. Some other thoughts: the food is delicious, but the portions aren't huge (especially if you're coming from the States). The desserts were fantastic, but a bit pricy (6 euros a piece). In hind sight, they were actually quite large, and we probably could have shared two.  Overall, our meal came to 68 euros, with all the above mentioned dishes, lots of bread (you'll want to use it to enjoy all your extra sauce), and a beer. Considering the quality of the food and service, we all felt this place was an excellent value.

We now schedule our visits to make sure we have time to enjoy a meal at Vinos both when arriving in Spain and as our last memory when we are leaving. If I lived in Madrid, this is the place that I would want to meet friends to drink a bottle of wine, to have a quick bite in the bar, or to have a wonderful meal. The staff are so friendly and cool that you want to become friends with them as well! Every dish is to die for, but I especially crave the bellota pork dish. Vinos, as the name suggests, also has a very nice, modestly priced wine list. Just writing this makes me want to plan another trip to Madrid!

review_preview: This is a tiny bar on the east side of Retiro Park.  Tapas and entrees served. THE best croquettas we had in Spain, crunchy on the outside, creamy on the inside, one type filled with a mushroom cream, the other with manchego. Also had a...
review_full: This is a tiny bar on the east side of Retiro Park. Tapas and entrees served. THE best croquettas we had in Spain, crunchy on the outside, creamy on the inside, one type filled with a mushroom cream, the other with manchego. Also had a fried mussel tapa. These were bizarre but I liked them very much. Mussel shell filled with a mussel cream, then breaded and deep fried. We also had the black pudding that was wrapped in a crispy pastry shell, looked like the size of a pirouette cookie. Also had a rice dish with duck confit. It was really good, much better than Valencia paella. They had another rice dish with mushrooms and beans, but didn't see that one until after we ordered. The only dish that I would rate "good" but not great, was a tuna and roasted red peppers. The waiter thought I had ordered it, but we didn't == just a miscommunication in languages. He was so nice and we didn't want to offend him, so accepted it. I was expecting raw tuna, but it was cooked, which I am really not a fan of, however, the flavors paired really well. All dishes were plated creatively. I think reservations are essential. Very casual place, with a big screen TV that had soccer game playing which made the place more fun. Just two guys running the place, a bartender and the waiter. The bar tender was mixing what looked like killer drinks. Wine by the bottle and glass (nice pours and only 2.10E each!). Definitely a local hangout.

review_full: I stopped in for tapas tonight with my sister and my two young daughters. We had been vainly looking for another restaurant recommended by a friend but we gave up and opted for this as we liked the look of it.  So incredibly pleased we did! This place is a find.  We started off with complimentary black pudding parcels and egg salad crisps - they were delicious and an indication of the amazing food standard that was to come. We had beef and cheese croquettes, a beautifully dressed and plentiful salad, goats cheese, wrinkled potatoes. All the dishes were thoughtfully presented and excellently executed.  The desserts didn't disappoint either. We shared home made chocolate and caramel ice cream and a stand-out strawberry cheesecake. It's rare for cheesecake to leave a lasting impression, but this did! Every element of it was 100% on point. From the base to the creamyness/cheesiness factor and the fruit topping....even the sweetness. It really was impressive! The service. Again. Amazing. The waiter - I think he was the owner, helped us order and then we he could see we had perhaps over ordered cancelled our final dish without charge. He checked, unobtrusively, throughout our meal that everything was satisfactory and was just totally charming. I actually cannot wait to recommend this place to my friends. I can't wait to return. This is my go-to Madrid restaurant for every future visit.

review_full: We were staying in a hotel near this restaurant to it flagged up when we searched tripadvisor for the nearest ones. It's in a small side street so glad we looked it up as we wouldn't have just stumbled upon it! We arrived just after 8.30, we hadn't reserved but they had a table for 2. If you intend to arrive later than this probably best to book as the restaurant filled up quickly, mostly with bookings. Waiters were really friendly, I am a Spanish speaker but my friend isn't so when they realised I was translating for her they were more than happy to explain everything in excellent English. They advised us to share a couple of the smaller dishes to start and then have a main, either from the meat section or the rice section. We shared the goats cheese in honey and basil and the octopus with foamed potatoes. Both were absolutely fantastic and good sized portions. Definitely could have eaten them twice over! We then shared Fideua as a main which is like paella but instead of rice uses small noodles. This was also fantastic, a more than ample portion for two people and although we were both quite full we couldn't bring ourselves to leave any! We didn't have dessert, too full up, but we saw some people having the famed mojito sorbet and they said how good it was. We also had a couple of glasses of nice wine with our meal. Had we been staying longer in Madrid I'm certain we would have returned here to try some of the other things on the menu and I'd definitely return next time I'm in Madrid. Food was fantastic, Spanish but with a modern twist and very reasonably priced for the quality.

Our server was so courteous and found us a place to sit even though the restaurant usually takes reservations. He then proceeded to ask us what language menu we would prefer. The menu offered a lot of vegetarian options which was great as some of us did not eat meat. While we waited for our drinks, he brought out a couple of hors d'oeuvres for us to share. The food did not take long between courses and always came out hot. After dessert, the server gave us a mini piña colada to wash everything down. Overall it was such a great experience and I would definitely go back.

review_full: I was very surprised this place did not have a larger menu. I ordered croquettes with beef and cheese and they were delicious! I was very pleased with presentation and taste. I also ordered the sautéed porcini mushrooms with crispy spinach which was really good as well. I was satisfied with the food and the service but I wish the place was a little bigger and the menu offered more. There were a lot of drinks to choose from but not many entree dishes or desserts. I had the caramel ice cream for dessert and fell in love, only bad part was it was a single scoop so if you do order this ask for an extra scoop! I had a great time here but it was definitely a place for an older group and I'm a college student so it didn't really wow me. I would come back just with a friend not a group. The place was very clean and decorated nice I would recommend this for maybe those that just want to have a beer and tapas.

review_preview: After reading reviews on Trip Advisor, we decided to try this restaurant for our last evening in Madrid. We wanted to try authentic Spanish food, where locals may choose to eat. This is a small restaurant but when we arrived at 7.30 there were only...
review_full: After reading reviews on Trip Advisor, we decided to try this restaurant for our last evening in Madrid. We wanted to try authentic Spanish food, where locals may choose to eat. This is a small restaurant but when we arrived at 7.30 there were only two other tables occupied, the decor is simple but lovely. The waiters are attentive and try very hard to communicate in English, which was good as we know no Spanish. On arrival we were treated to an amuse bouche which was delightful and at the end of the meal we were given a dish of sweets - lovely! Where they thought we were over ordering they suggested we hold back which proved sensible, they advised on the menu successfully and we enjoyed all of our food. The small portion of patas bravas was enough for two as a started and completely delicious. My son had the salad filled with nuts and a lovely dressing, For main I had the hake, my partner had the monkfish with noodles and my son the croquettes. He also managed cheesecake which he assured us was fabulous. We rounded the meal off with Irish coffee which was perfect. The bill was reasonable barely €50 for the food for three, all left very full. Definitely worth the 30 minute walk through the park.

review_full: This restaurant is a gem. The best tapas of my life. Truely unique combinations of flavours and using only the very best ingredients. The chef has worked at the famous El Bulli together with Rene Redzepi, the chef of Noma in Denmark, voted as the world's best restaurant. Well Gastromaquia has the same philosophy of using top local produce and combining them in ways you have never tried before. They do more than tapas. The dark chocolate desert was also fantastic - explosion of flavours. Service was also excellent and the chef took a lot of time to guide us in ordering and chatting with us. Among the best dinning experiences in my life - and I have been to Noma. This place is just much more affordable. When in Madrid, go there. Amazing experience.

review_preview: My wife & I. ate at Gastromaquia this evening....we have booked a return engagement in 3 days. If you are in Madrid, this place must be at the head of your list. It is small, so be sure to book in advance.  The menu in...
review_full: My wife & I. ate at Gastromaquia this evening....we have booked a return engagement in 3 days. If you are in Madrid, this place must be at the head of your list. It is small, so be sure to book in advance. The menu in Spanish will be...not translated, but explained and illuminated by Hugo, the co-owner. Then you will be treated to an array of choices...almost all with a slight creative twist, but all extraordinary and delicious. Every serving but 1 or 2 is large enough for sharing, which Hugo encourages. We shared a salad of goat cheese & greens with a marvelous dressing, my wife had Hugo's version of spare ribs....the meat literally coming off the bone after very slow cooking. I have never tasted spare ribs even remotely as succulent (11.50E).  This is one of the best restaurants I have ever eaten at and surely the best in Madrid so far.

review_preview: Walked right by the restaurant, it is easy to miss. We were glad we decided to eat there and had resevations as we watched people turned away. The food is the star here: absolutely divine. The owner/chef/waiter really made us feel comfortable and his time...
review_full: Walked right by the restaurant, it is easy to miss. We were glad we decided to eat there and had resevations as we watched people turned away. The food is the star here: absolutely divine. The owner/chef/waiter really made us feel comfortable and his time working at Jaleo in Washington, DC made his English fantastic. The staff bent over backwards to ensure we enjoyed our experience. The food was innovative and delicious. We had the goat cheese salad which was one of the bestmI ever had. The mussels tikka masala were wonderful and the Iberian pork melted in our mouths. The only thing that kept it from being 5 stars was the neighborhood and the Formica table atmosphere. For foodies, a great find- any great restaurant would be proud to serve it! Enjoy, enjoy.

review_full: We throughly enjoyed our tapas at Taberna Gastromaquia! Hugo (owner/chef) speaks perfect English & is very helpful in explaining his creations. We all were surprised to see guacamole on the menu and man, is it delicious. Had plenty of guac in our day and this was heavenly. Baby new potatoes with red pepper sauce were great, mussels outstanding! Since Hugo is passionate about the ingredients he uses, so we asked him for his recommendation for olive oil to purchase & bring back to the states. Not only did write down the brand/type/region, he also told us where we could get it! The store was closed by the time we finished our dinner but we were able to go the following day. Hugo & his food are king here, don't expect fancy but do know you will have a great dining experience!

The reviews were good so thought we would try turning up without a reservation and luckily there was a table free. The inside has cute and quirky decor, the staff were friendly and the food was amazing! We opted for the ‘full brunch’ which included either an orange juice, mimosa or cava, a tea or coffee, yoghurt with fruit and granola, selection of breads and croissants with jam etc then followed by a chose of various cooked elements - we opted for the brunch salad which had poached eggs, spinach, avocado and bacon. We were so full after all of that which cost €17 which we felt was a great price for such an amount of food including drinks. There was a smaller option which cost quite a bit less and then a menu which you can choose your own items from. So pleased we found this place thanks to tripadvisor! Shame we found it on our last day in Madrid else we would have definitely visited again.

review_preview: Gastromaquia is in the gay neighborhood of Madrid. This restaurant is small, but service and food is excellent. We got the fried goat cheese with honey and basil oil, octopus with foamed potatoes, and the black rice paella. The goat cheese is served with bread...
review_full: Gastromaquia is in the gay neighborhood of Madrid. This restaurant is small, but service and food is excellent. We got the fried goat cheese with honey and basil oil, octopus with foamed potatoes, and the black rice paella. The goat cheese is served with bread and is so savory. My husband is not a fan of goat cheese, but he LOVED this dish. The honey and the basil oil made the sour taste that is associate with goat cheese disappear. Get this dish when you come here. The foamed potato and octopus was also very good. The octopus was so soft and not hard and rubbery. The dish kind of reminded me of the steamed eggs you get at Japanese restaurants. You can definitely taste the potato in the foam. It was very unique and delicious at the same time. The black rice paella was huge. We were so full after the paella. It takes 25 minute to make but it is worth the wait. It comes out super hot and there is shrimp, mussels, and clams in it. I recommend getting the paella and maybe 2 other dishes or just stick to all there other dishes so you can try more things and not get full from paella. We were STUFFED after our meal and could not finish the paella. The servers here are very attentive and can give you some recommendations if you are a visitor in Madrid. We called the day of to get a reservation for this restaurant because it is small and fills up really fast. There were diners who walked into the restaurant, but could not get a seat because the restaurant was full. The restaurant has great food, great service at an incredible price.

Our impression was that Vinos de Bellota was run by a few youngish graduates who are destined to make a go of things. Based on the number of, mostly Spanish, people eating and drinking there they are succeeding. We made a reservation for the following night and found Vinos de Bellota even busier with people prepared to wait up to an hour for a table. The food was just as good but the service, although still very pleasant, was much less efficient.  We would strongly recommend Vinos de Bellota and would certainly choose to eat there again. One thing to watch though is that, for some reason, they put payments made by card through in your national currency not Euros. They really should ask first.

review_full: Writing this review just after eating at Taberna. The food was very, very well done and the host/waiter/co-owner Hugo was an excellent guide through the menu. He is a chef as well, speaks great English, and explained his menu nicely. It is a creative menu of relatively simple foods but executed well. Goat cheese salad is a must -- my wife is still talking about the dressing. The guacamole is fresh, full of flavor and had me mopping up the last bits with my bread because the plantain chips were gone. My octopus ("pupo") in a "potato foam" was absolutely outstanding. I'm thinking of going back again tomorrow. Asparagus done with parmasean and a light balsamic was simple, flavorful and delightful. The skewers of pork were perfectly spiced, succulent. The restaurant is a small, very casual place that might benefit from a touch more decorating. If you were to walk by and not know what was within you might not stop. But this would be your mistake. The food is great, the prices right, and the host very charming. His passion for the food is very obvious and it shows on the plates. By the way, Hugo worked at Jaleo in Washington, D.C. under Jose Andres which explains a lot about his passion and his execution.

The only thing I would disagree with on many of the posted ratings is the lack of atmosphere, I agree the decore is quite plain but decore doesn't create atmosphere alone, this place was full of local people having a great time and it was buzzing. No point going on about the actual menu content as that's all been said and the reviews have been spot on, all I would recommend is that you go and see for yourself and dont forget to book as you might be dissapointed!

title_review: Holy crap this place is good
review_preview: So my girlfriend and I were looking for a last minute place for a dinner reservation and stumbled onto Gastromaquia via Trip Advisor.  Simply put food phenomenal . . . service was great, and the ambiance was relaxed and local.We shared everything we had...
review_full: So my girlfriend and I were looking for a last minute place for a dinner reservation and stumbled onto Gastromaquia via Trip Advisor. Simply put food phenomenal . . . service was great, and the ambiance was relaxed and local. We shared everything we had and probably ordered more than we should as everything sounded so good. We had the potatoes to start with the red pepper sauce which were simple and delicious. Then the goat cheese salad came out which was the best goat cheese I've ever had, warmed to perfection with a slightly crispy bottom layer with an amazing balsamic reduction that was the perfect blend of sweet with the vinegar. Then the Mussels with a tikka masala sauce that was a combination I never would have thought of and was again amazing. The asparagus with the same balsamic reduction and slightly melted finely shredded parmesan cheese was the best by far. Every bite just disintegrated in our mouth's and blew us away. At this point we were both pleasantly stuffed and thought we could handle no more. We had caught notice of one dessert at the table next to us that was intriguing. It was some sort of green gelato with rum poured on top. Our waiter then came up with perfect timing and explained that it was a mojito sorbet. It was just that only better than any mojitio I have ever had. We shared it as it we ate soo much it would have been impossible for us both to have our own. Our waiter recognized us as american and was very curious to hear where we were from and what we were doing in madrid. he made conversation and handled the small but busy resturant well and the food was timely but not rushed. definitely a visit that we will make again.

title_review: Incredible Food, in a no frills environment!

review_full: I would not have found this place without tripadvisor so I am especially drawn to write a review. I have now been to Gastromaquia twice and I can happily say that if I had more time in Madrid I know I would be back. The first time I went with my girlfriend and sisters and I can safely say we ordered nearly half of the menu. The types of dishes they make and the interesting twists they place on Spanish classics displays a true love for food and desire to provide a unique and interesting dinning experience. Add on top of that the helpful staff and fact that one of the two chefs is in charge of the dinning room, so he is always talking about the food and doing so with great English, and you have an incredible dinning experience that is accessible to anyone. Obviously most of the time you would expect to pay excessively for this type of food, but I can happily say that this meal left both our stomachs and wallets 100% satisfied!

title_review: Great food, better service and even better staff!
review_preview: My wife and I came in late the night we before we were going to head out back to the US. The place was pretty much empty and they said they were out of food. Initially he, the host (also server) said that if we...
review_full: My wife and I came in late the night we before we were going to head out back to the US. The place was pretty much empty and they said they were out of food. Initially he, the host (also server) said that if we came back tomorrow, they would be able to do a better job of serving us. We didn't ask but I think he was also the chef. He was very chatty and I think that made the meal that much better. He had spent some time in NYC and spoke pretty English quite well. When told that this was our last night in Madrid, he said his food options were limited, as they had run out of most of their food. We said we would take whatever.  The starters were delicious, potatoes in an amazing local sauce and guacamole, and the local beer and wine were great as well. They were recommended by the host with significant discussion regarding sourcing the wine (which was pretty cheap BTW).  The rabbit was very good and the pork skewers were absolutely delicious. The chocolate dessert was awesome. I think the food was very good, we would have given it 4 stars based on just the food. Then again I would never have ordered guacamole in Spain when I live in California. Thats not to say it wasn't very good and given the slim pickings, the late night accomodation, I wish I could give them 6 stars. Overall for 1 beer, 1 wine and a bottle of water, 2 good sized appetizers and 2 main dishes as well as desert, the total was just under 50 euros. The priceless service and accomodation we will be thankful forever as my pregnant wife was starving.

The chef's remarks were that he wanted to make good food available to everyone for an affordable price, and he has definitely achieved it.

We liked the tapas to share like "asadillo de piementa"/pepper salad with tuna, "croquets exoticas"(3 different tastes), "crujiente queso"(crispy baked goat cheese). Nice home made ice cream to finish (chocolate, nougat, tangerine). Large choice of tasty Spanish wine by the glass. Vermuth and beer also available. Rather overcrowded and loud restaurant where you grab some "vinos&tapas", not a place for a quiet, romantic dinner. Good price/quality ratio. Recommend the "Vinos de Bellota" to try delicious and creative tapas and enjoy Spanish wine "copas de vino".

It was followed up with toasted rice with porcini and duck confit. It just blew me away. The flavors in this dish were so perfectly blended together I could have just kept going back for seconds and thirds, etc... I was too full for dessert but the other two had the tiramisu and loved it.  They also gave us wonderful complimentary aperitifs of soup and a whipped coffee confection for dessert.  Service was excellent and prices very reasonable.

But once the food is served, you know you are in the right place. We had a variety of starters, all excellently cooked. The foie gras with a gin sauce was the best I have ever tasted. The wine list is short, as is the menu, but the quality is perfect. The restaurant also boasts a long gin list and a very good homemade Gin Fizz shot. Our waiter was extremely friendly and helpful. When the bill came, we were surprised about the low price. An absolutely excellent restaurant and do recommend to reserve a table. Even on Sunday, guests still came past 22:00.

review_preview: If you get the chance to come here - then seize the moment. You must book as it is tiny. There is a relaxed but caring atmosphere - with everything done with an eye for detail. Although I had booked we had to wait for...
review_full: If you get the chance to come here - then seize the moment. You must book as it is tiny. There is a relaxed but caring atmosphere - with everything done with an eye for detail. Although I had booked we had to wait for a few minutes for our table as the occupants were paying there bill. We had a gin & tonic made with fresh herbs & served with canapés ( melon mousse on a cracker and mini chorizo sausage rolls - amazing) before sitting down for a late lunch. We ordered a selection of items which came on after the other - a highlight was black pudding cigarillos trickled with mayonnaise, also a broad bean, crispy spinach and egg dish with a balsamic dressing. All the flavours were clear and pronounced. The service was impeccable. I finished with beautiful caramel ice cream - with coffee came dishes of sweeties. We had a bill which was astonishing low for the quality (and quantity) of our meal - about 60 euros for 2. As you can tell - we loved it. Good Albarino too.

review_full: two years ago, we found this place and it was fabulous. Sometimes going back to a place you are left disappointed; but not here. Back in Madrid two years later and this place is still fabulous. A tiny place, good to make reservations. They don't speak English, but are very patient with our attempt to speak Spanish....Muchas Gracias Jorge! Being a group of seven we tried nearly every tapa (I think we ordered 15). All were fabulous, particularly the croquettas, still the best I've ever had. Other standouts included a mushroom and bean saute surrounded by crispy spinach, small potatoes that were halved, and topped with a sauce. They were different than potatoes bravas. The goat cheese was excellent, as was the pate with the gin and tonic jelly. Wine list was wonderful, but if you go, get a Gin and Tonic (Larios 12 anos) -- sensational. So good that with tastes from my glass, 4 others at the table ordered them! 7E each seemed to be comparable price in the USA, however, upon arrival they were 3x the size of a gin and tonic in the USA.  This is a very local hangout...on the other side of Retiro than Sol. Bottom line, this place is 100% recommended. Go!

The salty cod was the best of the starters. The main courses (hake, artichokes with surimi noodles, papas, croquettes, duck vermicelli) were as expected: tasty but nothing out-of -this-world. The surprise came with the bill: for this quality, you would usually be paying a lot more, even by Madrid standards. Maybe that was one of the reasons so many locals were dining too.

review_full: **This will be posted on Yelp, TripAdvisor, and Google because those are the places I look before picking a place** Incredible service! I mean, the kind of service that made us look at each other and say "this would never happen in the states". Our waiter was quick, kind, and knowledgeable about the dishes we wanted to try (mainly the paella). He spoke English, but engaged in our attempts to speak Spanish when we could. The paella is made from scratch, so it does take 25 minutes to arrive. In that time, he recommended we get a little something to munch on, but we told him we couldn't really afford to (we're students with very little money). Of course, when a plate of guacamole and plantains comes to our table, we became concerned and flagged him over to tell him we didn't order it. Do you want to know how he responded? "We've all been young once." The only problem is, I am now burdened with the task to pay it forward! What a genuinely kind gesture to two students looking for some good food. The food was more than that: it was delicious! We opted for Arroz Negro because neither of us had tried squid ink before. This would definitely be the place to try it out. The guacamole is different than what we have in the states, but it was a great appetizer before our HUGE dish of Arroz Negro arrived. We ate until we were full, and there was still more left. You are definitely getting at least your money's worth here. While paying, another waiter was really friendly, and talked to us about family he has in the states. He told us to hold on before leaving, and came back with two shots of Bailey's to send us on our way. This is the kind of restaurant that leaves both your stomach and your smile full. We will be back to enjoy it some more. Thank you for the great service!!

review_full: I came here in search of the best paella in Madrid after doing some research on TripAdvior where it was ranked number 1. While I did enjoy the “surf and turf” paella that we had, it is my opinion that it could have been better. I found that (a) the chicken was cut into some small, unfamiliar pieces, (b) the seafood (shrimp, mussels and calamari) was somewhat over cooked and (c) it lacked the “socrito” (the crispy base that forms in the bottom of the pan) that good paella is known for. The rice and seasoning were very good. I suspect that the proteins were prepared separately and then added to each order resulting in them being over cooked and that the chicken pieces were cut small to facilitate quick cooking. I did notice the pan itself was well seasoned enough to allow for a socrito to form had there been less liquid in the pan and it had been allowed to cook just a bit longer. The earlier comment about the proteins being cooked separately and then assembled per order could have also contributed to the overall dish satisfaction. We did try some super outstanding eggplant chips that were drizzled with what was described on the menu as honey but was more resemblant of molasses. They were thin, flash fried morsels of deliciousness and worth a trip here for only those. We enjoyed a bottle of excellent rose wine that went well with both dishes. Our servers, Laura and Sheryl, were friendly and engaging. I also found prices to be very reasonable. Fun, hip and enjoyable food off a small street near the bustling Plaza del Sol.

review_preview: GASTROMAQUIA SERVES EXCELLENT Spanish food done in unusual and original ways. There are lots of small dishes to chose from  (tapas or racoon style) but don't expect to find only the traditional items that carry the tapas label. We ordered the octopus with potato foam,...
review_full: GASTROMAQUIA SERVES EXCELLENT Spanish food done in unusual and original ways. There are lots of small dishes to chose from (tapas or racoon style) but don't expect to find only the traditional items that carry the tapas label. We ordered the octopus with potato foam, the seared goat cheese with honey and basil oil,the oreja (pigs ear- delicious) and the coquinas (little clams in a tomato-based sauce) and the thing shaved artichokes with balsamic vinegar and the tuna tartare. If you want traditional tapas you'll find some dishes like patatas bravas and some arroces, as well as paella but my advice is to be a bit adventurous. This is a small, modest looking restaurant in the gay-friendly Chueca district.Book ahead or you may be lucky if you turn up immediately after the place opens.

review_preview: I was a typical tourist in Madrid trying to find a decent restaurant for dinner,  among many to randomly choose from and hope for the best. My spanish is poor so wherever I went there would be an element of risk/adventure. I stumbled upon Gastromaquia...
review_full: I was a typical tourist in Madrid trying to find a decent restaurant for dinner, among many to randomly choose from and hope for the best. My spanish is poor so wherever I went there would be an element of risk/adventure. I stumbled upon Gastromaquia by chance while walking along Calle Pelayo. I am delighted I did. Every aspect of the experience was beyond my expectations..  My waiter Pablo spoke perfect english and was welcoming, knowledgeable and gracious. I am not a meat eater so that narrowed my options considerably. Pablo was able to recommend a coupled dishes which I tried (the guacamole with banana plantain chips, porcini croquettes and sautéed asparagus with parmesan cheese and balsamic vinaigrette. The dishes were all cooked to perfection. I ate slowly since I did not want the meal/the flavors to end. What a delightful experience. Please visit it and let your taste buds experience a treat.

review_full: We went to this place according to Tripadvisor ratings as usual - which normally result in a good choice. However this restaurant we think is definitely over-rated from 2.5 -3 star to 4.5 star. The place is pretty small with out of date decoration. Very limited choices of food and drink - only one beer option. Several dishes appeared on the menu are only served in winter time. Food is very slow - we waited for over 1 hour for the main dish after they served our food one by one - and slowly. The first two dishes are salty and the beer glass is so small. Then we waited for ages for pur main dish which is a seafood fried noodle which we expect to be less salty. However, this dish was extremely salty - even saltier than the most salty Kebab I have ever had in an Austria kebab shop. We can't even finish 1/4 of the dish because of its poor tasting and pure salty taste. Things happens but the waiter charged the salty dish for 2 persons in checkout which apparently it didn't write as "min 2 persons" like some other dishes. We pointed this out and the waiter became less patient and showed bad mood - even they let us waited so long with very little customers at that time. and the salty food - little poor beer. Then we pointed out how salty the food is - I definitely have high tolerance on salty food than my wife but even me never had this salty fried noodle before.  Anyway, this restaurant is not good at least for now in 2016 - you can try them and see how many stars they deserve - definitely not the 4.5 stars rating.

review_preview: Rosi La Loca - What a fun dinner we had at this restaurant with an unexpected menu!  This little place is difficult to find.  It’s on a tiny side street amongst many other small restaurants.  First of all, the decor makes you bust out laughing....
review_full: Rosi La Loca - What a fun dinner we had at this restaurant with an unexpected menu! This little place is difficult to find. It’s on a tiny side street amongst many other small restaurants. First of all, the decor makes you bust out laughing. There are huge bunches of colorful paper flowers all over the walls, which gives it a tropical (maybe Hawaiian) theme - but not. Maybe “The Little Shop of Horrors” theme - but not. The menu seems straight up, but when the dishes come out, our mouths drop in surprise and laughter.  When the Burrata salad comes out, there’s a huge white eyeball thing on the plate. It’s the size of a softball. Then, the waitress, and all of them have a strong sense of humor - must be a prerequisite to be hired at this restaurant - pulls out a huge hypodermic needle and injects the white ball with liquid green pesto. Hmmm, that’s kinda different. The shredded pork is between two soft Chinese bao buns in a V shape. They’re Chinese shredded pork tacos - that’s what they are but we are in Madrid! They are nicely seasoned and very tasty.  They didn’t have the baby squid that was listed on the menu so they substitute it for beef. The grilled octopus is good but could have a bit more flavor. There is mild chaos at Rosi La Loca but it’s all just fun.

title_review: A true joy, should become even better in time (if they'll listen)
review_preview: We were there twice. The first time for tapas, the second time for paella. We saw them on TA with good reviews, very near to our hotel so we decided to have dinner there. the place is run by young passionate guys, very involved on...
review_full: We were there twice. The first time for tapas, the second time for paella. We saw them on TA with good reviews, very near to our hotel so we decided to have dinner there. the place is run by young passionate guys, very involved on what they're doing. the head waiter/manager has excellent English and is most helpfull. We went by his recommendations without fail. There's something a bit confusing in this place. the food is wonderfull, and so are the people. But the design of the place and the menu is lacking. The menu seems to belong to a work place mensa, the bright bluish white lighting... doesn't contribute either. at least 3 times when we were there the lights went off - probably when one too many ovens were switched on in the kitchen. Don't get me wrong - I highly reccomend this restaurant, but also I highly reccomend the owners to take care of the styling, menu design, lighting deign and... call an electrician!

title_review: Impeccable food, friendly owner and Chueca nightlife just outside
review_preview: This place is all about excellent food. Just like the previous reviewers have already said, it's a small, simple place and the main focus is on the food itself. Last summer I visited here 3 to 4 times and had different courses each time -...
review_full: This place is all about excellent food. Just like the previous reviewers have already said, it's a small, simple place and the main focus is on the food itself. Last summer I visited here 3 to 4 times and had different courses each time - everything was very tasty and I was rather disappointed that I wasn't able to taste everything during my summer break in Madrid! The best part is that the owner - who is such a nice and sincere guy - was kind enough to provide tips on how to cook the courses myself! It's in the middle of bustling Chueca and the atmosphere is best described as "lively and loud" - just like in all the best places in Madrid. The restaurant itself is a reason good enough to pay a visit to Chueca. My favorites? Octopus (pulpo) with red wine!

review_preview: Really glad we checked TripAdvisor to find this little gem.  Its small with 10 tables, with a humble decor that you would never imagine from the outside to have the amazing the service and food would be.  The menu is in Spainish but the host...
review_full: Really glad we checked TripAdvisor to find this little gem. Its small with 10 tables, with a humble decor that you would never imagine from the outside to have the amazing the service and food would be. The menu is in Spainish but the host came out and explained the menu to us, which was great. He was really hospitable and the place was full of locals rather than tourists - didn't hear any english around us. He recommend a lovely bottle of Ribera del Duero wine for us to enjoy our meal with. We had ensalladilla (a cold cream potato salad) as lovely to start with on the warm evening. Then came a tikka mussel meal and then asparagus with balsamic and parmesan shavings. All delicious and left us full. However we still managed to squeeze in the mint mojito sorbet served in a cocktail glass which he filled up with rum - Amazing. Definitely get this no matter how full you are!

review_preview: Not sure where to start, which dish to elaborate on or praise. Not sure which one is my favorite. Three food lovers, very hungry .... tried half of the dishes of the small (but superb) menu. The potatoes with the hot salsa, I could just...
review_full: Not sure where to start, which dish to elaborate on or praise. Not sure which one is my favorite. Three food lovers, very hungry .... tried half of the dishes of the small (but superb) menu. The potatoes with the hot salsa, I could just eat that by spoon, yes it is spicy. The guacomole served with banana crisps...........there was something about it that I can't put my finger on, just yummm. Curried octopus was not just excellent in taste but also in texture. There was more that we ate, but I cannot not say how good the pan fried goat cheese was, have it as a salad or just as entree it's awesome. Now that I have recollected my gastronomical memories lets talk about meager details. Place is small but cozy and full of trendy crowd (even at 4 pm in the evening, reservation recommended), service is excellent and prices, for the quality of food they serve it is very affordable. Our bill was about 120 Euros, including a bottle of wine, few more drinks and 6/7 dishes altogether, not a bad birthday meal, I would say.

review_preview: I almost walked by the restaurant after I saw how small it was but thought that I would trust my TripAdvisor advisors.  And you haven't let me down yet.I ordered the curried mussels and I was very pleased.  For other Indians out there, this...
review_full: I almost walked by the restaurant after I saw how small it was but thought that I would trust my TripAdvisor advisors. And you haven't let me down yet. I ordered the curried mussels and I was very pleased. For other Indians out there, this is not a tikka masala sauce but the flavoring is great nevertheless. After the mussels were done ( and there were plenty for just one person), I was sopping up the sauce with the bread they provided. They recommended the mojito sorbet. And while it was delicious, it was too big and sweet for me. Half the portion would've been plenty especially since I've been cutting back on sweets. All in all, my recommendation is to try the place and I know you'll enjoy it.

review_preview: We were only in Madrid for three nights but ate here on two occasions. Hugo, the manager and owner, made some excellent recommendations. He not only takes the bookings and orders but also serves the food so service was a little slow but very friendly....
review_full: We were only in Madrid for three nights but ate here on two occasions. Hugo, the manager and owner, made some excellent recommendations. He not only takes the bookings and orders but also serves the food so service was a little slow but very friendly. The honey goats cheese is one of the best dishes I have ever had. Not to mention the celery mojitos! The restaurant is TINY so a booking is essential as its very popular. Located in a very lively area of Madrid surrounded by many pubs and clubs, its an ideal dinner venue.

review_preview: During a three week trip through Spain, this was one of our favorite and still most-recalled restaurants!  Gastomaquia is not a large restaurant so reservations are recommended.  We did not call in advance, but the friendly co-owner, Hugo, was happy to let us sit at...
review_full: During a three week trip through Spain, this was one of our favorite and still most-recalled restaurants! Gastomaquia is not a large restaurant so reservations are recommended. We did not call in advance, but the friendly co-owner, Hugo, was happy to let us sit at the bar and order our dinner and took the time to chat with us. The restaurant was filled with in-the-know-tourists. The menu is limited, but everything is fresh. Here, you will find classic tapas but prepared with a contemporary twist. For example, the classic pulpo a la gallega (octopus with potatoes) is presented as slices of tender octopus, sprinkled with paprika, on fragrant potato foam. The flavors are the same as the classic preparation, but the opposing textures in Gastomaquia’s version leaves you wishing this was the version they were serving across Spain! The restaurant is away from the touristy main roads and in a gay neighborhood filled (at night) with prostitutes, but is definitely worth seeking out for an unforgettable and friendly dining experience in the capital!

review_preview: I'm still waiting for the tapas meal that makes me a convert and this didn't (quite) do it. The standout was a goats cheese brûlée, served with salad greens and balsamic. Very good. The grilled meat dishes were all good. The guacamole with banana chips...
review_full: I'm still waiting for the tapas meal that makes me a convert and this didn't (quite) do it. The standout was a goats cheese brûlée, served with salad greens and balsamic. Very good. The grilled meat dishes were all good. The guacamole with banana chips was ok but lacked any real flavour punch. The grilled octopus sadly came drenched in potato gloop (sold as potato foam). Most disappointing was a bowl of boiled new potatoes served with a dipping sauce. It just wasn't an elevated dish. The house red was good. Staff were friendly and helpful. Desserts were so-so.

review_full: I based my nights out in El Retiro district based on TripAdvisor reviews I had researched before travelling to Madrid. Travelling alone, I usually sit at a bar and chat to the staff and tonight was no different. I found the staff here, on my two visits, to be extremely friendly and engaging with time to answer my questions about their food, cocktails and wines.  The tapas served with every drink were exquisite, especially the savoury broth, which was most welcome, given the ambient temperature outside ( -1C ). In no time I felt at home, conversing with staff and locals alike.  I highly recommend this bar/restaurant as a destination on your tapas tour of Madrid.

review_preview: Great place for dinner.This is an unassuming street corner bar/restaurant that we had prebooked with a 9pm reservation. We turned up at 9.10pm and immediately thought Trip Advisor had let us down with a few people at the bar and no tables occupied. On...
review_full: Great place for dinner. This is an unassuming street corner bar/restaurant that we had prebooked with a 9pm reservation. On the brink of walking out we decided to give it a go and we were shown to our table by a very friendly waiter. By 9.30pm the place was packed with locals and the atmosphere was great. The food was good and the service exceptional. This is probably one of the best value restaurants I have ever eaten in and would highly recommend it, the food it not top notch but it is still a great place to eat.

title_review: Cosy local place with great food and drinks at reasonable prices
review_preview: I booked a big family Sunday lunch here last month based on the reviews although I was nervous because we have different tastes and it can be hard to please everyone.  I also thought its location would let us have a nice walk through the...
review_full: I booked a big family Sunday lunch here last month based on the reviews although I was nervous because we have different tastes and it can be hard to please everyone. I also thought its location would let us have a nice walk through the Retiro Park to and from the restaurant either side of a good lunch, and follow it up with free entry to the Reina Sofia (from 1330 on a Sunday) or the Prado (1700-1900) . To my relief, everybody loved it although we skipped the museums afterwards because it was great weather and we all wanted to walk lunch off a bit. We liked the look of the starters more than the mains and so ordered large starter portions to put in the middle to share which the waiter was happy to help us sort out. The food was delicious and arrived at intervals so we each tucked into the same dish. It worked really well because the oven baked rice, one of their specialities, takes a while to prepare and arrived last. All of the food was of a very good standard, with the steak, "tigre" mussels and cheesecake really standing out. The drinks as well were fantastic as the bar specializes in cocktails so some of us had a few to finish our meal off along with a shared desert.  It's a small, modest but very local place so we were the only tourists, which my sister liked. Service was good and we always had something to eat or drink, which my other sister liked. The wine and cocktails kept my parents happy while my wife liked the general ambience. We were all very happy with the food and I was very impressed with the value for money. A very definite trip advisor hit!

title_review: Delightful spot with good food well priced
review_preview: We found this restauant on tripadvisor and went there our second night in Madrid. Because of the traffic patterns, we had to take a cab clear around Retiro Park, but Madrid cabs are not expensive.We arrived about 8:15, and of course most patrons were...
review_full: We found this restauant on tripadvisor and went there our second night in Madrid. Because of the traffic patterns, we had to take a cab clear around Retiro Park, but Madrid cabs are not expensive. We arrived about 8:15, and of course most patrons were still outside sipping wine. We ate inside and found it had a very pleasant, relaxed atmosphere. The waiter was friendly and helpful, and there was an Englsh menu, although all the other patrons seemed to be locals.  I ordered a pork loin, and was asked how I wanted it cooked. Somewhat surprised, I said medium well done. Then I remembered that in Europe the way they feed hogs does not carry any danger of trichinosis, so I did not need to have it well done. When it arrived, it was slightly pink, and very moist and tender, better that the somewhat dry pork we eat here. It was quite a treat. Edith also was very pleased with her vegetable dish and house wine, while I had bottled water that was slightly more costly than the wine - a not uncommon event in European restaurants. The total tab, with tip, was less than 50 Euros, and that made this not only a fine meal, but a bargain also. This restaurant is highly recomended. Not a Michelin Star establishment but absolutely fine for a very good, reasonable meal in a pleasant, local venue,

She said he seemed wowed that we ordered a large nachos as a starter but took the order anyway. The plate of nachos that came out wouldve been more suitable for 4 to 6 people to start them off. They were absolutely delicious but by the time our mains came out we were quite full and unable to finish our mains which I found disappointing as they were also tasty. I just felt the waiter should have drawn her attention more to the fact that the large nachos was really that big and not really suitable as a starter for 2. I think we would have enjoyed our mains so much more. I would still recommend this place and will return on my next visit to Madrid.
